title: The 'Long stop' demo opens an 'Off the route' card when admin's long-stop time is about 14 minutes or more
description: playDemo(longStop) feeds the real monitor samples at one point, for up to (longStopMinutes+1)*60 s. On every sample the monitor also evaluates _tooLong, using the straight-line expectation of the demo plan: about 4.7 km at 8.3 m/s, roughly 566 s, with a limit of 566*1.5 ≈ 849 s. If admin's longStopMinutes is 14 or more, _tooLong fires the offRoute trigger (longer than expected) before the long stop exceeds its threshold. The loop stops at the first hit and opens the off-route card, while the demo page title says 'Long stop'.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:346-354  for (var s = 0; s <= seconds && hit == null; s += 5) { hit = monitor.addSample(...) }
ride_check_monitor.dart:376-380  _crash(...) ?? _longStop(sample) ?? _offRoute(sample) ?? _tooLong(sample)
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway test: with the mock's longStopMinutes set to 15, playDemo(longStop) returned shown with session.trigger == offRoute. The demo page described as 'Long stop' shows 'taking N% longer than expected'.
suggested_fix: Build the demo with a monitor whose offRoute trigger is off (settings.copyWith(offRouteEnabled: false)), or feed only the long-stop path.

title: The monitor marks a trigger as fired even when the card could not open (another card up), so that trigger is lost for the rest of the trip
description: RideCheckMonitor._fire adds the trigger to `_fired` before the controller tries to open it. RideCheckController.open returns `busy` when any session is up (line 379), and the result is ignored (`unawaited(open(...))` at lines 274/290, and the tripEnded result). Because `_canFire` checks `_fired`, the trigger can never fire again on this trip. The droppedFar check at finish is lost if an unanswered mid-trip card is still up, and an off-route hit is lost while a long-stop card is open.
failure_scenario: A long-stop card is open and the rider has not answered. The driver then finishes 5 km from the drop-off. tripEnded fires droppedFar, open() returns busy, and droppedFar is now marked fired. After the rider answers the long-stop card, no 'finished far from drop-off' check ever appears for this trip.
suggested_fix: Mark the trigger fired only when open() returns shown, or queue the detection and open it after the current card closes.

title: After a reload or app restart, a trigger the rider already answered can open the card again for the same trip
description: The 'once per trip' guard is the in-memory `_shown` set plus the monitor's `_fired`, and both start empty after a reload. R-web restores live rides. resume() seeds `_shown` only from an unanswered event; resolved Ride check events saved for the ride are not consulted. A freshly attached monitor can therefore hit the same trigger again, for example the car still standing at the same place, and open() shows a second card for a trigger already answered on this trip.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:383-385  final key = '$id|${trigger.name}'; if (!again && _shown.contains(key)) return RideCheckOpenResult.alreadyShown; _shown.add(key);
ride_check_controller.dart:437-441  (only the unanswered event is added to _shown)
failure_scenario: The rider answers 'I'm OK' to a long-stop card and the web app is then reloaded mid-trip. The car is still stopped at the same spot, and 2 minutes later the same long-stop card opens again and blocks the screen.
suggested_fix: On attachTrip or resume, seed `_shown` from the ride's saved Ride check events, resolved ones included (cachedRideCheckEvents).

title: Failures to change the PIN, the PIN requirement, trip-share settings or the Ride check switch are never shown to the rider
description: setPinRequired, rotatePin, setTripShare and setRideCheck catch the error and set `error` to a translated message (safetyPinChangeFailed and the others). No widget reads SafetyController.error except the contact editor. PinVerificationPage, TripSharePage, RideCheckPage and SafetyHub never render it. After 'Change PIN?' > Change fails, the dialog closes and nothing says the PIN was not changed. Failed toggles flip back silently.
evidence:
safety_controller.dart:202-211
  Future<void> rotatePin() async { error = null; try { await _session.rotatePin(); ... } catch (_) { error = L10n.current.safetyPinChangeFailed; } notifyListeners(); }
pin_verification_page.dart:74  if (ok == true) await _ctl.rotatePin();   // result never surfaced
(grep: `controller.error` is read only in emergency_contacts_page.dart:288)
failure_scenario: Offline, the rider taps Change PIN and confirms. The request fails, the old PIN stays on screen and no message appears, so the rider may believe the PIN was rotated. Toggling 'Require PIN' or 'Ride check alerts' offline snaps back with no explanation.
suggested_fix: Show `_ctl.error` (a toast or inline text) on the PIN, Trip share and Ride check pages after these calls, or have the calls return a result that the pages report.

title: Trip share contact list shows the raw English relationship ('Family', 'Partner') in every language
description: Relationships are stored in English and translated with relationshipLabel(), which the Emergency contacts page uses (emergency_contacts_page.dart:190 and :342). The Trip share checkbox subtitle shows `shareable[i].relationship` directly, so Swedish and French riders see the English words.
evidence:
trip_share_page.dart:160-161
                              subtitle: Text(
                                shareable[i].relationship,
failure_scenario: With the app in Swedish, Safety > Share trip lists 'Anna / Family' while the contacts page shows the translated label.
suggested_fix: Use relationshipLabel(shareable[i].relationship).

title: Editing a contact whose stored relationship is not one of the five fixed values trips the Dropdown assertion
description: _ContactEditor seeds `_relationship` from `existing.relationship` and passes it as DropdownButtonFormField.initialValue. The items are only kEmergencyContactRelationships. EmergencyContact.fromJson keeps any server string, and relationshipLabel's own doc says 'Anything else is shown as it was typed'. updateContact also sends whatever relationship it is given. A contact whose relationship is, for example, 'Sibling' or 'family' makes the dropdown assert. Debug builds show a red error screen; release builds show an empty relationship field.
failure_scenario: Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: with a mock contact whose relationship is 'Sibling', tapping it on Emergency contacts raised _AssertionError: 'package:flutter/src/material/dropdown.dart': Failed assertion: line 1852 ... 'items == null || ...'.
suggested_fix: Normalise the value (fall back to 'Other' when it is not in the list), or add the stored value as an extra item.

title: Each Safety Kit recording leaves a permanent orphan 'still recording' entry in the persisted safety cache
description: initAudio applies an optimistic AudioRecording with a client id ('aud_<local>'). The server assigns its own id ('aud_<requestId>' in the mock), and the confirm step only removes entries whose id matches the confirmed one: `_cache.recordings.where((r) => r.id != value.id)`. The optimistic entry (createdAt set, endedAt null) is never removed. completeAudio and deleteAudio work on the server id, so the orphan stays in movera_safety_cache_v1 forever, one per recording. A related gap: when stop() hits NO_AUDIO (null path or zero-length file), the init entry is never completed or removed, and the zero-byte file is not deleted.
failure_scenario: Record and stop audio in the Safety Kit N times. The cache holds 2N recording rows, N of them stale 'recording' rows with no end, and the persisted SharedPreferences blob grows with every use.
suggested_fix: In the apply callback, also drop the optimistic id (`r.id != value.id && r.id != rec.id`), as createContact already does (FLOW-20). On NO_AUDIO, remove the init entry and delete the empty file.

title: If the recorder's stop throws a platform error, the recording stays marked 'active' and the Ride check card raises an unhandled error
description: SafetyAudioService.stop() clears `_active` only after `_recorder.stop()` returns. NativeSafetyRecorder.stop can throw a PlatformException from the record plugin, or a FileSystemException from exists() or length(). In that case `_active` stays set, so isRecording stays true, the card keeps showing the running clock, and every later Start fails with ALREADY_RECORDING. RideCheckController.toggleRecording catches only SafetyAudioException on the stop branch, so the error escapes the InkWell callback as an unhandled async error and no note is shown. The Safety Kit has a generic catch; the card does not.
failure_scenario: On Android the recorder's stop throws, for example because the microphone was taken by another app. Tapping 'tap to stop' on the card throws an uncaught error, the card still shows 'Recording 1:23', and the rider cannot stop or restart recording from the card.
suggested_fix: Wrap `_recorder.stop()` in try/finally so `_active` is cleared (and cancel() is attempted), map other errors to SafetyAudioException, and add a generic catch on the stop branch of toggleRecording.

title: Rider cancels are sent without the reasonCode that the contract's CancelCommand requires, and a 400 leaves the cancel stuck in the outbox for good
description: openapi.yaml `CancelCommand` has `required: [expectedVersion, reasonCode]`, and CONTRACT.md §1 says validation errors are `400 invalid_request`. With cancel-first, Finding calls `_match.cancelSearch()` with no reason (finding_drivers.dart:580). `_requestServerCancel` then posts `entry.body(reasonId)`, which is `{...CancelReasonCodes.riderCancelBody(null), 'expectedVersion': v}`. `riderCancelBody(null)` returns `{}`, so the body has no `reasonCode`. BookingCoordinator's stand-down and duplicate cancels (booking_coordinator.dart:778 and 808) send only `{expectedVersion}` too. The in-process mock hides this because it only checks `reasonCode` when one is sent (in_process_mock_client.dart:684 `reasonCode != null && ...`). A server that follows openapi answers 400. `isPermanentCancelFailure` (pending_cancel_store.dart:161) treats only 404/409/410/422 as final, so a 400 falls through to `SearchCancelResult.queued`. The ride stays live and the outbox replays the same rejected body on every reconnect. The why-sheet reason is sent later as a second `/cancel` on an already `cancelled_by_rider` trip. The contract table has no row for that (terminal → `409 invalid_transition`), so on a contract server the reason is also lost. The mock's R-O3 branch (in_process_mock_client.dart:690) answers 200 there instead.
evidence:
cancel_reasons.dart:39-42 `static Map<String, Object> riderCancelBody(String? reason) => { if (isRiderCode(reason)) 'reasonCode': reason!, if (reason != null) 'reason': reason, };`
finding_drivers.dart:580 `final result = await (request ??= _match.cancelSearch());`
pending_cancel_store.dart:77-80 `Map<String, dynamic> body([String? fallbackReason]) => { ...CancelReasonCodes.riderCancelBody(reasonId ?? fallbackReason), 'expectedVersion': ?expectedVersion, };`
openapi.yaml CancelCommand: `required: - expectedVersion - reasonCode`
pending_cancel_store.dart:161 `return status == 404 || status == 409 || status == 410 || status == 422;`
in_process_mock_client.dart:684 `} else if (reasonCode != null && !_reasonAllowed(...`
failure_scenario: Against a backend built from openapi.yaml, the rider taps Cancel request on Finding. The server returns 400 invalid_request (reasonCode missing). The app shows the ride as cancelling but it is never cancelled: the search goes on, a driver can still be matched and charged, and every reconnect resends the same 400 body.
suggested_fix: Always send a contract rider code: use the chosen reason, or a default such as `something_else` for cancel-first. Send the later why-sheet reason as feedback, not as a second cancel. Make the mock require `reasonCode` the way openapi does, and treat 400 as a permanent refusal in `isPermanentCancelFailure`.

title: A driver drop is reported as an admin reassign when any later event (for example a new offer) lands before the next poll
description: When a matched trip comes back as searching or offered, `_poll` calls `_reassignedByAdmin(ride, explicitKind)` (line 198) to decide between a driver drop and an admin reassign. With no `cancellation.actor` in the projection (the mock never sets one for the non-terminal driver cancel → searching, see `_apply` line 1426, which only fills it for terminals), the check falls back to `explicitKind != null && explicitKind != RealtimeKind.driverCancelled`. `explicitKind` is the kind of the latest committed event (`envelope['kind'] ?? ride['eventKind']`), not the kind of the event that ended the match. Dispatch normally re-offers the trip right after a driver drops it (`send_offer`, kind `trip_projection`). If that happens inside the 2 s poll window, the poll sees status `offered` with kind `trip_projection` and labels the driver drop as an admin reassign. The event then carries `reassignedBy: admin` and kind `trip_projection` instead of `driver_cancelled`, so the rider is never told their driver cancelled. Reproduced with a throwaway test against InProcessMockClient: after driver_to_pickup, `POST /status {command: cancel, actor: driver}` then `{command: send_offer, actor: system}`, then resync. Output: `status=RideStatus.cancelledByDriver kind=trip_projection adminReassign=true server=offered cancellation=null`.
evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:143-145 `final explicitKind = RealtimeKindWire.parse(envelope['kind'] ?? ride['eventKind']);`
:198 `final byAdmin = reassigned && _reassignedByAdmin(ride, explicitKind);`
:299 `return explicitKind != null && explicitKind != RealtimeKind.driverCancelled;`
in_process_mock_client.dart:1029 `'kind': ride['eventKind'],` (last event only)
failure_scenario: The driver cancels before pickup and dispatch sends the trip to the next driver within about 2 s. The rider's poll sees `offered` with kind trip_projection. Waiting treats it as an admin reassign (Q13 path): no 'your driver cancelled' notice, only a silent return to searching.
suggested_fix: Decide driver drop or admin reassign from the event or command that left the matched state, or from `cancellation.actor`. Do not use the newest event's kind. When the polled projection cannot tell, default to the driver-cancelled notice, or read `GET /trips/{id}/events?after=` for the skipped events.

title: Mock and readers use `{trip}` / `{trips}` envelopes for the rider trip read models; openapi defines a bare TripProjection (204 when none) and a Page with `items`
description: openapi `GET /rider/trips/active` returns a bare `TripProjection`, or `204` when there is no active trip. `GET /rider/trips` returns `TripProjectionPage` (`{items, nextCursor}`). The in-process mock returns `{code, trip}` and `{code, trips, nextCursor}`, and the release readers are built to that shape. `ApiActiveTripRepository.fetchActive` reads `json['trip'] ?? json['ride']` (active_trip_repositories.dart:29). `ApiRideHistoryRepository` reads `json['trips']` (ride_history_repositories.dart:38). Against a contract server the active-trip answer is the projection itself, so `trip` is null and the app concludes there is no live trip. The history page keeps its rows under `items`, so History is always empty. Only `nextCursor` matches.
evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:1165 `payload = {'code': 'OK', 'trip': live, 'requestId': requestId};`
:1172-1176 `'trips': finished, 'nextCursor': null,`
active_trip_repositories.dart:29 `final trip = json['trip'] ?? json['ride'];`
ride_history_repositories.dart:38 `final trips = json['trips'];`
openapi.yaml /rider/trips/active → `$ref: '#/components/schemas/TripProjection'`, '204': No active trip; /rider/trips → `TripProjectionPage` (Page.items)
failure_scenario: In a release build on a contract backend, the rider books on another device, or the snapshot was evicted, and then cold-starts or taps a push. `fetchActive` returns null, so the live ride is not restored. The History screen shows no server trips.
suggested_fix: Read a bare projection (`tripProjectionOf(json)`) for the active trip and `items` for pages. Change the mock to answer as openapi does (bare projection or 204, and `{items, nextCursor}`).

title: Several contract mutations are sent without the Idempotency-Key that openapi requires; the mock accepts mutations without a key
description: openapi `components/parameters/IdempotencyKey` is `required: true` ('Required on every mutation') on `POST /quotes`, `POST /trips/{id}/route-quote` and `POST /payments/{id}/confirm`. The rider sends these without a key. ApiQuoteRepository posts `/api/v1/quotes` with no `idempotencyKey` (api_quote_repository.dart:29). RouteChangeController posts `/api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote` with none (route_change_controller.dart:200). ApiPaymentGateway.confirm posts `/api/v1/payments/$id/confirm` with none (api_payment_gateway.dart:85). The stand-in server never notices, because a request without a key just skips the replay table (`replayKey = key == null || key.isEmpty ? null : ...`). The rider app was never checked against the requirement. A contract server rejects these requests. Even a lenient one cannot de-duplicate a confirm that is retried after a lost response.
evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:286 `final replayKey = key == null || key.isEmpty ? null : '$method $path $key';`
api_quote_repository.dart:29 `final json = await api.post('/api/v1/quotes', body: {...});` (no idempotencyKey)
route_change_controller.dart:199-202 `() => _api.post('/api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote', body: {...draft.toRequest(), 'expectedVersion': ?version}),`
api_payment_gateway.dart:85 `final response = await _api.post('/api/v1/payments/$id/confirm');`
openapi.yaml IdempotencyKey: `required: true`
failure_scenario: On a backend that enforces the contract header, Select Ride gets no prices (quote request refused) and the in-trip destination change cannot be priced. A card confirm that is retried after a timeout has no key the server can use to recognise the repeat.
suggested_fix: Send a stable Idempotency-Key (MutationAttempt or stableIdempotencyKey) on every POST/PATCH/DELETE the contract defines. Have the mock answer 400 when a mutation has no key.

title: The rider speaks X-Api-Version 0.4 but polls and books on the `/rides` routes that openapi v0.4 lists as removed after v0.3, and reads a quote shape that is not the contract's
description: ApiClient sends `X-Api-Version: 0.4` on every request (api_client.dart:15). openapi v0.4 has only two `/rides` routes, `GET /rides/{rideId}` and `POST /rides/{rideId}/cancel`, both marked 'Deprecated alias ... Removed after v0.3'. It has no `POST /rides`, `PATCH /rides/{id}`, `/rides/{id}/route-quote`, `/rides/{id}/end-early` or `/rides/{id}/feedback`; those live under `/trips` and `/trips/{id}/rating`. Release realtime polls `GET /api/v1/rides/{id}`. On a v0.4 server that alias is gone, so each poll 404s, and after `notFoundLimit` (3) polling pauses and the ride freezes. Booking has the same mismatch. ApiQuoteRepository requires `json['quote']` plus a non-contract `signedPayload`, where the contract returns `QuoteList {quotes, zoneId}`, and it leaves out `stops` when empty although QuoteRequest says stops 'MUST be sent'. This is a different defect from the known projection-field one (ride_projection.dart:80): here the routes and the quote container do not match the contract the app declares.
evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:99 `final json = await _api.get('/api/v1/rides/${Uri.encodeComponent(poll.id)}');`
api_client.dart:15 `static const apiVersion = '0.4';`
openapi.yaml /rides/{rideId}: `summary: Deprecated alias of GET /trips/{tripId}` `description: Removed after v0.3.`
api_quote_repository.dart:47-52 `if (stops.isNotEmpty) 'stops': [...]` / `final raw = json['quote']; if (raw is! Map) throw const FormatException('malformed quote');` and the signedPayload check at :69-72
failure_scenario: Pointed at a v0.4 backend (MOVERA_API_BASE_URL), the rider cannot get quotes (FormatException 'malformed quote'), cannot book (POST /api/v1/rides is not a contract route), and a ride's realtime poll 404s three times and then stops.
suggested_fix: Move the rider wire to the v0.4 routes (`/trips`, `/trips/{id}/events|end-early|rating`, `POST /quotes` → `quotes[]`). Until then, send the version the client actually speaks, not 0.4.

title: OfferWire.parse drops Offer.kind, expiresAt, driverEarnings and reasonCode: system Exclusive offers become Radar trips, the countdown ignores the server's expiry, and `wallet` shows as Card
description: The contract `Offer` carries `kind` (radar | exclusive | assigned | reservation | next_trip), `expiresAt`, `driverEarnings` and, for Exclusive offers, `reasonCode`. `OfferWire.parse` reads `kind` only to tell `reservation` (line 89) and `next_trip` (line 309) apart. RideOffer has no field for an Exclusive offer, and `isAdminDirectAssign` is just `source == admin && groupId == null`. So a dispatch Exclusive offer (`kind: exclusive, source: system`) becomes an ordinary Radar trip: no one-driver Accept/Decline flow, and no auto-offline count (Q16) for it. `expiresAt` is never read, so the card countdown uses the local `DriverOfferRules.radarTime` / `exclusiveAcceptTime` from when the card appears. An offer loaded late (from `GET /driver/offers` after a reconnect, or delivered late on the feed) shows a full timer while the server has already expired it. `driverEarnings` (required, includes driverBonus) is ignored; the net fare is later recomputed locally from a label. `_payments` has no `wallet` entry, so a wallet-paid offer shows 'Card'.
evidence:
api_dispatch_repository.dart:14-19 `_payments = {'cash': 'Cash', 'card': 'Card', 'apple_pay': 'Apple Pay', 'google_pay': 'Google Pay'}`
:59-95 `return RideOffer(id: text('offerId'), tripId: text('tripId'), version: whole('version'), ... payment: _payments[json['paymentMethod']] ?? 'Card', reservationTime: json['kind'] == 'reservation' && at != null ? ... : null, ...)` (no kind/expiresAt/driverEarnings/reasonCode)
dispatch_repository.dart:185-186 `bool get isAdminDirectAssign => source == OfferSource.admin && groupId == null;`
failure_scenario: Once ApiDispatchRepository is installed, dispatch sends this driver an Exclusive offer. It appears among Radar trips with a fresh 15 s timer, not as the Exclusive card. If the server's expiresAt was 5 s away, the driver taps Match after it lapsed and gets 'expired'. Missed Exclusive offers never count towards auto-offline.
suggested_fix: Carry `kind`, `expiresAt`, `driverEarnings` and `reasonCode` into RideOffer. Drive the Exclusive/Radar choice and the countdown from them. Map `wallet` to its own label.

title: Mock rider PIN is the clock's microseconds mod 10000; on web that is always one of ten values (0000, 1000 … 9000)
description: `_newPin` sets `n = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch % 10000`. On dart2js, `DateTime.now()` has millisecond precision (the microsecond part is 0), so `microsecondsSinceEpoch` is always a multiple of 1000 and `n` is `(ms % 10) * 1000`. Every PIN issued or rotated on the public web demo, the transport the Pages build actually runs, ends in 000: there are only 10 possible PINs, and the digit is just the last digit of the current millisecond. The rider page then says 'Your driver must confirm your PIN before starting the trip' over a code anyone can guess. The mock also writes the digits in plaintext to localStorage (`movera_safety_demo_v1`, persist() line 87-94), although safety_data_sources.dart:146-149 says web keeps the PIN 'in memory only (P-06) — never in this plaintext prefs blob'. Verified by reading only (no web test runner).
evidence:
safety_mock_api.dart:155-161 `final now = DateTime.now().toUtc(); final n = now.microsecondsSinceEpoch % 10000; return { 'pinId': 'pin_${now.microsecondsSinceEpoch}', ... 'pin': n.toString().padLeft(4, '0'),`
:87-94 `await prefs.setString(storageKey, jsonEncode({'preferences': preferences, 'pin': pin, ...}))`
failure_scenario: On the GitHub Pages demo, Safety › PIN shows e.g. '7000'. Change PIN gives '3000', '0000' and so on, always ending in 000.
suggested_fix: Generate the mock PIN with `Random.secure().nextInt(10000)`. Do not persist the digits in the plaintext demo blob.

title: Admin-published rider cancel reasons (`RiderAppConfig.cancelReasons`) are parsed but never used; the reason sheet is hard-coded
description: CONTRACT.md §5 lists 'Cancel reasons (Dispatch › Cancel reasons) | rider.cancelReasons | Rider reason list'. RiderAppConfig parses `cancelReasons` (rider_app_config.dart:295) and keeps rider codes only. Nothing in lib reads `config.cancelReasons`; the only references are in tests. Cancel sheets and reservation cancels use the fixed `CancellationReason.forPhase` lists. If admin removes or retitles a reason, the rider still offers and sends the shipped list. The server validates `reasonCode` per actor and may refuse a code that admin turned off.
evidence:
rider_app_config.dart:295-296 `cancelReasons: _reasons(raw['cancelReasons']) ?? fallback?.cancelReasons ?? const [],`
grep `.cancelReasons` → only rider_app_config.dart and test/contracts/rider_app_config_admin_export_test.dart
cancel_reason_sheet.dart:67 `final reasons = CancellationReason.forPhase(widget.phase);`
cancellation_reason.dart:60-96 fixed lists
failure_scenario: The zone document publishes cancelReasons [pickup_incorrect, plans_changed, something_else] (contracts/fixtures/config/rider_app_config.json). The rider's searching sheet still shows seven reasons, including wrong_ride_option, requested_by_mistake, wait_too_long and destination_change, with app-bundled titles instead of admin's.
suggested_fix: Build the reason sheet from `RiderAppConfig.current.cancelReasons` (filtered per phase), and fall back to the seed lists only when the document has none.

title: API_V1_MOCK.md says three 404s end the ride as cancelledBySystem and that ApiClient sends X-Api-Version v1; the code does neither
description: ARCHITECTURE.md points to docs/API_V1_MOCK.md as the mock contract. That document says 'Three `404`s in a row end the ride as `cancelledBySystem`' (line 99) and '`X-Api-Version` | Always `v1` from `ApiClient`' (line 27). It also says POST /rides returns status `findingDriver`/`bookingRequested` (line 84). In the code, `_endNotFound` only pauses polling and marks the connection failed, with no status change (api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353). ApiClient sends `'0.4'` (api_client.dart:15), and the mock stores contract names `searching`/`requested`. A QA or backend engineer working from the doc expects a cancelledBySystem terminal (History entry, Home) and a v1 header; neither happens.
evidence:
API_V1_MOCK.md:99 `Three \`404\`s in a row end the ride as \`cancelledBySystem\`; failures back off.`
API_V1_MOCK.md:27 `| \`X-Api-Version\` | yes | Always \`v1\` from \`ApiClient\` |`
api_ride_realtime.dart:347-352 `void _endNotFound(_RidePoll poll) { poll.ended = true; poll.timer?.cancel(); ... connection.markFailed(); }`
api_client.dart:15 `static const apiVersion = '0.4';`
failure_scenario: The server forgets a ride (three 404s). Following the doc, QA expects the ride to end as cancelledBySystem. Instead the ride stays on its last status with polling stopped.
suggested_fix: Update API_V1_MOCK.md to the current behaviour (polling pauses with no client-invented status, header 0.4, contract status names), or change the code to match the documented behaviour.

title: A wallet-paid ride is only deducted if the completion screen is still open when paymentFinalized arrives, so tapping Done or Back early, or ending the trip early, means the ride is never charged
description: D-022 says a wallet-paid ride is deducted once it reaches paymentFinalized. The only caller of WalletController.chargeCompletedRideById is RideCompleted._maybeChargeWallet, which runs from initState and from the realtime listener on this screen. The Done button is enabled at every completion status (`onPressed: _leaving ? null : _closeAndHome`), and Back with nothing selected leaves at once. If the rider leaves while the status is still tripCompleted or paymentProcessing, three things happen: _leave calls closeCompletedRide, which archives the ride and runs `_store.clear()` on the snapshot; dispose cancels _completionSub; and the later paymentFinalized event reaches nobody. Nothing tries the charge again: the snapshot is gone and nothing else calls chargeCompletedRide. Ended-early trips are never charged at all, because initState returns before both _maybeChargeWallet calls (`if (widget.endedEarly != null) return;`).
failure_scenario: Demo/dev build. The wallet holds 500 kr and the rider books a 259 kr ride paid by Movera Wallet. When the trip completes, the mock realtime only sends paymentFinalized after about 1 s (paymentProcessingAfter plus paymentFinalizedAfter, 500 ms each). The rider taps Done straight away and the balance stays at 500 kr for good. I reproduced this with a throwaway widget test built on phase105_wallet_ride_charge_test: pump RideCompleted at tripCompleted, replace it with SizedBox, then emit paymentFinalized. Output: 'balance after leaving early then paymentFinalized: 500.0' (expected 241). The same happens for any ended-early trip paid from the wallet.
evidence:
ride_completed.dart:102 `if (widget.endedEarly != null) return;` (before _maybeChargeWallet at 143)
ride_completed.dart:151-154 `if (_completionRank(_status) < _completionRank(RideStatus.paymentFinalized)) { return; }`
ride_completed.dart:414 `onPressed: _leaving ? null : _closeAndHome,`
ride_completed.dart:252-253 `await _controller.closeCompletedRide(widget.rideId!);`
active_ride_controller.dart:461 `await _store.clear();`
wallet_controller.dart:238-244 chargeCompletedRideById reads LastCompletedRide or RideSnapshotStore.readForArchive(); its only caller is ride_completed.dart:163
suggested_fix: Do not tie the debit to this screen's lifetime. Either record a pending wallet charge for the ride id when it completes and settle it from an app-level listener once the payment is final, or charge when the ride closes, using the booked wallet part or the ended-early `charged` amount, keeping the existing charged-rides guard against double charging.

title: In release builds the default chosen on the Payments tab only goes to local prefs, while Select Ride reads and writes the server default, so the choice is ignored at booking
description: In release, di.dart sets `defaultPayment = methods` (ApiPaymentMethodRepository, server GET/PATCH /api/v1/payment-methods). RideSelectionController.restoreDefaultPayment and _persistSelectedBrand use that store (select_ride.dart:274 `paymentStore: AppScope.instance.defaultPayment`). The Wallet & Payments 'How do you want to pay' tab (WalletScreen) does not use it: _restorePaymentSettings and _savePaymentSettings go through WalletController.loadPayments/savePayments, which call WalletStore and read and write the SharedPreferences key 'movera_default_payment' directly. This tab is a bottom tab in every build (home.dart:1849 `WalletAndPaymentsScreen(initialTab: 1)`). In release the two defaults therefore drift apart. The tab marks a method 'Default for rides' that Select Ride never preselects, and a default the rider picks at Select Ride is never shown on the tab.
failure_scenario: Staging/production. On the Payments tab the rider taps Google Pay, and the tile shows the check and 'Default for rides'. They open Select Ride, which calls ApiPaymentMethodRepository.read(), gets the server's defaultMethodId ('cash') and preselects Cash. The rider books a cash ride although they set Google Pay as their default.
evidence:
di.dart:150-153 `if (release) { final methods = ApiPaymentMethodRepository(api: api); payments = methods; defaultPayment = methods;`
wallet.dart:763 `final saved = await _wallet.loadPayments();`
wallet.dart:774-781 `await _wallet.savePayments(WalletPaymentSettings(defaultMethod: _selectedMethod, ...))`
wallet_repository.dart:91 `final savedDefault = prefs.getString('movera_default_payment');`
wallet_repository.dart:114-120 `await prefs.setString('movera_default_payment', ...)`
ride_selection_controller.dart:573-574 `final store = _paymentStore; final saved = store == null ? null : await store.read();`
suggested_fix: Read and save the default method on the Payments tab through AppScope.instance.defaultPayment (the composed DefaultPaymentStore), and keep WalletStore for the wallet-only settings (business, use wallet first).

title: 'Days left' on a promotion uses local-midnight Duration.inDays, so it is one day short across spring-forward and says 'Ends today' for a promotion that ends tomorrow
description: validityText builds two local midnights and uses `last.difference(today).inDays`. When the range includes the spring-forward night, the two midnights are 23 h apart per transition, so inDays rounds down. Every count across the DST change is one day short. When the promotion ends the day after the change, days is 0 and the sheet shows 'Ends today'.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a throwaway test run under TZ=Europe/Stockholm. A promotion with endsAt '2026-03-30T18:00:00' viewed at 2026-03-29 12:00 showed 'Ends today' (expected '1 day left'). A promotion ending on 15 Apr viewed on 1 Mar showed 'Valid until 15 Apr 2026 · 44 days left' (expected 45).
evidence:
promotion_details_sheet.dart:110-113
`final today = DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day);`
`final last = DateTime(ends.year, ends.month, ends.day);`
`final days = last.difference(today).inDays;`
`if (days <= 0) return L10n.current.endsToday;`
suggested_fix: Count calendar days with UTC dates: `DateTime.utc(ends.year, ends.month, ends.day).difference(DateTime.utc(now.year, now.month, now.day)).inDays`.

title: New History records store English cancel reasons ('No driver found', 'Request expired', 'Cancelled by Movera', ...), which the detail sheet shows untranslated
description: recordFor falls back to `_endedSearchReason(terminalStatus)` when no reason code is given. That writes English sentences into Reservation.cancellationReason for every server-ended ride (noDriverFound, bookingExpired, cancelledByAdmin, cancelledBySystem, noShow, tripFailed, endedByDriver). The History detail line shows them through ReservationFormat.reasonLabel. That function only translates reason ids, `system_*` codes, `admin_*` and snake_case strings, and returns anything else unchanged ('older records already hold a label ... and are shown as they are'). Records created today therefore keep English text in sv and fr, although translated strings exist (L10n.termNoDriverFound, cancelledByMovera, reasonNoShow, ...).
failure_scenario: App language is Swedish. A search ends with no driver, so the ride is archived as noDriverFound. In History › Cancelled › tap the ride, the line reads 'Reason: No driver found' in English inside a Swedish sheet.
evidence:
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:228-231 `cancellationReason: cancellationReason ?? snapshot.cancellationReason ?? _endedSearchReason(terminalStatus),`
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:261-271 `RideStatus.noDriverFound => 'No driver found', RideStatus.bookingExpired => 'Request expired', RideStatus.cancelledByAdmin => 'Cancelled by Movera', ...`
reservation_format.dart:60-64 snake_case check, then `return value;`
ride_history.dart:561 `context.l10n.reasonLine(ReservationFormat.reasonLabel(ride.cancellationReason!))`
suggested_fix: Store reason codes (for example 'system_no_driver', 'system_expired', 'admin_cancelled', 'rider_no_show', 'system_error', 'driver_ended') and map them in ReservationFormat._reasonLabels to the existing l10n strings.

title: Ride receipt shows the stored payment names 'Movera Wallet' / 'Card' in English; only Cash is translated
description: The completion receipt builds its Payment method row with `L10n.isCashLabel(trip.method) ? payCash : trip.method`. trip.method is the snapshot's English paymentMethod name, set when Select Ride books with `paymentMethod: payment.name`. A wallet or generic-card ride therefore shows 'Movera Wallet' or 'Card' in every language, although the ARB files translate them (sv 'Movera Plånbok' / 'Kort', fr 'Portefeuille Movera' / 'Carte') and payment_labels.dart already has paymentLabelFor for exactly this mapping. The known finding covers the History detail at ride_history.dart:552; this is the separate receipt on the ride-complete screen.
failure_scenario: App language is French. The rider pays a ride with the Movera Wallet. The Ride summary's Trip details card shows 'Payment method: Movera Wallet' instead of 'Portefeuille Movera'.
evidence:
trip_detail.dart:75-80 `_detailRow(context.l10n.paymentMethod, L10n.isCashLabel(trip.method) ? context.l10n.payCash : trip.method,)`
driver_repository.dart:116 `method: ride.paymentMethod,`
payment_labels.dart:24-29 `String paymentLabelFor(String stored) => switch (stored.trim()) { 'Cash' => ..., 'Card' => L10n.current.payCard, 'Movera Wallet' => L10n.current.moveraWallet, ...`
suggested_fix: Use `paymentLabelFor(trip.method)` for the receipt row, and also accept the localized cash label if isCashLabel is still needed.

title: A failed PATCH of the default payment method is swallowed, and the next read() puts the server's old default back, so the rider's choice silently reverts
description: save() sets `_defaultId = brand` first and then only logs a PATCH failure. Nothing retries the PATCH. read() then overwrites `_defaultId` with the server's `defaultMethodId` whenever the GET succeeds. RideSelectionController calls read() on every Select Ride open (restoreDefaultPayment), so after one failed PATCH the next open preselects the old method with no message.
failure_scenario: Release build with a flaky network. At Select Ride the rider switches from Cash to Google Pay. The PATCH /payment-methods/default fails and is logged as payments.default_save_failed. They back out and open Select Ride again. The GET succeeds with defaultMethodId 'cash', and Cash is preselected again, so the rider may book with a method they had changed away from.
evidence:
api_payment_method_repository.dart:55-68 `_defaultId = brand; try { await _api.patch('$path/default', ...); } catch (error) { AppLog.warning('payments.default_save_failed', ...); }`
api_payment_method_repository.dart:40-43 `final json = await _api.get(path); _defaultId = _string(json['defaultMethodId']) ?? _defaultId;`
ride_selection_controller.dart:609 `unawaited(store.save(selected.brand));`
suggested_fix: Keep a pending-save flag: retry the PATCH on the next read(), and don't let the server value overwrite the local choice until the PATCH succeeds. Or surface the failure so the UI can tell the rider.

title: Saved cards that have expired stay listed and selectable as the ride and default payment method
description: Expiry is checked only when a card is added (CardInput.expiryInFuture in add()). list() returns every stored card. RideSelectionController.savedCardItems offers every listed card as a booking method, and the Payments tab offers it as the default (wallet.dart:987). Neither checks expMonth/expYear against today. A card that expired after it was saved can therefore be preselected and used to book.
failure_scenario: Demo build. In August 2026 the rider saves a card expiring 09/26. In October 2026 Select Ride still lists 'Visa •••• 4242 · Expires 09/26' and preselects it if it is the default. The ride is booked against an expired card with no warning.
evidence:
saved_cards_controller.dart:142 `List<SavedCard> list() => List.unmodifiable(_cards);`
saved_cards_controller.dart:179 expiry is checked only in add(): `if (!CardInput.expiryInFuture(expMonth, expYear, now: now))`
ride_selection_controller.dart:217-223 `for (final card in _savedCards.list()) RidePaymentItem(brand: card.methodBrand, ...)`
wallet.dart:987 `for (final card in _offers('card') ? _cards.list() : const <SavedCard>[])`
suggested_fix: Filter out expired cards, or show them as disabled, when building the payment lists (CardInput.expiryInFuture(card.expMonth, card.expYear)). Fall back to the default method when the saved default card has expired.

title: Outbox flush replays a cancel queued during search against a trip a driver has since accepted, and rebases expectedVersion so the server cannot refuse it
description: RC-03 and the controller's own comments say a cancel queued during the search must never cancel a ride a driver accepted meanwhile. Line 381 says "never for a ride a driver already accepted", lines 948-950 say "the stale request leaves the outbox so it cannot cancel the matched ride later", and ARCHITECTURE says a driver-accepted race moves the rider on to Waiting. The flush (`_flushPendingCancels`) runs from the reconnect watcher, the bootstrap flush, the restore `_dropIfCancelQueued` flush and the Finding listener. It re-reads the trip first. `_rereadForReplay` accepts the cancel whenever `TripStateMachine.apply(status, 'cancel', rider)` is non-null, and the rider `cancel` transition is legal from accepted, driver_to_pickup and arrived (trip_transitions.dart:101). Then, when the version moved (a driver accepting bumps it), `cancel.forVersion(version)` mints a new key and sends the trip's current version. So the R-O2 version check, which would have answered 409 version_mismatch / stale, is defeated, and the server cancels the matched trip. The entry has no field saying it was queued while searching, so nothing else stops this.
failure_scenario: The rider taps Cancel request while offline, so the cancel is queued and the screen shows Cancelling…. A driver accepts on the server. Connectivity returns: the reconnect watcher's flush GETs the trip (accepted), rebases the version and POSTs the cancel, and the server cancels the accepted trip (possibly with a late-cancel fee and a driver penalty). Meanwhile Finding may already have received the match, shown "A driver already accepted your ride" and opened Waiting, which then dies as cancelled. After a reload (cold restore) the rider lands on Home with the ride archived as cancelled, although the documented outcome is that the match wins.
suggested_fix: Record on the entry the stage it was queued at (or keep the original expectedVersion). For a Finding cancel, treat any re-read outside requested/searching/offered as stale (report it so `_completeAssigned` / onCancelRefused runs), and do not rebase the version across a status change.

title: Price raise the server accepted is thrown away and reported as failed when the rider taps Cancel during the PATCH; the fare shown stays the old one
description: `cancelSearch` does not check `_editInFlight`. It just bumps `_editEpoch` (line 1102), and the Cancel X stays tappable while the price-bump card is busy. When the raise PATCH response then arrives, `ride.observeProjection(response)` records the new version, but `_editInvalid(editToken)` is true, so the method returns false before `_snapshot` or the store is updated and before `_bumpDismissed`/`offerConfirmation` are set. `_raiseOffer` then shows `editFeedback ?? editOfferFailed`, and `editFeedback` was reset to null, so the rider sees "couldn't update your offer". If the cancel does not commit (409 driver accepted, or `stale` because the raise bumped the version), the search goes on with the pre-raise price: the card shows again, `_persistAssigned` saves the old price, and Waiting gets `price: _match.currentPrice` (old). A second raise is computed from the old fare while the server adds it on top of the already-raised fare.
failure_scenario: After 45 s the rider taps +20 kr. While the PATCH is in flight they hit X → Cancel request. The server applies the raise (279 kr). The cancel comes back 409 (version changed / driver accepted). Finding says the offer failed and keeps showing 259 kr, Waiting and History show 259 kr, and the rider is charged 279 kr. If they raise again (+20), the server makes it 299 kr while the button previewed 279 kr.
suggested_fix: When the PATCH succeeded, apply the server fare to `_snapshot` (and the store) even if a cancel started meanwhile, unless the cancel committed. Or make `cancelSearch` wait for / refuse while `_editInFlight`, and disable the X while an edit is busy.

title: "Try again" after no driver found leaves the screen poppable while the new booking is created, orphaning a live search
description: `_handleTerminal` sets `_leaving = true` (line 323) before showing the no-driver sheet. On Try again, `_requestAgain` awaits `submitFinding` (a quote plus POST /rides, two round trips) and only resets `_leaving = false` after success (line 380). The screen's `PopScope(canPop: _leaving)` therefore lets a system back / swipe pop Finding during the request, and the X is inert (`_confirmCancel` returns on `_leaving`). The booking still creates the server ride and saves its snapshot (BookingCoordinator._submitFinding), but `_requestAgain` sees `!mounted` and returns false. No Finding owns the new live ride, `FindingDriverController.active` is null (cleared by `_completeTerminal`), and nothing navigates to it until a later lifecycle resume/reload restore.
evidence:
finding_drivers.dart:323 `_leaving = true;`
finding_drivers.dart:338-341 `final choice = await showNoDriverFoundSheet(context); ... if (choice == NoDriverChoice.tryAgain && await _requestAgain(ended)) {`
finding_drivers.dart:352 `rideId = await (widget.booking ?? BookingController()).submitFinding(`
finding_drivers.dart:376 `if (!mounted || rideId.trim().isEmpty) return false;`
finding_drivers.dart:808-811 `return PopScope(canPop: _leaving, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) { if (!didPop) _confirmCancel(); },`
booking_coordinator.dart:44 `bool get _findingAlreadyActive => FindingDriverController.active != null;`
failure_scenario: No driver found → the rider taps Try again, sees nothing change for a second and swipes back. Finding pops to Select Ride/Home. The server has a new searching ride with the stored snapshot, but no screen shows it. A driver can accept it unseen. If the rider books again from Select Ride, `_findingAlreadyActive` is false, so a second live ride is created.
suggested_fix: Set `_leaving = false` (or keep a separate rebooking flag that keeps canPop false and shows progress) while `_requestAgain` is in flight. If the widget unmounted after the ride was created, hand the ride to `RideRestoreCoordinator.recoverCreatedFinding`.

title: Cancel reason attached to an outbox entry is silently dropped when the replay re-read finds the trip already cancelled
description: For a queued cancel that the server already applied (the response was lost), Finding commits through the realtime listener (lines 375-378 → `_confirmQueuedCancel`) without removing the outbox entry. The why-sheet then calls `sendCancelReason`, and `PendingCancelStore.attachReason` finds the stale entry, stores the reason on it and returns true, so no POST is made (line 1376). When the outbox is later flushed, `_rereadForReplay` sees `cancelled_by_rider` and returns `sent` without sending anything, then the entry is removed. The reason never reaches the server, although the doc says it "rides along with a cancel still queued in the outbox". The mock contract stores a later reason on a cancelled ride, so the code plainly expects the server to have it.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:375-378 `if (_cancelQueued && event.status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider) { unawaited(_confirmQueuedCancel()); return; }` (no PendingCancelStore.remove)
finding_driver_controller.dart:1376 `if (await PendingCancelStore.attachReason(id, reasonId)) return;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1549-1551 `if (status == TripStatus.cancelledByRider) { return (result: PendingCancelResult.sent, version: version); }`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1498 `await PendingCancelStore.remove(cancel.rideId);`
failure_scenario: On a flaky network the cancel POST lands but both responses time out, so it is queued. The next poll shows cancelled_by_rider, Finding commits and the why-sheet opens. The rider picks "Driver too far" and Send. The reason is written into the outbox entry, and the next flush drops it unsent. Support/admin never see the rider's cancel reason.
suggested_fix: Remove the outbox entry when a queued cancel is confirmed by realtime/server check. Or, in `_rereadForReplay`, when the trip is already cancelled_by_rider and the entry carries a reason, still POST the (idempotent) cancel with the reason.

title: checkServerSearchState ignores a queued cancel: a server cancelled_by_rider is handled as a foreign terminal (no History record, no why-sheet, outbox entry left)
description: The realtime listener treats `cancelledByRider` while `_cancelQueued` as the queued cancel landing (`_confirmQueuedCancel`: archive, why-sheet). `checkServerSearchState` checks neither `_cancelQueued` before nor after its await. On a restore whose search is past `searchTimeout`, `start()` schedules `_reachSearchTimeout` as a microtask, which starts the GET before the async `_adoptQueuedCancel` has set `_cancelQueued`. When the GET answers cancelled_by_rider, it calls `_completeTerminal(cancelledByRider)`. That status is not in the archive list, so History gets no record, `_queuedReasonId` is lost, and `_handleTerminal` (with `_match.cancelled` false) shows the generic terminal sheet instead of the committed-cancel flow.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:355-360 `if (elapsedSeconds >= searchTimeout.inSeconds) { scheduleMicrotask(_reachSearchTimeout); } ... unawaited(_adoptQueuedCancel(snapshot.rideId));`
finding_driver_controller.dart:503-509 post-await guard has no `_cancelQueued`
finding_driver_controller.dart:527-529 `if (status.isTerminal) { _realtime.unsubscribe(); await _completeTerminal(status);`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1027-1034 archive list omits cancelledByRider
failure_scenario: The rider cancels offline 4 minutes into a search and reloads. The restore flush times out (no answer in 4 s), so Finding is restored as Cancelling…. The server-state GET comes back cancelled_by_rider. The ride ends with the generic sheet, is not in History, and the queued reason is never sent.
suggested_fix: In checkServerSearchState, after the await, route `status == cancelledByRider` with `_cancelQueued` (or a stored outbox entry) to `_confirmQueuedCancel()`. Or skip the check while a cancel is queued.

title: Every 409 on the search cancel is reported as "a driver already accepted", even when the ride ended another way
description: Apart from version_mismatch and already-cancelled-by-rider, `_requestServerCancel` maps any 409 to `driverAccepted` without looking at the error projection's status. The outbox path (`_refusalResult`) re-reads the trip to tell "driver accepted" from "already over", but the foreground path does not. The contract says 409 means "the ride moved on first", which includes the search expiring (expired / no_driver_found) or an admin/system cancel at the same moment.
failure_scenario: The search expires on the server just as the rider taps Cancel request, and the server answers 409 with projection status expired. The rider sees "A driver already accepted your ride", then the no-driver-found sheet when realtime delivers the terminal.
suggested_fix: Branch on `TripStatusWire.parse(error.projection?['status'])`. Return driverAccepted only for matched stages, and treat a terminal projection as rejected or terminal.

title: A storage failure while queueing the cancel wedges the search screen (cancel stuck in flight, cancel sheet flag never cleared, matches never navigate)
description: `cancelSearch` sets `_cancelInFlight = true` and stops the tick, then awaits `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` outside any try. If SharedPreferences throws (web quota/blocked storage), the error escapes `cancelSearch`. In the sheet, `_confirm` closes with false and rethrows. In `_confirmCancel`, `await request` throws before `_cancelSheetOpen = false`, so `_drainDeferredNavigation` returns early from then on. In the controller, `_cancelInFlight` stays true: `cancelSearch` returns ignored, and `_completeAssigned` only sets `_assignmentPending` ("wait for the cancel"), which nothing ever resolves.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1101 `_cancelInFlight = true;` … 1175 `final entry = await PendingCancelStore.enqueue(` (no try)
finding_driver_controller.dart:939-944 `if (_editInFlight || _cancelInFlight) { _assignmentPending = true; return; }`
finding_drivers.dart:586 `final result = request == null ? null : await request;` 595 `_cancelSheetOpen = false;` (never reached)
finding_drivers.dart:272 `_cancelSheetOpen ||` blocks drain
failure_scenario: In a browser where localStorage writes throw, the rider taps Cancel request. The sheet closes, nothing is sent, the timer stops and the X does nothing. When a driver accepts, the rider is never moved to Waiting.
suggested_fix: Wrap the enqueue (and the whole server-cancel path) in try/catch. On failure, reset `_cancelInFlight`, restart the tick, still attempt the POST without the outbox, and make `_confirmCancel` clear `_cancelSheetOpen` in a finally.

title: Search elapsed clock freezes while a cancel is in flight or queued and resumes from the old value after a refusal
description: ARCH-3/RIDE-5 say elapsed counts from when the search started (`start()` derives it from `snapshot.searchStart`). `cancelSearch` and `_adoptQueuedCancel` cancel the 1-second tick. After a refusal (409/422/stale, or an outbox refused/stale outcome) `_startTick()` just restarts it, so `elapsedSeconds` misses the whole in-flight or offline period. The still-looking mark (searchTimeout), the periodic server check cadence, the price-bump time, the copy rotation and the progress bar all run late by that amount, while a reload would jump to the true value.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1105-1106 `_tick?.cancel(); _tick = null;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1242-1243 (queued adopt) `_tick?.cancel(); _tick = null;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1151-1152 `} else if (!_assigned) { _startTick(); }`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1284-1285 `} else if (!_assigned) { _startTick();`
finding_driver_controller.dart:339-340 `final sinceStart = DateTime.now().difference(snapshot.searchStart); elapsedSeconds = ...`
failure_scenario: The rider's cancel sits queued for 2 minutes offline, then is refused because a driver was about to accept, but the match falls through. The search shows 1:00 elapsed instead of 3:00, and the "Still looking for a driver" card and server check come 2 minutes late.
suggested_fix: In `_startTick` (or on refusal), recompute `elapsedSeconds` from `_snapshot.searchStart`, and run `_afterElapsed` for the skipped span.

title: Price-bump card rounds a SEK fare with öre to whole kronor, so its preview total and ceiling disagree with what the controller and server apply
description: For SEK the card computes from `major.round() * 100` for both the current fare and maxPrice. The controller adds the increase to the exact fare (`snapshot.fare.amountMinor + increase`) and checks it against the exact `maxOfferMinor`. SEK fares with öre happen when the demo promotion's percentage discount is applied in the quote (`(fullMinor * percentOff / 100).round()`). So the button preview ("Raise to 240 kr") is not the fare charged, and a typed total the card accepts as within the ceiling is refused locally by `confirmPriceIncreaseBy` with "couldn't update your offer".
evidence:
price_bump_card.dart:88-90 `int _minorOf(double major) => _kronor ? major.round() * _unitMinor : Money.fromLegacyMajor(major, widget.currency).amountMinor;`
price_bump_card.dart:117-118 `final extra = total * _unitMinor - _currentMinor; if (extra <= 0 || total * _unitMinor > _minorOf(widget.maxPrice)) {`
finding_driver_controller.dart:790-796 `final next = Money(snapshot.fare.amountMinor + increase.amountMinor, currency).major; if (next > maxOfferPrice || ...) return false;`
failure_scenario: With a promo the fare is 133.45 kr and maxOfferMinor is 24000 (240 kr). The rider types 240. The card enables "Raise to 240 kr" and sends +107 kr. The controller computes 240.45 kr > 240 and returns false, and the rider is told the raise failed.
suggested_fix: Compute the card's increase from the exact fare minor units (or send the target total and let the server price it), and compare against the exact maxOfferMinor.

title: Route-change pricing starts from the booked fare, so any route change (even re-quoting the same route) cancels and refunds the rider's offer raise
description: `_routeChangePricing` builds `newMinor` from `_bookedMinor(ride)`, which is `bookedFare`, the fare at booking *before* offer raises. It then works out `differenceMinor` against `_fareMinor(ride)`, the current fare, which *includes* the raise. So the raise the rider paid to get a driver comes out of every route quote and every applied route change. On PATCH routeChange, `_setFare(ride, newMinor)` lowers the fare and `maxOfferMinor` is recomputed from it. For non-cash methods a `refunded` paymentAdjustment is recorded. On the client, `route_change_flow.dart:166` credits the wallet with `-quote.differenceKr`. Path: Finding `confirmPriceIncreaseBy` sends PATCH {offerIncrease}, which `_setFare(fare+increase)` applies at line 993. Later, Waiting runs RouteChangeController.quote/apply, which calls POST route-quote and then PATCH routeChange, and those call `_routeChangePricing`.
evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:2055 `final bookedMinor = _bookedMinor(ride) ?? 0;`
2082-2091 `final newMinor = rates.roundToStep((bookedMinor + stops.length * rates.convertKronor(25) + (routeKm - bookedKm) * rates.perKmMinor)...); final currentMinor = _fareMinor(ride) ?? bookedMinor; return {'newMinor': newMinor, 'differenceMinor': newMinor - currentMinor, ...`
1928 `/// The fare at booking, before offers and route changes.`
Reproduced with a throwaway test: booked fare 28700, after +5000 raise 33700, route-quote of the *unchanged* route -> `newTotalMinor=28700 differenceMinor=-5000`.
failure_scenario: The rider books for kr 287 and raises the offer by kr 50 while searching (fare kr 337), then a driver accepts. On Waiting the rider adds a destination tweak or re-confirms the same destination. The route quote shows the new price as kr 287 with a kr 50 refund. Applying it lowers the fare to kr 287, records a kr 50 refund (or a wallet credit) and resets the offer ceiling, so the driver loses the raise they accepted.
suggested_fix: Price route changes from the current fare (or bookedFare plus the accumulated offerIncrease), not from bookedFare alone; keep the raise when computing newMinor.

title: Resuming a restored ride at driverWaiting restarts the GPS approach and regresses the status to driverArriving
description: In the primeResume path of `subscribe`, every non-trip matched status, driverWaiting included, places the driver about 850 m from the pickup and calls `_startGps()`. The first 3 s GPS tick moves the driver 18% closer, so it is still more than 50 m away. It then sets `status = RideStatus.driverArriving` and emits it with a newer version, which RideSession/DriverTrackingController accept. Path: a public Pages reload while the driver waits at the pickup goes through RideRestoreCoordinator.pageFor, which calls `realtime.primeResume(status: driverWaiting, ...)`, and then Waiting subscribes. The driver shows as arriving again, the waiting clock is lost, and the 'arrived' sheet comes back only after the walk repeats (about 30-40 s), then the 8 s board timer runs.
evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:206-212 `} else { // The remaining isMatched statuses are the pre-trip approach: driverAssigned, driverArriving, driverWaiting. lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; lastLng ??= _pickupLng! - 0.0048; _startGps(); }`
398-412 `lastLat = lastLat! + (pickupLat - lastLat!) * 0.18; ... var status = RideStatus.driverArriving; ... if (distance < 50) { status = RideStatus.driverWaiting; } lastStatus = status; _emit(status);`
Throwaway test: primeResume(status: driverWaiting, version: 7) + subscribe, after 3.3 s -> `statuses: [RideStatus.driverWaiting, RideStatus.driverArriving]`.
failure_scenario: The driver has arrived and the rider reloads the page. Waiting briefly shows 'Driver has arrived', then switches to 'Driver arriving, N min' with the marker 800 m away, and only later reports arrival again with a new waiting clock.
suggested_fix: For a driverWaiting resume, place the driver at the pickup and call `_startTrip()` (board timer) instead of `_startGps()`; also never let a GPS tick downgrade driverWaiting.

title: Pickup coordinates are not reset between rides, so the next ride's driver spawns near the previous ride's pickup
description: For a new ride, `subscribe` resets lastLat/lastLng, progress, trip start and clocks, but not `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`. `_assignNow` then uses `_pickupLat ??= ...` and `lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072` *before* `_hydratePickup()` fetches the new ride's pickup. On the second and later rides of a session, the driver is spawned next to the *previous* ride's pickup. That position is committed to the server through `_persistAssignment` (driverLat/driverLng) and is emitted to the UI, and the GPS walk then has to cross the whole distance. This is a different root cause from the known hard-coded Stockholm spawn (that one concerns the first ride or a resume, when the field is null).
evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:151-178 (reset block: `_rideId = rideId; _acceptedAt = null; ... lastLat = null; lastLng = null; ... _tripStartLng = null;`, no reset of `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`)
263-266 `_pickupLat ??= 59.3293; _pickupLng ??= 18.0686; lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; lastLng ??= _pickupLng! - 0.0048;`
305 `unawaited(_hydratePickup());` (only after the emit)
Throwaway test: ride r1 pickup Södertälje (59.1955), cancelRide, ride r2 pickup Arlanda (59.6498) -> `r2 assigned driver at 59.2027,17.6205; server driverLat=59.2027`.
failure_scenario: In one session the rider takes a ride from Södertälje and then books a ride from Arlanda. The 'driver found' marker and ETA show a driver about 50 km away at the old pickup, who then speeds across the map for about 100 s; the server projection stores that position too.
suggested_fix: Reset `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng` in subscribe for a new ride, and hydrate the pickup before spawning or emitting the assigned driver.

title: Mock driver never learns a pickup moved by a route change; it drives to and 'arrives' at the old pickup
description: The mock's GPS approach and `_etaSeconds` use `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`, which are set only once by `_hydratePickup()` after assignment. When the rider moves the pickup after accept (Q40, allowed up to maxPickupMoveMeters while accepted/driverToPickup), Waiting `_applyRouteChange` updates the tracking controller's pickup and the mock's destination only. It cannot update the mock's private pickup, and nothing re-reads it. The mock keeps walking to the old point and emits driverWaiting plus the 'arrived' signal within 50 m of the *old* pickup.
evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:379-383 `Future<void> _hydratePickup() async { final pickup = await _pickup(); _pickupLat = pickup.$1; _pickupLng = pickup.$2; }` (called only at line 305)
390-410 GPS walk toward `_pickupLat`/`_pickupLng`, `if (distance < 50) status = RideStatus.driverWaiting`
waiting_for_driver.dart:1230-1235 `if (realtime is MockRideRealtime) { realtime.destinationLat = ...; realtime.destinationLng = ...; }` (no pickup)
failure_scenario: After a driver accepts, the rider moves the pickup pin 250 m. The driver marker stops 250 m from the new pin and the sheet says 'Your driver has arrived at the pickup point'.
suggested_fix: Expose a pickup setter (as for the destination) and set it from `_applyRouteChange`, or re-hydrate the pickup from the server after a route change.

title: MockRideRealtime shows lifecycle steps the server refused or does not know, contrary to its own contract
description: The class contract says every step it shows is first committed on the stand-in server 'so the server projection and what the rider sees agree'. But `_enqueue` swallows every error, and `_assignNow` goes on to emit driverAssigned whatever `_persistAssignment` returned. The other steps (`_commit`) are fire-and-forget before the event is added. The in-process server keeps rides only in memory (ApiClient creates a fresh `InProcessMockClient` per page load and nothing re-seeds `rides`). So after a public Pages reload during Finding, the restored search runs on a ride the server does not have: POST /status answers 404, the error is ignored, and the rider is moved to Waiting with a made-up driver. The trip then plays out locally, and at the end POST /feedback answers 404. The same applies when the server refuses a commit for any other reason, for example a rider cancel that already landed.
evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:17-22 class doc `Every lifecycle step it shows is first committed on the stand-in server ... so the server projection and what the rider sees agree`
275 `await _persistAssignment(rideId);` then 301-303 `lastStatus = RideStatus.driverAssigned; _assignmentInFlight = false; _emit(RideStatus.driverAssigned);` (no check of the result)
786-793 `_commits = _commits.then((_) async { try { _observe(await call()); } catch (_) { // Mock transport: a refused or lost commit leaves the server as is. } });`
api_client.dart:30 `InProcessMockClient(persistSafety: true)` (only safety persisted)
Throwaway test on an id the server does not know: log `api.POST .../status ... status: 404` and then `statuses: [findingDriver, driverAssigned]; server knows ride: false`.
failure_scenario: On the public demo, the rider reloads while 'Finding a driver'. 25 s later a driver is 'found' and the trip completes, but the server has no such ride: route changes and the rating/tip POST fail with 404, and the completion screen shows that feedback could not be saved.
suggested_fix: Have `_enqueue` return the outcome and only emit a step whose commit succeeded (or resync from the server on refusal); for the demo, persist the mock's rides with the snapshot or re-seed the stand-in from the restored snapshot.

title: Polling drops fresh driver fixes whose coordinates did not change, so a stationary driver's location is marked stale
description: The 'nothing changed' short-circuit compares version, updatedAt, status and lat/lng, but not the fix time (`location.at` from `driverLocation.measuredAt` / `locationAt`). Location-only updates keep the version (and, in the documented stand-in, updatedAt) unchanged. So when the driver is stationary, for example waiting at the pickup or stopped at lights, every new fix with identical coordinates is swallowed and `locationAt` never advances. DriverTrackingController's 5 s stale check then marks the ETA stale after `DriverEta.staleAfter` (25 s) and shows 'Updating location…' / 'Waiting for fresh location' even though fresh fixes are arriving.
evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:205-211 `if (poll.version == version && poll.updatedAt == updatedAt && poll.lastStatus == status && poll.lastLat == location.lat && poll.lastLng == location.lng) { connection.markConnected(); return; }`
in_process_mock_client.dart:801-805 a GPS fix alone sets `locationAt` and only `_sequenceEvent(ride, 'location')` (no version/updatedAt bump)
driver_eta.dart:22 `static const staleAfter = Duration(seconds: 25);` and driver_tracking_controller.dart:196-202 the periodic staleness re-check
failure_scenario: In a release build the driver waits at the pickup and the phone reports the same coordinates every few seconds. About 25 s later the rider's Waiting sheet switches to 'Updating location…' and stays there while the driver waits, although the server has fresh fixes.
suggested_fix: Include the fix timestamp (and the eventId or sequence) in the no-change comparison, and track `poll.lastLocationAt`.

title: Not-found counter is not reset by non-404 failures, so non-consecutive 404s pause polling
description: `notFoundLimit` is documented as 'Consecutive 404s', but `poll.notFound` is reset only on a successful response. Timeouts, network errors and 5xx between two 404s leave it as it is, so an alternating pattern of 404 and timeout (for example a flaky gateway answering 404 during a deploy) reaches the limit. `_endNotFound` then cancels the timer, and the ride freezes until a resync. Per the known finding at line 383, a resync does not restart periodic polling.
evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:46-50 `/// Consecutive \`404\`s after which polling pauses`
102 `poll.notFound = 0;` (success path only)
264-271 `if (error is ApiError && error.statusCode == 404) { poll.notFound += 1; if (poll.notFound >= notFoundLimit) { _endNotFound(poll); return; } }` (no reset for other errors)
failure_scenario: A sequence of 404, timeout, 404, 503, 404 pauses polling for a live ride, and the rider's screen stops updating.
suggested_fix: Reset `poll.notFound = 0` in the catch block for any error that is not a 404.

title: API_V1_MOCK.md says three 404s end the ride as cancelledBySystem; ApiRideRealtime only pauses polling and emits nothing
description: The mock contract document states that realtime ends the ride as `cancelledBySystem` after three 404s in a row. The code deliberately emits no status (`_endNotFound` only cancels the timer and marks the connection failed), and a test pins that behaviour. Either the document or the code is wrong. As written, a ride the server deleted is never ended for the rider; it stays on a 'connection problem' state indefinitely.
evidence:
docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:99 `Three \`404\`s in a row end the ride as \`cancelledBySystem\`; failures back off.`
api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353 `void _endNotFound(_RidePoll poll) { poll.ended = true; poll.timer?.cancel(); poll.timer = null; ... connection.markFailed(); }`
failure_scenario: The backend purges a trip while the rider is on Waiting. After three polls the screen freezes with a connection banner instead of the documented system-cancel ending.
suggested_fix: Update docs/API_V1_MOCK.md to describe the pause/resync behaviour, or implement the documented terminal.

title: X-Api-Version sent is '0.4' while API_V1_MOCK.md documents 'Always v1 from ApiClient'
description: The documented mock contract says ApiClient always sends `X-Api-Version: v1`. The code sends `'0.4'`, which matches contracts/openapi.yaml (`const: '0.4'`). The ride-quote body separately still carries `'apiVersion': 'v1'`. The document is out of date, so a backend team working from API_V1_MOCK.md would expect a value the client never sends.
evidence:
api_client.dart:15 `static const apiVersion = '0.4';` / :84 `'X-Api-Version': apiVersion,`
docs/API_V1_MOCK.md:27 `| \`X-Api-Version\` | yes | Always \`v1\` from \`ApiClient\` |`
contracts/openapi.yaml:4518-4523 `name: X-Api-Version ... const: '0.4'`
failure_scenario: A gateway configured from API_V1_MOCK.md to require X-Api-Version: v1 rejects every request from the app.
suggested_fix: Fix the table row in docs/API_V1_MOCK.md to '0.4' (contract.json#headers).

title: The profile is never read from the server, so an empty device copy overwrites the rider's name and consents on the server with blanks
description: SyncedProfileRepository calls itself 'the profile the server knows', with the device copy only a cache (FLOW-7). But hydrate() only reads the local cache (`await _cache.hydrate()`). No GET is made. After any sign-out the cache is empty, because UserDataWipe removes movera_profile_v1 and clearLocal resets it to defaults; the same is true on a new device. Sign-in for a returning rider (isNewRider false) goes straight to Home, so the cache is never filled. Every later save sends the whole cached profile through body(): `'name': profile.name.trim()` (''), `language` 'en' and the default consents. The mock accepts an empty name, since it only rejects non-strings or names over 80 characters, and stores it. This was seen in a throwaway run, where the server profile became `{name: , language: en, consents: {rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: false, promotions: false}}`.
failure_scenario: A rider named 'Ada Lovelace' with promotions on signs out, then signs back in with the same phone (a returning rider, so no name step). She changes the app language in Account. The app sends PATCH /rider/profile {name: '', consents: {promotions: false, ...}}. Her name on the server (which the driver app shows) is erased and her marketing consent is switched off without her doing it.
suggested_fix: Read the server profile on hydrate or after sign-in (a GET or the verify response). Until it is known, send only the fields the rider changed, never the whole cached default profile.

title: Privacy switches build the next profile from a stale copy and do not move until the PATCH returns, so a second toggle reverts the first one locally and on the server
description: Each Switch's onChanged calls `_profile.update(ride.copyWith(...))`, where `ride` was captured at build time. ProfileController.update calls notifyListeners only after `_store.save(next)` returns. SyncedProfileRepository.save awaits the network PATCH (`await _sync(saved)`, up to the 15 s ApiClient timeout) before returning. So during the round trip the page does not rebuild: the tapped switch still shows its old value, and `ride` is still the old profile. If the rider taps another switch in that window, the new profile is built from the stale `ride` and overwrites the first change, both in the cache and in a second PATCH. This was reproduced with InProcessMockClient(latency: 2s): after tapping Offers, the switch still showed false while the model was true. Tapping Email then left promotions=false, both locally and on the server.
failure_scenario: On a slow connection the rider turns Offers on. The switch stays off, so they turn Email updates off as well. Offers ends up off on the device and on the server, although the rider turned it on.
suggested_fix: Notify listeners right after the cache write, before the network sync. Build each change from `_profile.profile` read at tap time, not from the build-time copy.

title: A 422 from the profile PATCH is treated as 'pending, retry later', so an over-long name blocks every later profile sync while the UI shows success
description: _sync catches every error, sets `_syncPending = true` and returns normally. A permanent 422 invalid_profile (the contract and mock reject names over 80 characters) therefore looks the same as a network failure. Every later save resends the same cached invalid name and fails again, so no consent or language change reaches the server. Callers are never told: PersonalInfoPage._save only shows saveFailed when update() throws, and it never throws for this. The name editor (showAccountTextEditor) has no length limit, and RiderNameScreen allows 40 + 1 + 40 = 81 characters. A throwaway run with an 81-character name showed `thrown=null pending=true server=null`. A later consent change gave `pending=true server=null`.
failure_scenario: A rider enters a long full name (over 80 characters) in Personal info. The tile shows the new name and no error appears. The server never gets it, and from then on every privacy or language change fails silently, so the server keeps stale consents.
suggested_fix: Mark only network/5xx/timeout errors as pending. Rethrow 4xx (422) errors so the screen can show them, and limit the name field to the contract's 80 characters.

title: The new-rider name step is not persisted: an app restart or web reload on it skips it for good and leaves the rider nameless
description: Whether the name step is needed is known only from the verify response (`result.isNewRider`). The tokens are already saved by then, and RiderNameScreen is shown as the root with no back button ('The session already exists here'). Nothing records that the name is still missing. On the next cold start or web reload, RideRestoreCoordinator._root() finds a valid session, so _shouldRequireSignIn is false, and returns pageFor(...), i.e. Home. RiderNameScreen is reachable only from PhoneVerification._verify, so the rider is never asked again. Android back at the root also exits the app (the gate's PopScope only blocks on web), with the same result.
failure_scenario: A first-time rider verifies the code, reaches 'What should we call you?', and the browser reloads or the app is killed. On reopening they land on Home with no name. Drivers see no rider name, the menu greets them with 'Welcome to Movera', and the step never comes back.
suggested_fix: Store a 'name pending' flag with the session, or send to the name step whenever the profile name is empty after sign-in, and route there from root() and enterMoveraApp.

title: OTP expiry is checked against the device clock, so a phone whose clock runs a few minutes fast can never sign in
description: OtpChallenge.isExpired compares the server's absolute `expiresAt` (mock: now + 5 min) with `DateTime.now().toUtc()` on the device. PhoneVerification._verify returns 'code expired' locally when it is true, before any request, and AuthRepository.verifyOtp throws StateError in the same case. If the device clock is ahead by more than the OTP lifetime, every challenge, including each one from Resend, is already expired on arrival and the code is never sent. The server is the authority and would answer 410 itself. The client check can only block valid codes.
failure_scenario: A laptop or phone with its clock set 6 minutes ahead opens Sign in. The rider types the correct code and gets 'This code has expired'. Resend gives the same result every time, so the rider cannot sign in.
suggested_fix: Work out the expiry from the local receipt time plus the server's remaining lifetime (expiresAt minus the server's issue time, or a TTL field), or let the server's 410 decide.

title: Successful OTP or provider sign-in waits for push registration (Firebase init, getToken, POST /push/devices) before the rider can continue
description: verifyOtp and signIn both `await _registerPushBestEffort()` before returning, so PhoneVerification keeps the Verify button busy and SignIn keeps the provider button busy until FirebasePushService.register() finishes. That means Firebase initialize, requestPermission, getToken (no timeout) and _replaceToken's POST (15 s timeout). Push consent is kept across sessions (movera.push_consent.v1 is not wiped, see the separate finding), so this happens on every later sign-in on a device where consent was ever given. This is the sign-in counterpart of the known cold-start finding at bootstrap.dart:130.
failure_scenario: On a poor connection a rider who once allowed notifications enters the correct code. The spinner keeps going for up to 15 s or more while the push device POST times out, then Home opens. It looks as if sign-in is hanging.
suggested_fix: Run registration with unawaited() after entering the app, as the bootstrap comment intends for the first frame.

title: Push consent ('movera.push_consent.v1') survives sign-out and account switch, so the next rider is registered for push without seeing the in-app explanation
description: UserDataWipe removes only keys starting with 'movera_' (except deviceKeys). PushPermissionGate stores consent under 'movera.push_consent.v1' (a dot, not an underscore), so it is never removed, and it is not listed among the documented kept keys either. After rider A accepted the primer and signs out, rider B's sign-in calls registerIfConsented, finds 'accepted' and registers B's device token straight away.
