The OS permission is already granted, so B sees no prompt. B never saw or accepted the explanation, although UI-17 says registration is only for 'a rider who accepted the in-app explanation'.
failure_scenario: On a shared phone, rider A turns on ride updates and signs out. Rider B signs in and starts getting ride push notifications without ever being asked.
suggested_fix: Either clear the consent key in UserDataWipe or list it explicitly in deviceKeys with the decision documented.

title: Inbound push routing (foreground, opened and the launch notification) is attached only after the backend acknowledges the device token
description: register() calls `_attachInboundStreams()` only after `await _replaceToken(token)` succeeds. That call POSTs /push/devices and throws when the request fails or is not acknowledged. `_attachInboundStreams` is the only place that listens to onMessage and onMessageOpenedApp and that reads getInitialMessage into `_initialMessage`. If the registration POST fails at cold start (5xx, timeout, offline; bootstrap catches and only logs it), PushCoordinator.start() gets null from takeInitialMessage(), and no foreground or opened push reaches it for the rest of the session. The OS still shows the notifications, because the FCM token exists. Sign-out's unregister() cancels the subscriptions, so a failed re-registration after the next sign-in has the same effect.
failure_scenario: The API is briefly unavailable when a rider taps a 'Your driver has arrived' notification that launches the app. POST /push/devices fails, so the tap lands on the default root instead of the ride. Later notification taps in that session also do nothing in the app.
suggested_fix: Attach the inbound listeners and read getInitialMessage as soon as Firebase is initialised and permission is granted, separately from whether the server acknowledged the token.

title: Foreground ride pushes never trigger a ride resync, although the feed code says ride pushes drive authoritative resync
description: NotificationsRepository.ingest skips data-only ride pushes because 'Data-only ride pushes still drive authoritative ride resync'. PushCoordinator._handleForeground (the only listener of foregroundMessages) only ingests and logs, and never calls rideRealtime.reconnectAndResync or the restore coordinator. A foreground 'driver assigned/arrived/cancelled' push therefore has no effect until the next poll or backoff tick. If polling is paused (for example after the not-found pause), the push that should wake the ride is dropped.
failure_scenario: The app is in the foreground on Finding and polling is in backoff after network errors. The server sends a data-only 'ride.driver_assigned' push, the app does nothing with it, and the rider keeps seeing 'Finding a driver' until the next successful poll.
suggested_fix: For a ride push in the foreground (payload.routedRideId != null), call AppScope.instance.rideRealtime.reconnectAndResync(rideId).

title: A push with a title but no body shows its raw wire type (e.g. 'ride.driver_assigned') as the notification text
description: The subtitle falls back to `payload.type` when the body is empty. The type is the internal event code that PushPayload requires (`ride.`/`trip.` prefixes), not text meant for the rider, so it is shown untranslated in every language.
evidence:
notifications_repository.dart:51-52
        title: title?.isNotEmpty == true ? title! : 'Movera',
        subtitle: body?.isNotEmpty == true ? body! : payload.type,
failure_scenario: The server sends a notification titled 'Your driver is here' with no body. The Notifications list shows 'Your driver is here' over the line 'ride.driver_arrived'.
suggested_fix: Use an empty subtitle, or a localized label per known type, when there is no body.

title: Menu pushes Notifications and Safety without route names, so pushPageOnce stacks a second copy when a push or the Safety bridge opens them
description: pushPageOnce avoids duplicates only by checking `_topRoute(nav)?.settings.name == name`. The side menu (and Account for SafetyHub) pushes `RightToLeftTransition(const NotificationScreen())` without settings, so the route name is null. A notification opened while the rider is on the menu's Notifications screen (PushCoordinator → _openNotificationsFromPush → pushPageOnce(..., AppRoutes.notifications)) pushes a second NotificationScreen on top. The web Safety bridge does the same over a menu-opened SafetyHub. This breaks bootstrap.dart's 'a second open does not stack a copy'.
failure_scenario: The rider opens Menu › Notifications. A promo push arrives and they tap the system banner. A second Notifications screen slides in, and Back has to be pressed twice to leave.
suggested_fix: Push these screens with RouteSettings(name: AppRoutes.notifications / AppRoutes.safety) everywhere, or open them through pushPageOnce.

title: Support ride rows show the full fare for cancelled rides and '0 · Cancelled' elsewhere, ignoring any recorded cancellation fee
description: SupportController.rideFor never passes the reservation's cancellationFee (`extra` is never set). SupportRide.priceLabel therefore shows `formatMajor(0)` · Cancelled for every cancelled ride (SupportHome cards, the SupportChat header and SelectIssue's trip line), even when a late-cancel fee was recorded. Ride History shows the same fee (`ride.cancellationFee ... context.l10n.cancelFee`). The 'View all' list (_RideRow) shows `formatMajor(ride.price, ...)` for the same cancelled ride, i.e. the full fare as if it had been charged. The two Support screens contradict each other, and both can differ from History.
evidence:
support.dart:1097  ride.failed ? context.l10n.supportFailed : formatMajor(ride.price, ride.currency),
domain/support.dart:41-46  if (cancelled) { final zero = formatMajor(0, currency); return extra == null ? L10n.current.supportPriceCancelled(zero) : ... }
support_controller.dart:39-47 rideFor sets no extra
local_reservation_repository.dart:233  cancellationFee: fee != null && fee.isPositive ? fee : null,
failure_scenario: A rider cancelled a kr 189 Comfort ride. Support › View all lists it at 'kr 189', while Support Home says 'kr 0 · Cancelled'. For a late-cancelled reservation with a kr 50 fee, History shows the kr 50 fee but Support shows kr 0. The rider raising a money issue sees the wrong amount.
suggested_fix: Carry the cancellation fee into SupportRide (extra or a fee field), and make _RideRow use the same priceLabel for cancelled rides.

title: Support 'Cases' always says 'No active cases', even right after the rider sent a ride issue
description: SupportMessages is static: it always renders 'No active cases' and 'You have no closed support cases.' No data source backs it. SupportChat really sends the message (POST /rides/{id}/disputes, which answers `status: submitted`) and says 'Sent to Movera. The team reviews it…'. Opening Cases straight afterwards states that there is no active case.
failure_scenario: A rider reports 'I was charged twice', sees 'Sent to Movera', taps Support › Cases and reads 'No active cases'. They conclude the report was lost and send it again.
suggested_fix: Keep the disputes sent in this session (or read them from the server) and list them, or replace the empty state with copy that does not claim there are no cases.

title: Menu greeting falls back to the English literal 'Welcome to Movera' in every language
description: For a rider with no name, RiderMenuPage._profileHeader shows controller.displayName(), which returns the constant ProfileRepository.emptyDisplayName. That constant is not translated and has no ARB entry. Account home uses the translated context.l10n.accountAddYourName in the same case. A rider with no name is common: a returning rider after sign-out, or the skipped name step reported above.
failure_scenario: A Swedish rider without a saved name opens the menu and sees 'Welcome to Movera' in English above Swedish menu items.
suggested_fix: Use a localized string (e.g. L10n.current for a new key) for the empty-name greeting.

title: The profile sent to the server says language 'en' while the app speaks the zone language, until the rider picks one by hand
description: RiderProfileData.language defaults to 'en'. AppLanguageController (the language the app actually uses: the rider's choice, else the zone default, Swedish in Stockholm) never writes it into the profile. Only pickAppLanguage does. RiderNameScreen._save (and every other profile save) sends `language: 'en'` in the PATCH (FLOW-7: the server uses the language for the rider), even though the rider has been using the app in Swedish all along.
failure_scenario: A new rider in Stockholm signs up with the Swedish UI and enters their name. The server stores language 'en', so server-sent messages and receipts arrive in English.
suggested_fix: Send AppScope.instance.language.code (or keep the profile language in step with AppLanguageController) instead of the default.

title: signOutOtherDevices ignores the session counter that load() uses, so a result for a signed-out rider can be written after clearLocal
description: clearLocal says 'A load still in flight for that rider is ignored when it lands' and bumps `_session`. load() checks it, but signOutOtherDevices does not: it assigns `state = await _repository.signOutOtherDevices()` and clears `loading` unconditionally. If sign-out (UserDataWipe → accountSecurity.clearLocal) happens while this request is in flight, the previous rider's security state (phone, email, sessions) can be stored again. Account and Personal info then show it to the next rider, because they only reload when state == null.
failure_scenario: A rider taps 'Sign out other devices' on a slow network, then signs out from the menu before the request finishes. The response lands after the wipe, and the next rider to sign in opens Account and sees the previous rider's phone number and email.
suggested_fix: Capture `_session` before the await and drop the result if it has changed, as load() does.

title: On web, the moving driver car makes a new blob URL that is never revoked, plus an image load, about 20 times a second for the whole live ride
description: The car's ease now runs for almost the whole gap between fixes, because driverEaseDuration copies that gap (0.4 to 4 s). Its listener rebuilds the marker set every 50 ms (lines 1999-2013). Each set has a driver Marker at a new position (lines 2298-2308). Its icon is a BytesMapBitmap with no width or height: `BitmapDescriptor.bytes(data.buffer.asUint8List())` at lib/shared/widgets/movera_map_markers.dart:173. GoogleMap sees the driver marker as changed on every update. google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2 then runs, per update: `_changeMarker` -> `_markerOptionsFromMarker` -> `_gmIconFromBitmapDescriptor` -> `urlFromMapBitmap`, which calls `URL.createObjectURL(Blob(bytes))` (convert.dart:754-760). The URL cache is cleared after every batch (`_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches()`, google_maps_controller.dart:577), so every update gets a fresh Blob copy of the PNG. The plugin never calls revokeObjectURL for marker icons, so each Blob lives until the page unloads. With no width or height given, `_getBitmapSize` -> `_fetchBitmapSize` also creates an HTMLImageElement and waits for it to load on every update (convert.dart:404). Then `marker.options = ...` gives Google Maps a new icon URL to fetch and decode. The U7 change only kept the map leaf from rebuilding. It did not stop the per-update icon churn on the web, which is the main shipped platform. The comment in home_controller.dart:172-178 shows the team knew each repaint costs "a new blob URL and image decode on the web". It does not account for those URLs never being freed.
failure_scenario: A rider on iPhone Safari (public web demo or a real web build) follows a 30-minute trip: driver to pickup, then in trip. The mock or live feed sends a fix every 2-3 s, so the ease never stops. Worked by hand: about 20 marker updates/s x 1800 s = about 36,000 Blob URLs of the 31x31 car PNG (about 1-2 KB each), so about 36-72 MB kept in the blob store. Also about 36,000 image elements loaded, and an icon swap on every frame. Memory grows without bound and the map stutters. On a longer trip, iOS Safari kills the tab mid-ride and the page reloads. Not run (read-only audit); traced through the plugin source in ~/.pub-cache.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:1999-2012 `)..addListener(() { ... if (_driverAnim.isAnimating && last != null && now.difference(last) < const Duration(milliseconds: 50)) { return; } _lastAnimRebuild = now; _markers = _buildMarkers(); });`
waiting_for_driver.dart:2298-2307 `Marker(markerId: const MarkerId('driver'), position: driverPosition, rotation: _currentDriverHeading(), ... icon: _driverCar ?? ...)`
movera_map_markers.dart:173 `return BitmapDescriptor.bytes(data.buffer.asUint8List());`
google_maps_flutter_web convert.dart:754-760 `_bitmapBlobUrlCache.putIfAbsent(bytesMapBitmap.byteData.hashCode, () { final Blob blob = Blob(...); return URL.createObjectURL(blob as JSObject); })`
google_maps_controller.dart:577 `_cleanUpBitmapConversionCaches();`
suggested_fix: On web, give frequently moving markers an icon that does not go through a blob. One option is an AssetMapBitmap (BitmapDescriptor.asset with explicit width/height), which resolves to a stable asset URL with no Blob and no size probe. Another is to cap web driver-marker updates to once per fix (no 20 fps interpolation). At minimum, pass width/height to BitmapDescriptor.bytes to skip the per-update image probe.

title: Home puck pulse on web creates a never-revoked blob URL every 850 ms while Home is open
description: startPulse flips pulseExpanded every 850 ms and calls onTick, which is Home's _updateLocationVisuals. On web that runs _paintWebPuck (home.dart:1588-1601). It swaps the puck icon between the cached 'expanded' and 'compact' rotated BitmapDescriptors, both BitmapDescriptor.bytes (home.dart:1562). paintUserPuck sees a non-identical icon and publishes a new marker Set (home_controller.dart:702-713). google_maps_flutter_web then runs _changeMarker for the puck, and urlFromMapBitmap makes a fresh `URL.createObjectURL(Blob(png))` each time, because its cache is cleared after every batch and the URL is never revoked. Every GPS fix (a position change) does the same. RotatedPuckCache (U7) only avoids re-rasterising in Dart. Each icon swap still allocates a new Blob in the browser that lives until the page unloads. The pulse runs for as long as Home is the current route and the camera is still, which is the app's idle state.
failure_scenario: A rider leaves the web app open on Home (for example, an installed PWA on iPhone left in the foreground) with location granted. Worked by hand: 3600/0.85 = about 4,235 pulse swaps/hour plus one per GPS fix, each a new Blob of the 65x75 puck PNG (a few KB). That is about 10-20 MB/hour that is never freed, plus one Google Maps icon decode each time. Over a long session this adds to the WebGL map's memory and raises the risk of iOS Safari killing the tab. Not run; traced by reading the code and the plugin source.
evidence:
home_controller.dart:642-646 `_pulseTimer = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 850), (_) { if (!isMounted() || _livePaused || cameraMoving) return; pulseExpanded = !pulseExpanded; onTick(); });`
home.dart:1596-1601 `_locationCtl.paintUserPuck(target: target, icon: rotated ?? (...)!, heading: rotated == null ? heading : 0);`
home_controller.dart:702-713 `markers = { Marker(markerId: const MarkerId('live_user_location'), ... icon: icon, ...) }; notifyListeners();`
home_controller.dart:174-175 comment: `swaps the marker bitmap (a new blob URL and image decode on the web)`
suggested_fix: On web, draw the pulse without swapping marker bitmaps, for example with a Circle overlay whose radius alternates, or with asset-backed icons. Another option is to keep one icon and stop pulsing on web. Do not send BytesMapBitmap icon changes at timer cadence.

title: Driver car (and Finding's nearby cars) never rotate on web: Marker.rotation is ignored by google_maps_flutter_web
description: Waiting computes an interpolated heading for the car and passes it as `rotation: _currentDriverHeading()` with `flat: true`. Finding passes `rotation: vehicle.bearing` (finding_drivers.dart:433). google_maps_flutter_web 0.5.14+2 never maps rotation or flat onto the JS marker (convert.dart:516: "Flat and Rotation are not supported directly on the web."). The top-down car bitmap (MoveraVehicleMarker, headlight dot at the top) therefore always points north on the web. Home already handles this plugin gap by pre-rotating its puck bitmaps on web (home.dart:1521-1541, 1575-1583). The driver markers do not, so the heading work in _bearingDegrees and lerpHeading has no visible effect on the main web platform.
failure_scenario: On the web demo, the driver heads east along a street towards the pickup, or the trip runs west. The car icon slides sideways, still pointing north, instead of facing where it is driving. Nearby cars on Finding likewise ignore their bearing. On Android and iOS the same code rotates correctly. Not run; read from the plugin source.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:2298-2304 `Marker(markerId: const MarkerId('driver'), position: driverPosition, rotation: _currentDriverHeading(), flat: true, ...)`
finding_drivers.dart:433 `rotation: vehicle.bearing,`
google_maps_flutter_web convert.dart:516 `// Flat and Rotation are not supported directly on the web.`
home.dart:1576-1577 `// The web bitmap is turned on screen, not on the ground: take the map's own bearing off`
suggested_fix: Reuse Home's approach for the car on web: a small cache of pre-rotated car bitmaps per heading bucket, with heading minus the map bearing. Give those icons explicit width/height or asset URLs so the blob leak above is not made worse.

title: Confirm pickup spot redraws a Flutter overlay above the map on every camera-move frame during a pinch, the pattern Set pickup removed after it crashed iPhone Safari
description: onCameraMove writes `_zoom.value = position.zoom` on every camera frame. During a pinch or wheel zoom (fractional zoom is on through rider_map_camera.js), the value changes every frame. The ValueListenableBuilder (line 354) then rebuilds and repaints the semi-transparent accuracy ring, sized from the zoom, that sits over the platform map. Set pickup documents that this exact pattern, a Flutter animation over a moving web map, "re-renders every canvas on each frame, and iPhone Safari ran out of graphics memory doing that and reloaded" (set_pickup_page.dart:466-471). That page was changed so nothing animates while the map slides. Confirm pickup spot, reached from Home's pickup prefill and from route change's 'pick on map', still does it.
failure_scenario: On iPhone Safari a rider opens Confirm pickup spot (or Confirm destination from Change route) and pinch-zooms the map. Every frame of the pinch repaints the overlay ring above the moving map, so Flutter's overlay canvas is re-rendered over the WebGL map each frame. This is the GPU-memory pressure the codebase blames for a Safari reload on Set pickup, so a reload or heavy jank is possible on lower-memory iPhones. Not run; based on the code and the in-repo incident note.
evidence:
confirm_pickup_spot.dart:339-344 `onCameraMove: (position) { _moving = true; _center = position.target; // D-011: the radius overlay follows zoom live ... _zoom.value = position.zoom; },`
confirm_pickup_spot.dart:354-363 `child: ValueListenableBuilder<double>(valueListenable: _zoom, builder: (context, zoom, _) { final radius = ConfirmPickupSpot.metersToPixels(...); return Container(key: const ValueKey('pickup-accuracy-overlay'), ...`
set_pickup_page.dart:468-471 `// ... the lift never runs while the map itself is sliding: animating over a moving map re-renders every canvas on each frame, and iPhone Safari ran out of graphics memory doing that and reloaded.`
suggested_fix: On web, update the ring only on onCameraIdle, or hide it while the camera moves. Another option is to draw it as a google_maps Circle, which the map renders itself.

title: Road-route cache is unbounded and gets a new entry every 10 s of a live ride (driver position is part of the key)
description: roadLine stores every resolved road geometry in a per-RoutingService map that is never evicted (`cache[key] = points`). The key is built from the endpoints at 5 decimals. AppScope holds one RoutingService for the app's lifetime (di.dart:191-192). Waiting's paintIfDue calls _refreshRoadRoute at most every 10 s (waiting_for_driver.dart:2097-2102). Its endpoints are the driver's live position and the pickup or destination (lines 2328-2357), so each refresh while the driver moves is a new key and a new cached polyline. Nothing ever reads these stale driver-origin entries again. With a real route provider each entry can hold hundreds of points, so memory grows with every ride in a session.
failure_scenario: With the real /api/v1/routes backend, which returns road polylines, a rider takes several rides in one long web or PWA session. A 30-minute trip adds about 180 entries of a few hundred GeoPoints each, never freed. Memory grows by MBs per ride and adds to the web map's footprint. The in-process mock returns 2-point lines, so the demo grows slowly, but the pattern is the same. Not run; traced by reading the code.
evidence:
routing_service.dart:41-44 `final cache = _roadCaches[this] ??= <String, List<GeoPoint>>{}; final key = _roadCacheKey(from, to); final cached = cache[key];`
routing_service.dart:77 `cache[key] = points;`
waiting_for_driver.dart:2097-2101 `if (_mapReady && (_lastRouteRefresh == null || now.difference(_lastRouteRefresh!) >= const Duration(seconds: 10))) { unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute()); }`
suggested_fix: Bound the cache: an LRU of a few dozen entries. Another option is to skip caching for requests whose origin is a live driver position.

title: Ride check buttons (Call 112, I'm OK, Done, answer rows, options, Record) have no semantic tap action because excludeSemantics also drops the InkWell's action
description: _BigButton, _Call112Now, _RecordAudio, _RowTile and _OptionButton all wrap their InkWell in `Semantics(button: true, label: ..., excludeSemantics: true, child: Material(child: InkWell(onTap: onTap ...)))` and never pass `onTap` to the Semantics. In Flutter, `excludeSemantics` makes RenderSemanticsAnnotations skip visitChildrenForSemantics (rendering/object.dart:4931), so the descendant InkWell's RenderSemanticsGestureHandler never contributes its tap action. The resulting node is a labelled 'button' with no SemanticsAction.tap. The codebase's own pattern elsewhere (safety_ui.dart:161-170, side_menu.dart:709-713) forwards `onTap:` to the Semantics for exactly this reason, and safety_test.dart:111 asserts hasAction(tap) for Safety hub rows; nothing tests the Ride check card this way. RideCheckLayer makes the card modal (non-dismissible ModalBarrier, PopScope canPop: !answering), so a screen-reader user who cannot activate these nodes cannot answer, call 112 or close it.
failure_scenario: Android TalkBack user (native or Flutter web semantics) is in a trip, a Ride check (long stop / possible crash) opens. Focus lands on 'Call 112' / 'I'm OK'. Double-tap sends ACTION_CLICK, but the node has no tap action, so nothing happens. The card blocks the screen (barrier not dismissible, back blocked), so the rider is stuck on a safety prompt. VoiceOver on native iOS may still work through its simulated-touch fallback.
evidence:
ride_check_card.dart:794-803 `return Semantics(
      button: true,
      label: label,
      excludeSemantics: true,
      child: Material(... child: InkWell(
          onTap: onTap,` ; same at :840-848 (_Call112Now, label rcCall112NowSemantics), :1011-1021 (_RecordAudio), :1089-1095 (_RowTile), :1159-1167 (_OptionButton). Contrast safety_ui.dart:161-170 `Semantics(button: onTap != null, label: ..., onTap: onTap, child: ExcludeSemantics(child: InkWell(onTap: onTap,`
suggested_fix: Pass `onTap: onTap` (and `enabled`) to each of these Semantics widgets, as safety_ui.dart and side_menu.dart already do, and add a test that asserts SemanticsAction.tap on the Ride check buttons.

title: Sign-in primary and Apple/Google buttons expose no semantic tap action (excludeSemantics hides the InkWell)
description: AuthPrimaryButton (Continue / Send code / Verify / Let's ride) and AuthProviderButton (Continue with Apple / Google) are `Semantics(button: true, enabled: ..., label: ..., excludeSemantics: true, child: ... InkWell(onTap: ...))` with no `onTap` on the Semantics. excludeSemantics stops the framework from visiting the InkWell's gesture semantics, so the button nodes have a label and the button flag but no tap action. The auth tests only use pointer taps on `find.bySemanticsLabel(...)` (phase73_auth_ui_test.dart:267, phone_verification_copy_test.dart:145), so they pass whether or not the node is actionable.
failure_scenario: A TalkBack user opens Sign in, focuses 'Continue with Google' or, after typing the number, 'Send code', and double-taps. No tap action is dispatched and nothing happens, so the user cannot sign in. The same happens for 'Verify' on the OTP step.
evidence:
auth_controls.dart:26-31 `return Semantics(
      button: true,
      enabled: enabled,
      label: label,
      excludeSemantics: true,
      child: SizedBox(` ... :56-58 `child: InkWell(
              borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(16),
              onTap: enabled ? onPressed : null,` ; :116-121 same pattern for AuthProviderButton with `onTap: busy ? null : onPressed` at :131
suggested_fix: Add `onTap: enabled ? onPressed : null` to both Semantics widgets (or drop excludeSemantics and use ExcludeSemantics only around the visual children) and test with `tester.semantics`/hasAction(SemanticsAction.tap).

title: Save Home/Work address sheet adds the keyboard inset a second time, overflows, and its buttons stop taking taps once the keyboard opens
description: MoveraSheet.show already wraps every builder in `Padding(bottom: MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(ctx).bottom)` (movera_sheet.dart:36-41). MoveraModalSheetRoute uses `SheetViewport(child: child)` with zero padding, and smooth_sheets 1.2 does not consume viewInsets (viewport.dart:225-240 asks the caller to pad), so the builder still sees the full keyboard inset. _showAddressPicker pads by `MediaQuery.of(context).viewInsets.bottom` again, so the content area shrinks by twice the keyboard height. The TextField has autofocus, so this happens as soon as the sheet opens.
failure_scenario: Native iPhone 390x844 with a 336 px keyboard: sheet content max = 844 - 2*336 = 172, minus the Container's ~32 px padding leaves 140 px. The fixed content (handle, title row with close button 48, field ~50, 'Use current location' row ~56, spacers) needs about 197 px. Typing a query adds 'Use this address' (+62). The Column overflows by 57-119 px. The parts outside the Column are painted but not hit-tested (RenderBox.hitTest checks size), so 'Use current location' and 'Use this address' cannot be tapped. The sheet is pushed up to y=0 under the status bar, with a transparent keyboard-height band below it. On a 360x640 Android phone (Android Chrome web reports the keyboard as viewInsets too), only about 9 px is left.
evidence:
movera_sheet.dart:36-41 `final keyboardInset = MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(ctx).bottom; ... child: Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.only(bottom: keyboardInset),` ; home.dart:1098-1101 `return Padding(
                    padding: EdgeInsets.only(
                      bottom: MediaQuery.of(context).viewInsets.bottom,
                    ),` ; home.dart:1152 `autofocus: true,`
suggested_fix: Remove the inner viewInsets Padding (MoveraSheet already applies it), and make the sheet body scrollable.

title: Receipt dispute sheet double-pads for the keyboard, so Submit is out of reach while the rider types
description: _openDispute's builder pads its non-scrolling Column with `20 + MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom`, on top of MoveraSheet.show's own keyboard Padding. The multiline field (minLines 2, maxLines 4) uses a newline return key, so on iOS the keyboard cannot be dismissed from the keyboard. Flutter does not unfocus on a touch tap outside the field on mobile. A tap on the transparent band falls through to the barrier and closes the sheet, losing the text.
failure_scenario: Native iPhone 390x844, keyboard 336 px: the Column gets 844 - 336 - 336 - 40 = 132 px but needs about 213 px (title 25, body ~40, field ~72, spacers, button 40). The FilledButton 'Submit issue' starts at about 173 px, outside the Column, so it is not hit-testable. The rider types the issue and cannot submit it. Tapping above the sheet dismisses it and the typed text is lost.
evidence:
trip_detail.dart:145-151 `return Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(
              20,
              20,
              20,
              20 + MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(context).bottom,
            ),
            child: Column(` ; :163-166 `minLines: 2,
                  maxLines: 4,` ; movera_sheet.dart:36-41 already pads by the keyboard inset
suggested_fix: Drop the viewInsets term (keep the 20), and wrap the Column in a SingleChildScrollView.

title: Pickup address search sheet floats a full keyboard height above the keyboard and overflows on short phones
description: _searchAddress pads the sheet body with `MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(sheetContext).bottom` even though MoveraSheet.show already does, and the TextField autofocuses. The sheet is lifted by twice the keyboard height. The area between the sheet and the keyboard is transparent (it is part of the sheet, so a tap there falls through to the barrier and dismisses it).
failure_scenario: 360x640 Android (native, or Chrome where Flutter web reports the keyboard in viewInsets), keyboard about 280 px: the Container gets 640 - 560 = 80 px for 141 px of content (padding 42, title ~25, 12, field ~56). The field overflows the Column, and the part below 80 px is outside the hit area. On 390x844 iOS the sheet fits but hangs in mid-screen with a 336 px see-through gap above the keyboard.
evidence:
set_pickup_page.dart:658-664 `final query = await MoveraSheet.show<String>(
      context: context,
      builder: (sheetContext) => PointerInterceptor(
        child: Padding(
          padding: EdgeInsets.only(
            bottom: MediaQuery.viewInsetsOf(sheetContext).bottom,
          ),` ; :679 `autofocus: true,`
suggested_fix: Remove the extra viewInsets Padding.

title: Emergency contact editor shrinks by twice the keyboard height and leaves a 40-140 px strip to edit in
description: _ContactEditor (opened via MoveraSheet.show at :42) pads by `20 + MediaQuery.of(context).viewInsets.bottom`, and MoveraSheet already pads by the keyboard inset. The SingleChildScrollView keeps it from overflowing, but its viewport is the screen height minus 2x keyboard minus 36.
failure_scenario: Rider adds a trusted contact on a 360x640 phone with a ~280 px keyboard: the scrollable form viewport is 640 - 560 - 36 = 44 px, floating 280 px above the keyboard. Name, phone, relationship, share-trips switch and Save show through a 44 px slit. On 390x844 iOS it is about 136 px.
suggested_fix: Use only the fixed 20 px bottom padding, since MoveraSheet applies the keyboard inset.

title: Schedule Continue button: hard-coded English screen-reader label, no semantic tap action, and a test that cannot detect either
description: The Continue CTA on the date/time step is wrapped as `Semantics(container: true, label: 'Schedule Continue', button: true, enabled: enabled, child: ExcludeSemantics(child: ElevatedButton(onPressed: ...)))`. The literal label replaces the localized visible text (continueLabel = 'Continuer'/'Fortsätt', or 'Continuing…' while busy). ExcludeSemantics removes the ElevatedButton's tap action, and the outer Semantics has no onTap, so the node cannot be activated by assistive tech. test/scheduled_rides/phase81_schedule_continue_test.dart is titled 'Schedule Continue is accessible' but only does `tester.tap(find.bySemanticsLabel('Schedule Continue'))`, a pointer tap, so it passes either way.
failure_scenario: A Swedish TalkBack user on Book for later hears 'Schedule Continue' in English, hears no 'Continuing…' busy state, and double-tapping does nothing because the node has no tap action. They cannot leave the date/time step.
evidence:
select_date_time.dart:789-797 `child: Semantics(
                container: true,
                label: 'Schedule Continue',
                button: true,
                enabled: enabled,
                child: ExcludeSemantics(
                  child: ElevatedButton(
                    onPressed: enabled ? _goNext : null,` ; test phase81_schedule_continue_test.dart:35,53 `find.bySemanticsLabel('Schedule Continue')` + `tester.tap(...)`
suggested_fix: Drop the wrapper (the ElevatedButton already has correct semantics), or use a localized label plus `onTap: enabled ? _goNext : null`. Make the test assert SemanticsAction.tap.

title: Driver rating stars have no labels and no value for screen readers
description: RideCompletedGiveReview uses flutter_rating_bar 4.0.1's RatingBar.builder with plain `Icon(Icons.star_rounded)` items (no semanticLabel) and no Semantics wrapper. RatingBar builds a GestureDetector per star with onTapDown/drag only. Each star becomes an unlabeled actionable node: Flutter turns the TapGestureRecognizer into a semantic tap (gesture_detector.dart:1721), but nothing says which star it is, and the current rating is never exposed (no value, increase or decrease actions).
failure_scenario: On the ride summary a VoiceOver or TalkBack user swipes to the rating area and hears five unnamed 'button's (or nothing useful), with no '3 of 5 stars' state. They cannot tell what they are rating or what they already chose, on the main post-trip feedback path.
evidence:
give_review.dart:48-69 `child: RatingBar.builder(
            initialRating: _rating, ... itemBuilder: (context, _) =>
                Icon(Icons.star_rounded, color: Color(0xffF99417)),
            onRatingUpdate: (rating) {` ; flutter_rating_bar-4.0.1 rating_bar.dart:294-295 `child: GestureDetector(
        onTapDown: (details) {` (no Semantics anywhere in the package)
suggested_fix: Wrap the bar in a Semantics slider (label 'Rate your driver', value '$n of 5', onIncrease/onDecrease), or label each star item ('1 star' … '5 stars', selected).

title: Expanded Set pickup sheet is height-capped at 72% with NeverScrollableScrollPhysics, so Confirm and the payment line get clipped and cannot be scrolled to
description: The sheet Container is capped at `media.size.height * 0.72` and its content sits in a SingleChildScrollView with NeverScrollableScrollPhysics, which clips anything taller. When the rider opens the sheet (handle tap or drag), _reveal adds the ride header, bags row, price box (extra rows for a promotion and wallet split) and payment line above the Confirm button. The matrix tests at 320x568/2x only check for exceptions, and clipping throws none.
failure_scenario: iPhone SE 375x667, 1x: cap 480, minus 26 padding = 454 available. The open sheet needs about 475 (handle 16, header 59, spot row 30, card 68, chips 49, bags 49, price 60, payment 58, Confirm 56, gaps). The bottom of Confirm is clipped. With an active promotion (+~69) Confirm and part of the payment 'Change' line disappear. With promotion and wallet on 390x844 (cap ~547) Confirm is hidden too. The same happens at 1.3x text. The rider sees Confirm vanish when expanding and cannot reach Change payment.
evidence:
set_pickup_page.dart:966 `constraints: BoxConstraints(maxHeight: media.size.height * 0.72),` ; :979-980 `child: SingleChildScrollView(
                physics: const NeverScrollableScrollPhysics(),` ; :1018-1022 `_reveal(0.25, 0.85, _bagsRow()),
                    _reveal(0.35, 0.95, _priceBox()),
                    _reveal(0.45, 1.0, _paymentLine()),
                    const SizedBox(height: 14),
                    _confirmButton(),`
suggested_fix: Keep Confirm outside the clipped area (a pinned footer), or allow scrolling once content exceeds the cap (the drag gesture can still move the sheet when the scroll is at the top).

title: Icon-only close/back buttons in the Book-for-later flow have no accessible name (and are 42 px)
description: Several icon-only navigation buttons are a bare InkWell around an Icon with no tooltip, semanticLabel or Semantics label. Screen readers announce an unlabeled button. Two of them are also 42x42, below the app's own 44 px floor (A11y.minTapIOS, 'the floor for every tap target').
failure_scenario: After booking a scheduled ride, a VoiceOver/TalkBack user on RideScheduledPage hears 'button' with no name for the only exit control. The same happens on the date/time step's back button and the address step's back button, so the scheduling flow cannot be navigated by name.
evidence:
ride_scheduled.dart:128-139 `child: InkWell(
                  onTap: _goBack,
                  customBorder: const CircleBorder(),
                  child: const SizedBox(
                    width: 42,
                    height: 42,
                    child: Icon(
                      Icons.close_rounded,` ; select_date_time.dart:566-573 `child: InkWell(
            onTap: widget.onBack ?? () => Navigator.maybePop(context), ... child: const SizedBox(
              width: 42,
              height: 42,
              child: Icon(Icons.arrow_back_rounded,` ; schedule_ride.dart:289-299 `child: InkWell(
                            onTap: goToPreviousStep, ... child: const SizedBox(
                              width: 44,
                              height: 44,
                              child: Icon(
                                Icons.arrow_back_rounded,`
suggested_fix: Use MoveraIconButton (tooltip + 48 px) or wrap in Semantics(button: true, label: l10n.close/back).

title: Saved-place location picker close button is a 26 px unlabeled InkWell
description: RiderSearchPickupLocation (opened from Add place → location field, add_place.dart:62-70) closes through an InkWell wrapping a `ResSize.h * 26` x `ResSize.w * 26` circle with an Icon and no label. That is a 22-32 px target, far below the 44 px floor, and screen readers get no name.
failure_scenario: On a 320x568 phone the close hit area is about 22x22 px. A TalkBack user hears an unnamed button as the first control. Sighted users on small phones miss it often.
suggested_fix: Wrap it in MoveraHitArea(label: l10n.close, ...) like add_place.dart:171 does for its back button.

title: Home reservation chrono's countdown Column overflows its 54 px disc in French and at larger text sizes
description: The chrono is a fixed 54x54 box. Inside Padding(8,7,8,6) the Column gets 38x41 px and holds an 11 px car image, 1 px, and the countdown Text(s) with no maxLines. French strings are longer: 'Maintenant' (now) and '{m} min' (durMinutes) at 13 px w700 are wider than 38 px and wrap. 'Maintenant' is one word, so it breaks per character onto about 3 lines. The badge Stack uses Clip.none, so overflowing text paints outside the circle over the map.
failure_scenario: French rider with a reservation, in its last minute: primary 'Maintenant' wraps to about 3 lines * 13 = 39 px, plus 12 = 51 > 41 → RenderFlex overflow (about 10 px), text spills past the disc. At 1.3x text, sv/fr '45 min' (2 lines of 16.9 px) gives 46 > 41. At 2x in English, '2h'/'45m' gives 11+1+26+19.8 = 58 > 41. The matrix tests render Home without reservations, so the chrono is never laid out there.
evidence:
home_reservation_chrono.dart:258-260 `child: SizedBox(
                width: 54,
                height: 54,` ; :281-313 `padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(8, 7, 8, 6),
                            child: Column(... Image.asset(AppAssets.scheduleRideCar, height: 11 ...), ... Text(
                                    parts.primary,
                                    style: GoogleFonts.poppins(
                                      fontSize: parts.secondary == null
                                          ? 13
                                          : 11,` ; app_fr.arb `"now": "Maintenant"`, `"durMinutes": "{minutes} min"`
suggested_fix: Wrap the countdown in FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown) with maxLines: 1, or use a short 'now' form for the chrono.

title: Share-trip button on Waiting and in-trip panels is a 40x40 target, below the 44 px floor
description: WaitingShareButton is `Padding(EdgeInsets.all(10), child: Icon(size: 20))` inside a circular InkWell, so the hit area is 40x40. A11y.minTapIOS documents 44 as 'the floor for every tap target', and MoveraIconButton uses 48. This button is in the pickup header (_fixedPickupHeader) and the in-trip panel header, a main safety action.
failure_scenario: A rider in a moving car tries to share the trip from the in-trip panel and misses the 40 px circle. The tap lands on the sheet or the headline instead.
evidence:
waiting_sheet_bits.dart:81-91 `child: InkWell(
          customBorder: const CircleBorder(),
          onTap: () => _share(context),
          child: const Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.all(10),
            child: Icon(
              Icons.ios_share_rounded,
              size: 20,`
suggested_fix: Constrain to A11y.minTap (48) or wrap in MoveraHitArea.

title: Driver card 'Message' button Row has no flex: overflows into the call chip in Swedish or at large text
description: The Message control sits in an Expanded next to two 44 px icon chips. Inside it a centred Row holds Icon(18) + 8 + Text(message) + optional unread badge, and no child is Flexible. Swedish 'Meddelande' is about 6.0em at 14 px w600. Row overflow paints past the Material (Clip.none) over the phone chip.
failure_scenario: 360 px phone, Waiting or in-trip, driver assigned. The Expanded gets 360-40-28-104 = 188 px. In Swedish at 2x text the Row needs 18+8+~169 = 195 px (+~33 with an unread badge), so a RenderFlex overflow pushes the text under the call button. At 320 px even English at 2x overflows once a message arrives (~147 + 33 > 148). The 200% tests pump WaitingForDriver without a driver, so this card is never laid out.
evidence:
waiting_sheet_bits.dart:396-409 `child: Row(
                        mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.center,
                        children: [
                          const Icon(
                            Icons.chat_bubble_outline_rounded,
                            size: 18, ... Text(
                            context.l10n.message,
                            style: waitingText(14, weight: FontWeight.w600),
                          ),
                          if (unreadMessages > 0) ...[` ; app_sv.arb `"message": "Meddelande"`
suggested_fix: Wrap the Text in Flexible with maxLines: 1 and ellipsis.

title: In-trip status pill ('NÄRA DESTINATIONEN' / 'NEAR DESTINATION') is an unflexed Row and overflows at large text
description: The pill is `Container(padding 10/6) > Row(mainAxisSize.min, [Icon 14, 6, Text(UPPERCASE, 11px w700, letterSpacing 0.7)])` in a Column inside an Expanded that also has to leave room for the share button. The Text has no Flexible, maxLines or FittedBox.
failure_scenario: 320 px phone, trip approaching dropoff, 2x text: about 190 px is available for the text, while 'NEAR DESTINATION' needs ~224 px and Swedish 'NÄRA DESTINATIONEN' ~257 px. RenderFlex overflow, and the pill text runs past the pill. The Swedish label also overflows at 360 px. The in-trip state is not rendered by the text-scale tests.
evidence:
rider_in_trip_panel.dart:76-92 `child: Row(
                        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
                        children: [
                          const Icon(
                            Icons.navigation_rounded,
                            size: 14, ... Text(
                            approaching ? context.l10n.nearDestinationUpper : context.l10n.onTripUpper,
                            style: waitingText(
                              11,` ; app_sv.arb `"nearDestinationUpper": "NÄRA DESTINATIONEN"`
suggested_fix: Make the Text Flexible with maxLines: 1 and ellipsis (or use FittedBox.scaleDown).

title: Select ride filter chips and ride tiles show selection only visually: no button/selected semantics; filter chips are ~34 px tall
description: _filterChip is a GestureDetector > AnimatedContainer(padding 14/8) > Row(icon, Text 13). It is about 34 px tall and has no Semantics(button/selected), so the active filter (Recommended/Faster/Cheaper) is never announced. _rideTile marks the chosen category only with an accent border. Its InkWell has no Semantics(selected:), so a screen-reader user cannot tell which category will be booked. The Book CTA text includes it, but the list does not. The same visual-only pattern is in select_date_time.dart _modeOption (Pickup at / Arrive by) and the wallet top-up amount chips (wallet.dart:390-400).
failure_scenario: A VoiceOver user on Select ride swipes through Economy/Comfort/Premium and hears names and prices with no 'selected' state. They tap Faster and get no confirmation of which filter is active.
evidence:
select_ride.dart:2108-2113 `return GestureDetector(
      onTap: onTap,
      child: AnimatedContainer(
        duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 200),
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 14, vertical: 8),` ; :2181-2190 `child: InkWell(
          onTap: () => _selectRide(ride.id), ... border: Border.all(
                color: selected ? _accent : Colors.transparent,`
suggested_fix: Wrap chips and tiles in Semantics(button: true, selected: selected, ...) and give the chips a minimum height of 44.

title: Safety Kit and other non-scrolling sheets run past the screen at 200% text, cutting off their bottom actions
description: MoveraSheet content is laid out against the full viewport and these builders return a plain Column with no scroll view: RideSafetyKitSheet, CancelRideSheet (cancel_ride_sheet.dart:177), showCancelReservationFlow (reservation_edit_sheets.dart:24) and the History detail sheet (ride_history.dart:485). Their texts have no maxLines, so at large text they grow past the viewport and the bottom children are clipped and untappable. None of these sheets are covered by the text-scale tests.
failure_scenario: French, 2x text, 375x667. Open the Safety Kit during a trip and tap 'Enregistrer l'audio': the title takes 2 lines (123), the 3 tool tiles ~183 (their labels break mid-word in the ~90 px tiles), the recording note ~214 and the Safety preferences card ~207, about 870 px in total. RenderFlex overflow of ~200 px, and the 'Préférences de sécurité' link and part of the note are off-screen. On 360x640, the 'Taking longer' cancel sheet (148-char body ≈ 7-8 lines) also needs about 660 px, so 'Attendre un chauffeur' is clipped.
evidence:
ride_safety_kit.dart:250-255 `child: Padding(
        padding: EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(20, 8, 20, 20 + inset),
        child: Column(
          mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,` (no scroll view) ; :305-308 `if (_audioNote != null) ...[ ... Text(_audioNote!, style: _text(12, color: _muted)),` ; cancel_ride_sheet.dart:175-181 `return Padding(... child: Column(
        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,`
suggested_fix: Wrap these sheet bodies in SingleChildScrollView (as cancel_reason_sheet.dart and emergency contact editor already do).

title: Price-bump state raises the Finding sheet to a fixed 520 px and covers the Cancel and Safety buttons on short viewports
description: _minSheet is a constant 520 (+bottom padding) while the price-bump card shows, and _maxSheet is forced to at least minH+48 = 568. The top Cancel (X) and Safety Kit buttons sit at padding.top+8 and are drawn before the SheetViewport in the Stack, so the sheet paints over them when the viewport is shorter than about 576 px.
failure_scenario: iPhone SE in Safari (viewport ~375x548, padding.top 0): when the raise-your-offer card appears, the sheet top sits at y=28. The X button (y 8-56) and Safety Kit button are mostly covered and take taps only in their top 20 px. Dragging to the max stop (568 > 548) pushes the sheet's handle above the screen.
suggested_fix: Clamp the sheet stops to media.size.height - media.padding.top - 64 (below the top bar) and let the panel scroll.

title: Add/Edit place form is a non-scrolling Column with a Spacer; with the keyboard up it overflows once the error line shows
description: The Scaffold body is Padding > Column(16, name TextField, 16, location field, error, Spacer, Save 52, 16) with no scroll view, and the Scaffold resizes for the keyboard. When Save is tapped with a field empty, the error text appears while the keyboard is still up.
failure_scenario: 320x568 phone, keyboard ~260: the body is 568-20-56-260 = 232 px. The content needs ~216 px, then 245 px with the 'name and location' error, so RenderFlex overflow and the Save button is pushed under the keyboard. At 1.3x text it overflows even without the error.
evidence:
add_place.dart:214-218 `body: Padding(
        padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: screenHorizPadding),
        child: Column(` ; :258-269 `if (_error != null) ...[ ... ],
            const Spacer(),`
suggested_fix: Use a scrollable body (ListView or SingleChildScrollView with the button in bottomNavigationBar).

title: Choice sheets (language, gender) mark the current option only with a check icon; ListTile.selected is not set
description: showAccountChoice renders each option as a ListTile whose only selected indicator is `trailing: Icon(Icons.check_rounded)` with no semanticLabel. ListTile(selected:) is not set, so no selected flag reaches the semantics tree. It is used by the language picker (language_picker.dart:18) and the gender picker.
failure_scenario: A screen-reader user opens Language and hears 'English', 'Français', 'Svenska' with no indication of which is active.
evidence:
account_widgets.dart:409-418 `for (final option in options)
              ListTile(
                title: Text(
                  labelOf?.call(option) ?? option, ...),
                trailing: option == selected
                    ? const Icon(Icons.check_rounded, color: kAccountAccent)
                    : null,`
suggested_fix: Pass `selected: option == selected` to ListTile (or wrap in Semantics(selected: ...)).

title: Unread notifications are marked only by an 8 px dot with no semantics
description: _buildNotificationCard shows unread state solely as an 8 px primary-colour circle Container. The card's GestureDetector/Text semantics carry no unread flag or label, so screen-reader users cannot tell new notifications from read ones.
failure_scenario: A TalkBack user opens Notifications after a driver update and hears every card the same way, with nothing to tell which notifications are new.
evidence:
notifications.dart:195-205 `if (!notification.read) ...[
                4.width,
                Container(
                  width: ResSize.w * 8,
                  height: ResSize.w * 8,
                  decoration: BoxDecoration(
                    color: AppColor.primary,
                    shape: BoxShape.circle,`
suggested_fix: Add a localized 'Unread' semantics label (or Semantics(label:) on the card) when !notification.read.

title: Reservation completion screen shows the previous Book-now ride's driver, receipt and tip currency (LastCompletedRide is never cleared after a normal close)
description: The completion screen does not read its driver, receipt or tip currency from the ride it is showing. It reads them from the process-wide static `LastCompletedRide`, which only ActiveRideController writes, for on-demand rides. On the normal Done path (`closeCompletedRide`) the static is never cleared. Only `leaveEndedEarlySummary` and the sign-out wipe clear it. A scheduled ride completes through `ReservationLiveRide.pageFor` -> `onCompleted`, which pushes `RideCompleted(rideId: reservationId, persistOnDemandState: false)`. That path never calls `markCompleted`, so `LastCompletedRide` still holds the last Book-now ride. `RideCompletedDriverInfo` calls `AppScope.instance.rideComplete.driver()`, which reads `DriverRepository.current()`, which reads `LastCompletedRide.value`. `RideCompletedTripDetail` calls `receipt()`, which reads `TripReceiptRepository.last()`, which reads `LastCompletedRide.value`. `RideCompleteController._tripCurrency` and `initialTips()`/`tips()` also come from `LastCompletedRide.value`. None of them check the ride id against `widget.rideId`. The same stale copy shows for an on-demand completion whenever `markCompleted` returns early because `historyCandidate()` is null (active_ride_controller.dart:372).
failure_scenario: In one app session the rider completes a Book-now ride in EUR (driver 'Anna', Gamla stan -> Arlanda, 24 EUR) and taps Done. Later a scheduled reservation in SEK (driver 'Erik', Solna -> KTH, 320 kr) completes on the live screen. The 'Ride summary' then shows Anna's photo, car and plate, the receipt 'Gamla stan -> Arlanda, 24 EUR', and tip chips in EUR. If the rider picks a tip, `submitFeedback` sends it for the reservation id with `tipCurrency: EUR`. Verified by reading the code; nothing was run.
evidence:
lib/features/ride_complete/data/last_completed_ride.dart:13-17 `static RideSnapshot? _snapshot; ...` (cleared only at :44)
lib/features/active_ride/application/active_ride_controller.dart:448-462 `closeCompletedRide` ... `await _store.clear();` (no LastCompletedRide.clear)
lib/features/active_ride/application/active_ride_controller.dart:105-108 only `leaveEndedEarlySummary` clears it
lib/features/reservations/presentation/reservation_live_ride.dart:102-110 `RideCompleted(status: status, rideId: ride.reservationId, ..., persistOnDemandState: false, ...)`
lib/features/ride_complete/presentation/driver_info.dart:28 `final driver = AppScope.instance.rideComplete.driver();`
lib/features/ride_complete/presentation/trip_detail.dart:26 `final trip = (controller ?? AppScope.instance.rideComplete).receipt();`
lib/features/ride_booking/data/driver_repository.dart:40 and :106 `final ride = LastCompletedRide.value;`
lib/features/ride_complete/application/ride_complete_controller.dart:57-58 `String get _tripCurrency => LastCompletedRide.value?.currency ?? Money.defaultCurrency;`
suggested_fix: Clear LastCompletedRide in closeCompletedRide/markClosed. Also have DriverRepository.current/TripReceiptRepository.last/_tripCurrency return null unless `LastCompletedRide.value?.rideId` equals the screen's rideId. The reservation completion path should build its own driver and receipt from the Reservation.

title: Re-dispatch after a driver drop restores the offer ceiling from the booking-time RideSession copy, discarding the ceiling a route change set
description: The offer ceiling (ARCH-20) exists in two places: `RideSnapshot.maxOfferMinor` (in the store and in Finding's `_snapshot`) and `RideSession.bookedMaxOfferMinor`. Only booking and restore write `bookedMaxOfferMinor`. A route change sets a new ceiling: the mock server recomputes it, and `RouteChangeController.apply` saves `maxOfferMinor: serverMax` into the stored snapshot. The session copy is left at the booking value. When the driver drops the ride on Waiting, Waiting pops to Finding. `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` adopts the stored route and price, then calls `_startMatching` -> `startFrom`. `startFrom` builds a new snapshot whose ceiling is `session.bookedMaxOfferMinor`, the stale booking-time value. `maxOfferPrice` and `confirmPriceIncreaseBy` then use the wrong ceiling. `_evaluatePhase` and `_persistAssigned` later write it back over the store's correct value, so even a reload keeps it.
failure_scenario: Booked at 200 kr, so the server and client ceiling is 1.8 x 200 = 360 kr (36000 öre). On Waiting the rider changes the destination and the price becomes 300 kr. The server ceiling becomes 540 kr and the stored snapshot gets 54000. The driver then cancels. Finding resumes at 300 kr with maxOfferMinor 36000, so maxOfferPrice is 360. Raising by 100 kr (to 400 kr) returns false client-side, although the server allows up to 540. In the opposite case (route lowered to 100 kr, server ceiling 180 kr), the client still allows +150 kr (250 kr). The server refuses with 409 offer_above_maximum and the rider sees 'couldn't update offer'. About 90 s later the delayed-search save overwrites the stored 54000 with 36000. Worked by hand from the code; not run.
evidence:
lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:275-277 `categoryId: rideId == null ? null : session.bookedCategoryId, ... maxOfferMinor: rideId == null ? null : session.bookedMaxOfferMinor,`
lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:213-216 `final minor = _snapshot?.maxOfferMinor; if (minor != null) return Money(minor, currency).major;`
lib/features/finding_driver/presentation/finding_drivers.dart:297-312 `final current = await _match.storedRide(); ... _startMatching(price: effectivePrice, searchStartedAt: DateTime.now());`
lib/features/active_ride/application/route_change_controller.dart:289-296 `maxOfferMinor: serverMax is num && serverMax > 0 ? serverMax.round() : ... ; await RideSnapshotStore.save(updated);` (session not updated)
lib/core/api/in_process_mock_client.dart:894 `ride['maxOfferMinor'] = _maxOfferMinorFor(newMinor, rideCurrency);`
lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:586-593 delayed save of `_ordered(snapshot)` overwrites the store
suggested_fix: Make the snapshot the only owner of the ceiling. In _resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel, pass the stored snapshot's maxOfferMinor (and categoryId/paymentMethodId) into startFrom. Alternatively, have RouteChangeController.apply (it already has the session) update `bookedMaxOfferMinor` too.

title: Scheduled ride's live screen takes the waiting-fee terms and cancel-fee preview from the on-demand RideSession's last booked category
description: WaitingForDriver is reused for scheduled rides. Its widget comment says it runs 'without touching the on-demand ride session'. Two places still take the category from `AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId`, falling back to the on-demand `RideSnapshotStore` snapshot without checking its ride id: `_loadWaitingTerms` (waiting-fee counter) and `_cancelFeeNote` (the 'Cancelling now costs …' line). For a reservation, `widget.rideId` is the reservation id. The session's booked category belongs to whatever Book-now ride ran last in this process. It is never cleared: `RideSession.reset()` leaves `bookedCategoryId`/`bookedPaymentMethodId`/`bookedMaxOfferMinor` untouched, so it can even be the previous rider's after a sign-out. The reservation's own `categoryId` is never consulted. With no Book-now ride in this process, the note and counter silently disappear.
failure_scenario: Earlier in the session the rider booked an Economy ride (bookedCategoryId = 'economy'). Later their XL reservation goes live and the driver has accepted. Tapping Cancel shows 'Cancelling now costs 35 kr', the economy live fee (fixed 3500 öre after 2 free min). The XL live rule is 15% with a 50 kr minimum, and the reservation cancel that actually runs (`reservations.cancel`) applies reservation rules. When the driver waits at pickup, the fee counter uses economy's 5 free minutes instead of XL's 3. Not run; worked from the seed config in rider_app_config.dart:612-690.
evidence:
lib/features/active_ride/presentation/waiting_for_driver.dart:294-296 `final stored = await RouteChangeController.storedRide(); final category = AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId ?? stored?.categoryId;`
lib/features/active_ride/presentation/waiting_for_driver.dart:772-788 same lookup feeding `LiveCancelFeePreview.of(config, categoryId: category, ...)`
lib/features/reservations/presentation/reservation_live_ride.dart:64-77 `WaitingForDriver(... rideId: ride.reservationId, realtime: realtime, persistRideSnapshot: false, ...)` (category not passed)
lib/features/ride_booking/application/ride_session.dart:205-217 `reset()` does not clear bookedCategoryId/bookedPaymentMethodId/bookedMaxOfferMinor
suggested_fix: Pass the trip's categoryId into WaitingForDriver (the reservation's categoryId; for Book-now, the snapshot's) and use it instead of the session. Accept the stored snapshot only when its rideId equals `_rideId`. Clear the booked* fields in RideSession.reset().

title: After signing back in mid-ride on web, Home says 'Your ride search was interrupted. Book again' while the kept ride is being resumed
description: Whether a ride is live is recorded twice on web: in `RideSnapshotStore` and in a sessionStorage flag (`movera_search_live`). Every `RideSnapshotStore.save` sets the flag (`markSearchLive`). Only `RideRestoreCoordinator.goHome` and the sign-out wipe clear it; `RideSnapshotStore.clear()` does not. Home's initState treats a set flag as proof the search was dropped. Its comment still assumes the old document-load wipe ('the web build's snapshot is gone before Flutter starts'), which R-web removed. When a session expires mid-ride (staging/production, authRequired), `onSessionExpired` deliberately keeps the snapshot and roots Sign in. After the rider signs back in, `enterMoveraApp` mounts Home first, and Home takes the flag and posts the 8-second toast. Only then does `resumeIfNeeded` (which awaits the session check, the snapshot read and a network resync) swap the root to the live Finding/Waiting screen. The SnackBar lives in the root ScaffoldMessenger, so it is still showing on the ride screen. The same mismatch occurs when `_dropIfCancelQueued` ends a ride on reload: it clears the store without clearing the flag, so Home claims the search was interrupted although the rider's own cancel went through.
failure_scenario: Web staging: the rider's refresh token expires while a driver is on the way, and Sign in is shown with the ride kept. The rider signs in and lands on Home with the toast 'Your ride search was interrupted. Book again when you are ready.' A moment later the Waiting screen for the same ride appears under the same toast. The rider may book a second ride or think the trip was lost. Traced by reading the code; not run.
evidence:
lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:189-191 `final interrupted = SearchInterruptedNotice.shared.take() | takeWebSearchInterrupted();`
lib/features/ride_booking/data/ride_snapshot_store.dart:381 `markSearchLive();` (every live save) vs :512-519 `clear()` never calls clearSearchLive
lib/features/auth/presentation/auth_navigation.dart:19-27 `showMoveraRoot(const Home(), ...); if (shown) { unawaited(RideRestoreCoordinator.instance.resumeIfNeeded()); }`
lib/app/di.dart:104-115 session expiry keeps the snapshot
lib/features/ride_booking/application/ride_restore_coordinator.dart:155-163 `_dropIfCancelQueued` clears the snapshot, flag left set
suggested_fix: Derive the notice from the snapshot store, not a second flag. Call clearSearchLive() inside RideSnapshotStore.clear(). Have Home skip the notice while `RideSnapshotStore.read()` still returns a fresh live ride, or announce only after the restore decision (the first root/resumeIfNeeded result) says the ride was dropped.

title: BookingCoordinator's unfinished attempt (key plus replay closure) survives sign-out and is replayed for the next rider
description: `AppScope.instance.booking` is a process singleton. `UserDataWipe.resetInMemory` resets the ride session, Finding, pickup, profile, wallet and others, but never the BookingCoordinator. After a booking that timed out or got a 5xx (`maybeCreated`), `_attempt` is deliberately kept with its idempotency key and a `replay` closure capturing the first request body: the quote id and signed payload, address strings, wallet amount and notes. `_autoQuoteBinding` is kept too. If a different rider signs in on the same device within `BookingAttempt.reuseWindow` (5 min) and books the same intent (same ~11 m pickup/destination cells, category, payment id such as 'cash', notes, wallet flag), `_attemptFor` returns the old attempt. `_prepareFinding` then calls `attempt.replay`, sending the previous rider's body under the previous rider's key with the new rider's token. The in-process mock scopes idempotency only by method+path+key (in_process_mock_client.dart:286-308). If the first request had been stored, it returns the previous rider's ride, and the new rider's session and snapshot adopt it.
failure_scenario: Rider A's Book-now request times out and the mock stored the created ride. A signs out within 5 minutes. Rider B signs in on the same tablet and books the same route with Cash. B's tap replays A's stored request, so B's Finding screen shows A's ride id with A's pickup label and quoted fare, and B's snapshot now holds A's ride. Not run; traced from the code.
evidence:
lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:34-37 `Future<String>? _inflight; BookingAttempt? _attempt; String? _autoQuoteIntent; _BookingQuoteBinding? _autoQuoteBinding;`
lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:69-76 failure keeps `_attempt` unless refused
lib/features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart:355-361 `final attempt = _attemptFor(intentKey); ... if (replay != null) { id = await _sendOrRecover(attempt, replay, ...`
lib/features/auth/application/user_data_wipe.dart:113-143 resetInMemory has no booking reset
suggested_fix: Add a `reset()` to BookingCoordinator that clears _attempt, _inflight and the auto-quote binding, and call it from UserDataWipe.resetInMemory.

title: A cancel that fails with 5xx/429 while the connection is healthy is queued but never retried; the rider is told they are offline
description: _requestServerCancel tries twice. If neither try gets a permanent answer, it returns SearchCancelResult.queued (ActiveRideController._requestServerCancel returns pendingRetry the same way, active_ride_controller.dart:273). The outbox entry is then flushed in only three cases: (1) watchReconnectForPendingCancels, which fires only on a down-to-connected transition of the shared RealtimeConnection (lines 1434-1444); (2) a realtime event whose status is searching (line 382); (3) launch or app resume. When only POST /cancel fails (500/503, or a 429 rate limit), the realtime GET polls keep succeeding. The connection stays 'connected', so (1) never fires. ApiRideRealtime drops unchanged projections without emitting anything (api_ride_realtime.dart:205-211), so (2) never fires. cancelSearch also cancels the tick (line 1105), so checkServerSearchState no longer runs. The cancel sits unsent while the server keeps dispatching. When a driver accepts, _completeAssigned removes the queued entry (line 953) and moves the rider on to Waiting. On Waiting nothing triggers a flush at all.
failure_scenario: The rider taps Cancel request on Finding. The cancel endpoint answers 503 twice while GET /rides/{id} keeps working. The rider sees 'We couldn't reach Movera. We'll cancel your ride as soon as you're back online.' and 'Cancelling your ride…', although they are online. No retry is sent. A driver accepts a minute later and the rider is moved to Waiting with a driver on the way. On Waiting the same 5xx produces 'we'll retry automatically when you're back online'; no retry happens while the app stays in the foreground, the driver arrives, and a late-cancel or no-show fee can follow.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1214-1216 `// Still unreachable: the outbox entry ... stays for the reconnect / next-launch flush.
    return SearchCancelResult.queued;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1435-1439 `if (state == RealtimeState.connected) { if (wasDown) { ... flushPendingCancels(...)`
api_ride_realtime.dart:205-210 `if (poll.version == version && ... poll.lastStatus == status ...) { connection.markConnected(); return; }`
active_ride_controller.dart:273-277 `return (outcome: RideCancelOutcome.pendingRetry, ...)`
suggested_fix: While a cancel is queued, retry it on a backoff timer (respecting Retry-After) independent of connection transitions. Show the offline copy only for NETWORK/TIMEOUT/ClientException failures; give 5xx/429 their own message.

title: If POST /push/devices fails during register(), inbound push streams and the launch notification are never attached for the session
description: register() awaits _replaceToken (the POST /api/v1/push/devices call) before _attachInboundStreams(), and that is the only place _initialMessage is read and the foreground and opened-message streams are subscribed. If the POST throws (offline, timeout, 5xx), or ensureAppleTransportReady throws after 2 s because APNs has no token yet, those lines never run. PushPermissionGate._register catches the error and logs it, and nothing calls register() again during the session: bootstrap calls it once, and sign-in calls it again. PushCoordinator.start() then gets null from takeInitialMessage(), and its listeners sit on _foreground/_opened controllers that are never fed.
failure_scenario: A signed-in rider who accepted notifications cold-starts the app by tapping a 'Your driver has arrived' push while on a flaky network, so POST /push/devices times out. The app opens on Home instead of the ride, because the initial message was never read. For the rest of the session no foreground push reaches the in-app notification feed, and tapping later notifications while the app is in the background does nothing. The FCM token from a previous registration still receives pushes, so the rider does get notifications that do nothing when tapped.
evidence:
firebase_push_service.dart:216-227 `await _gateway.ensureAppleTransportReady(); final token = await _gateway.getToken(...); ... await _replaceToken(token.trim()); await _attachInboundStreams();`
firebase_push_service.dart:267 `_initialMessage = await _gateway.getInitialMessage();`
push_permission_gate.dart:87-89 `} catch (error) { AppLog.warning(logEvent, ...); return PushOptInResult.failed; }`
suggested_fix: Attach the inbound streams and read getInitialMessage before, and independently of, the token registration. Retry registration with backoff, or on the next connectivity or resume event.

title: When the first GPS fix on Home times out, Home says location is off and never retries
description: HomeLocationController.detectCurrent times out after 16 s (detectFixTimeout). It then catches the error, sets state temporarilyUnavailable and returns target null (home_controller.dart:438-446). _runDetectCurrentAddress then writes the 'Location off, set pickup' label and returns, so bindLiveLocation/startTracking never runs and no position stream exists. accessIssue maps only servicesDisabled and permissionRequired to a notice, so temporarilyUnavailable shows no notice and no Try again button. Nothing schedules a retry. The only recovery is an app pause/resume (didChangeAppLifecycleState → recoverLiveLocation) or a booking action that calls _awaitCurrentFix.
failure_scenario: An Android rider opens the app indoors with location permitted and services on. The high-accuracy cold fix takes longer than 16 s. Home keeps the default map with no puck and the pickup label 'Location off, set pickup', and offers no retry. The puck never appears while the rider stays on Home, even after the GPS gets a fix seconds later, until the app is backgrounded or the rider starts a booking.
evidence:
home_controller.dart:438-445 `} catch (_) { _setState(HomeLocationState.temporarilyUnavailable); return const DetectedLocation(target: null, address: locationOffPickupLabel, ... failure: HomeLocationFailure.unavailable);`
home.dart:365-370 `if (detected.denied || target == null) { ... setState(() => _pickupAddress = locationOffPickupLabel); } return; }`
home_controller.dart:303-310 `accessIssue => switch (state) { servicesDisabled => ..., permissionRequired => ..., _ => null }`
suggested_fix: On an 'unavailable' result, start the position stream anyway (startTracking has its own resubscribe backoff), or schedule detectCurrent again. Do not label a timeout as 'Location off'.

title: After location services are turned off and back on mid-session, Home tracking never restarts
description: When the position stream emits LocationServiceDisabledException or PermissionDeniedException, startTracking's onError cancels the subscription, sets _positionSub = null and returns without _scheduleResubscribe. On native the Home notice for servicesOff offers only 'Open settings' (locationSettingsOpenerFor), not the onRetry callback. When the rider comes back from Settings, didChangeAppLifecycleState restarts tracking only when the state is temporarilyUnavailable, or calls _detectCurrentAddress only when _currentLatLng is null. Here the state is servicesDisabled and _currentLatLng is set from the earlier fix, so neither branch runs. resumeLiveUpdates → _refreshAfterResume takes a single latestFix() and sets the state to live, which hides the notice, but no stream is subscribed again.
failure_scenario: A rider on Android has a live puck on Home and turns Location off in quick settings. The 'Location services are off – Open settings' notice appears. The rider turns Location back on and returns to the app. The notice disappears after one fresh fix, but the puck stays frozen at that point while the rider walks, because nothing listens to positions any more. The pickup label also never follows the rider. Only an app restart fixes it.
evidence:
home_controller.dart:478-485 `if (error is PermissionDeniedException) { _setState(HomeLocationState.permissionRequired); return; } if (error is LocationServiceDisabledException) { _setState(HomeLocationState.servicesDisabled); return; }`
home.dart:256-268 `if (_locationCtl.state == HomeLocationState.temporarilyUnavailable) { _locationCtl.recoverLiveLocation(...) } else if (_currentLatLng == null) { _detectCurrentAddress(); }`
home_controller.dart:755-758 `final target = await latestFix(); ... _setState(HomeLocationState.live); onFix(target, heading);` (no startTracking)
suggested_fix: On resume, when _positionSub is null and permission and services are now available, call startTracking. Alternatively, in _refreshAfterResume restart the stream whenever _positionSub == null.

title: Cold start of a signed-in rider with no local ride waits up to about 30 s on GET /rider/trips/active, showing a blank white screen
description: _root() returns `pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip())`, so with no local snapshot (the normal case) the root page waits for ApiActiveTripRepository.fetchActive(). That call goes through ApiClient.get → _getWithRetry: a 15 s timeout, retried once on timeout, plus a refresh round trip on a 401. Until it resolves, RideRestoreGate renders `_child ?? ColoredBox(white)`, and bootstrap has already dismissed the web splash on the first frame. adoptServerActiveTrip catches the eventual error, so the app does open on Home in the end, but only after the full timeout. Server-backed builds (staging/production) compose ApiActiveTripRepository.
failure_scenario: A signed-in rider opens the production app on a poor or captive network where the connection hangs instead of failing at once. They stare at a blank white screen for about 30 s before Home appears. With a 401 refresh in between it takes even longer. Nothing says the app is working, and an Active trip is not needed to show Home.
evidence:
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:453 `return pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip());`
api_client.dart:273-279 `for (var attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) { try { return await _client.get(uri, headers: headers).timeout(_timeout); } on TimeoutException ...`
ride_restore_gate.dart:80-82 `final child = _child ?? const ColoredBox(color: Color(0xFFFFFFFF), child: SizedBox.expand());`
suggested_fix: Render Home immediately and adopt the server trip in the background (replace the root if one comes back), or give the cold-start lookup a short deadline.

title: Safety Kit 'Contact 112' sends no SOS to Movera when the phone dialer cannot be opened
description: _call112 calls emergency.callEmergencyNumber() first and _ctl.sos() only after it. SystemEmergencyDialer.open throws EmergencyCallException whenever launchUrl(tel:) returns false or throws. That exception jumps to the outer `on EmergencyCallException` handler, which only shows a toast, so the SOS event for the ride is never posted. RideCheckController.call112 handles the same failure by still alerting the safety team (_sendAlert runs regardless of the dialer result), so the Safety Kit is the only path where a failed dial also drops the alert.
failure_scenario: On a device that cannot place calls (Android tablet without a dialer, iPad, some in-app browsers), a rider in an emergency during a trip taps 'Contact 112' in the Safety Kit. launchUrl returns false, and the rider sees 'Could not open the system phone dialer.' Movera is not told either: there is no call and no SOS. That is the moment the in-app alert matters most.
evidence:
ride_safety_kit.dart:166-182 `try { await _ctl.emergency.callEmergencyNumber(); try { final registered = await _ctl.sos(rideId: widget.rideId); ... } on EmergencyCallException catch (error) { ... MoveraToast.show(context, error.message); }`
emergency_call_service.dart:38-40 `final opened = await _launcher(uri); if (!opened) { throw EmergencyCallException(L10n.current.dialerOpenFailed); }`
suggested_fix: Send the SOS whatever the dialer outcome (or before dialing), and report both results to the rider.

title: 'My location' in Set pickup and Confirm pickup spot has no Dart-side timeout, so on web it can hang with no feedback
description: The codebase documents (D-003, home_controller.dart:393-395) that geolocator_web passes timeLimit in microseconds, so 15 s becomes about 4 h, and that a Dart-side .timeout is required. Home, current_address.dart, scheduled_category_gate.dart and ConfirmPickupSpot._refreshCurrentFix all add one. PickupMapController.currentPosition relies on timeLimit alone, and two callers await it with no timeout: SetPickupPage._useCurrentLocation (set_pickup_page.dart:631) and ConfirmPickupSpot._useCurrentLocation (confirm_pickup_spot.dart:241). Neither shows a busy state.
failure_scenario: On the public web build, a rider on a desktop or laptop browser with no quick fix taps the 'My location' button on Set pickup. The browser never returns a position, the call never times out, and nothing happens: no snackbar and the pin does not move. The 'location unavailable, move the map' message that exists for this case never appears.
evidence:
pickup_controller.dart:97-102 `final current = await location.getCurrentPosition(locationSettings: const LocationSettings(accuracy: LocationAccuracy.high, timeLimit: Duration(seconds: 15)));` (no .timeout)
home_controller.dart:393-395 `// D-003: geolocator_web passes timeLimit in microseconds ... The Dart-side timeout guarantees the fallback path still runs.`
set_pickup_page.dart:631 `final result = await _pickup.currentPosition();`
suggested_fix: Add `.timeout(...)` inside currentPosition, as the other callers do.

title: 'Book now two paths' tests never run Book now: a stand-in button labelled 'Select Movera' opens ConfirmPickupSpot, nothing starts Finding, and guard_test locks the stale assertion in place
description: The file says it is the 'Book now E2E on two paths' and claims GPS on and GPS off both open Confirm pickup. None of the tests goes through Home or SelectRide. 'GPS available/unavailable still opens Confirm pickup' pump `ConfirmPickupSpot` directly as `home:`, so all they show is that the widget renders. 'Confirm pickup then Select Movera starts Finding Driver' builds its own `TextButton(child: const Text('Select Movera'))` that calls `ConfirmPickupSpot.open`, then only checks `spot != null` and `spot.address == 'Pickup location'`.
