Nothing in it checks Finding, the ride status or `FindingDriverController.active`. The `findsNothing` checks on 'Connecting you with nearby drivers' look for copy the app no longer has (it is in no ARB or lib file), so they can never fail. guard_test.dart:600-620 does not check behaviour either: it only checks that these test names and the dead string appear in the test file's text. That pins the vacuous assertion in place.
failure_scenario: Change Home or SelectRide so that Book now with a GPS fix skips Set pickup/Confirm pickup and books straight away, or so that Confirm pickup never pushes FindingDrivers. Every test in this file still passes, and the guard test still passes because the strings are still in the file. Line 162 also treats the untranslated placeholder 'Pickup location' as the correct booked pickup address, which is the behaviour behind the known L10n.place finding.
suggested_fix: Drive the real flow: pump Home or SelectRide with a fake location repository (fix and no fix), tap the real CTA, and assert that ConfirmPickupSpot/SetPickupPage appears and then FindingDrivers with `ride.status == findingDriver`. Replace the dead-copy findsNothing with `find.byType(FindingDrivers)`, and delete the string-presence guard.

title: 'Book for later keeps the addresses already entered' asserts two local constants equal themselves
description: The test declares `const pickup = 'Klockarvägen 37'` and `const dropoff = 'Arlanda Express'`, switches a fresh RideSelectionController to scheduled, and ends with `expect(pickup, 'Klockarvägen 37'); expect(dropoff, 'Arlanda Express');`. The addresses never reach any production object, so the two address assertions compare a constant with itself. guard_test only checks that this test name exists.
failure_scenario: Home's 'Later' path replaces the addresses already typed with 'Current location' or an empty destination when it switches to Book for later (compare the known schedule_ride.dart:58 prefill bug). The test still passes, because the addresses it checks never left the test.
suggested_fix: Enter both addresses on Home or RoutePicker, choose Later, and assert the addresses shown on ScheduleDateTimeSelector/SelectRide/SetPickup and in the created reservation.

title: 'edit hydrates the saved payment instead of defaulting to Cash' does the hydration itself, so it cannot catch SelectRide losing it
description: In production, payment hydration on edit happens only in SelectRide.initState. It reads `_reservations.byId(widget.editingReservationId!)?.paymentMethod` and calls `_selection.selectPaymentNamed(paymentName)` (select_ride.dart:347-352, again at :406). The test never builds SelectRide. It first asserts that a fresh selection is NOT on Card, then calls `edit.selectPaymentNamed(first.paymentMethod)` itself, and finally asserts the reservation kept 'Card'. All it proves is that ScheduledRideBooking.confirm copies whatever the selection holds. No other test passes `editingReservationId` to SelectRide.
failure_scenario: Delete the `editingReservationId` branch in SelectRide.initState, or let `restoreDefaultPayment()` run after it. Editing a Card reservation then re-saves it as Cash, which is the bug the test title names, and the test still passes.
suggested_fix: Pump SelectRide with `editingReservationId` pointing at a reservation paid by Card, let `_loadSavedCards` finish, and assert the selected payment before confirming.

title: Required Phase 69 journey 'rider cancels after driver assignment' never mounts WaitingForDriver, and its cancel only succeeds through the 404 'no such ride' branch
description: batch5-phase69-test-integrity.yml requires this file as one of the six 'real Rider journeys'. The matched-cancel test pushes a hand-built Scaffold whose button 'Mirrors Waiting's production cancel'. It calls showCancelRideSheet and `ActiveRideController(api: _api()).markCancelled` directly, so none of WaitingForDriver._confirmCancel runs (fee note, phase, change-destination branch, outcome handling, map park, RideNavigator.home). Neither test seeds the ride on the server: `_api()` is a fresh InProcessMockClient with no `rides` entry, and `seed()` writes only local state. The cancel POST therefore gets `status = 404; _error('not_found')`. Both `_requestServerCancel` and Finding's cancel treat 404 as `confirmed`. Any 404 passes the journeys, including the mock's catch-all 'No route for $path' 404 for a wrong URL. The same unseeded pattern appears in cancel_first_controller_test.dart, web/installed_pwa_cancel_restore_test.dart and integration_test/ride_flow_test.dart:60.
failure_scenario: Break WaitingForDriver._confirmCancel, for example by dropping the `RideNavigator.home(context)` call or never calling markCancelled when phase is matched. Or change the cancel path segment so the request hits the mock's 'No route' 404. The 'rider cancels after driver assignment' journey still passes, and the CI gate reports the cancel journey as green.
suggested_fix: Mount the real WaitingForDriver (as waiting_external_terminal_test does) and seed `server.rides[rideId]` with an accepted trip. Assert that the server row becomes cancelled_by_rider, the route returns Home, and History holds the record.

title: Driver-drop tests replace the parked Finding route with a Text widget and then assert 'nothing archived, nothing wiped', so the parked Finding listener is never exercised
description: In the app, WaitingForDriver sits on top of a parked FindingDrivers route whose FindingDriverController listener is still subscribed. The listener has no `_assigned` guard, and `cancelledByDriver.isTerminal` is true, so it goes to `_completeTerminal`, which archives and clears. The driver-drop tests use `home: Text('audit-root')` or `Text('finding-parent')` as the parent. The code comment admits it: 'in the production stack that parent is the already parked Finding route'. They then assert `OnDemandRideHistoryStore.read()` is empty and that the ride is still findingDriver. The journey driver_cancel_research_test.dart, one of the six required Phase 69 journeys, does the same. The one test that does park a real Finding (finding_driver/audit_fix_research_route_test.dart) asserts only route and price, never History, the snapshot or the server status. The 'nothing archived, nothing wiped' guarantee is therefore never tested in the real stack.
failure_scenario: The known finding at finding_driver_controller.dart:394 (a parked Finding archives the drop as cancelled and clears the snapshot) is exactly what these tests would need to catch. With the real parent, the driver drop leaves a 'cancelled' History row and no snapshot, so a reload lands on Home. These tests stay green because the listener that does this is not in the tree.
suggested_fix: Push FindingDrivers first, let it match into WaitingForDriver (as audit_fix_research_route_test does), emit cancelledByDriver, and assert that History is empty, `RideSnapshotStore.read()?.status` is searching, and the session status is findingDriver.

title: Browser 'responsive matrix' gates look for RenderFlex overflow console errors in a --release build, which never emits them
description: The responsive-browser job builds `flutter build web --release -t lib/main_demo.dart`. It then fails a viewport only if a console error matches `/RenderFlex overflowed|A RenderFlex|...|Another exception|Assertion failed/`, or if `document.documentElement.scrollWidth > innerWidth`. Flutter reports layout overflow (RenderFlex._debugReportOverflow and the overflow indicator) and assertion failures only inside `assert(...)`, and asserts are compiled out of release builds. The Flutter view is also sized to the viewport, so a widget overflowing inside the canvas never makes the document wider. Neither check can see a clipped layout. qa-device-pwa-responsive.yml:59 uses the same pattern against the live release Pages build.
failure_scenario: A French label or the Select Ride sheet overflows by 40 px at 320x568. In release the text is clipped with no console output, docWidth stays at 320, and 'Local Chromium + WebKit responsive matrix' passes. The final-candidate gate then reports the build as certified.
suggested_fix: Run the overflow matrix on a debug or profile build (for example `flutter build web --profile`, or `flutter run -d web-server` in debug), or rely on the widget-test overflow matrix. Keep the release check only for crashes.

title: Global UAT 'top up wallet' step only adds two entries to WalletLedger and checks the sum; no wallet code path runs
description: The file says it 'drives booking, wallet, reservations, and profile through their real controllers ... so a regression in any of them fails CI'. The wallet step calls `AppScope.instance.wallet.add(WalletEntry(...))` twice and asserts `balanceMinor == start + 20000 - 34900`, which only tests list summation in WalletLedger. It never runs WalletController.topUp (gateway create/confirm, idempotency, creditTopUp), chargeRide, or the wallet balance repository the UI reads. The booking in the same test uses paymentMethod 'Wallet' for 349 kr, and nothing checks that it is charged. In integration_test/ride_flow_test.dart:29 ('quote then book'), the quote comes from a separate InProcessMockClient and is never passed to submitFinding, so the 'then book' part does not use that quote.
failure_scenario: WalletController.topUp stops crediting (creditTopUp throws or is skipped), or a Wallet-paid ride is never debited. The 'Booking wallet reservations profile UAT' step in batch7-phase85, deep-safe-recertification and backend-readiness still passes.
suggested_fix: Call `WalletController.topUp(...)` with the mock gateway and assert the balance from `walletBalances.loadBalance()`. Complete the Wallet-paid ride through `chargeCompletedRide` and assert the debit.

title: AUD-3 chevron test never taps the chevron: it is only built when the sheet is expanded, and the test never expands it
description: FindingDrivers renders the collapse chevron only `if (_sheetExpanded)`, and `_sheetExpanded` starts false. The test opens Finding at rest, looks up `find.bySemanticsLabel('Collapse')`, and taps it only `if (chevron.evaluate().isNotEmpty)`. That condition is false, so nothing is tapped, and `expect(find.text('Cancel ride?'), findsNothing)` holds trivially. The rest of the test checks the separate close button.
failure_scenario: Wire the chevron's onPressed to `_confirmCancel`, which is the AUD-3 regression. The test still passes because the chevron is never on screen when it looks.
suggested_fix: Drag the sheet up (or set it with `_sheetController`) first, assert the chevron is found (`findsOneWidget`, not an `if`), tap it, then assert 'Cancel ride?' is absent and the sheet collapsed.

title: 'each placeholder survives translation' skips every count/number placeholder, and plural =1 branches are never rendered
description: tool/gen_l10n_messages.py passes the sample `3` for int/num/double placeholders. It writes into `messagePlaceholders` only the names whose type is String (`if dart_type(s) == 'String'`). So for homeRideCount, ridesLeft, validUntilDays(days), driverTripCount, tripSharingStarted, safetyContactsCount, retrySeconds and resSeatsPayment(count), the test never checks that `{count}`/`{days}` survives in fr/sv. Every message is also rendered only with 3, so the `=1{...}` branch of each plural is never checked, for either 'translated' or 'placeholder present'.
failure_scenario: Change the sv text of retrySeconds to `{count, plural, =1{1 sekund} other{några sekunder}}`, or leave the fr `=1` branch of tripSharingStarted in English. The rider then sees 'några sekunder' with no number, or English in French, and rider-l10n.yml stays green.
suggested_fix: Use a distinctive numeric sample (for example 37), check that the rendered text contains '37' for numeric placeholders, and render each plural message with 1 as well, comparing it against English.

title: 'duplicate payment key returns same intent family' asserts only the amount, so it cannot detect a second intent (or the wrong intent) being returned
description: The test creates two intents with key 'dup' and asserts `second.amountMinor == 5000`. Any newly created intent for 5000 öre satisfies that, so idempotency is not tested. It also hides a defect in the mock: on a reused key MockPaymentGateway returns `_intents.values.last`, the most recently created intent of any key, not the one created for that key. ops_test 'top-up idempotency key reused' uses a single key too, so the mismatch is never seen.
evidence:
test/wallet/gateway_test.dart:28-41  await gw.create(amountMinor: 5000, ..., idempotencyKey: 'dup'); final second = await gw.create(..., idempotencyKey: 'dup'); expect(second.amountMinor, 5000);
lib/core/payments/mock_payment_gateway.dart:21-23  if (_usedKeys.contains(idempotencyKey) && _intents.isNotEmpty) { return _intents.values.last; }
failure_scenario: Remove the idempotency check, so every call creates `pi_<new>`, and the test still passes. Or create key A (100 kr), then key B (200 kr), then retry A. The mock returns B's 200 kr intent, and no test notices.
suggested_fix: Assert `second.id == first.id`. Add a two-key case and key the mock's map by idempotency key.

title: 'waiting/in-trip driver call is explicitly unavailable' injects the unavailable dialog itself, so it cannot catch WaitingForDriver wiring Call to anything else
description: Both widget tests build WaitingDriverCard/RiderInTripPanel with `onCall: () => showDriverCallUnavailable(...)` written in the test, then tap Call and find the dialog. The production wiring is WaitingForDriver passing `onCall: _callDriverUnavailable` (waiting_for_driver.dart:1888, :1903), and it is never exercised. The tests only show that a callback the test supplies is called.
evidence:
test/safety/phase71_real_calling_test.dart:95-98  onCall: () => showDriverCallUnavailable(context, driverName: _driver.firstName),
:126-129 same for RiderInTripPanel
lib/features/active_ride/presentation/waiting_for_driver.dart:1888  onCall: _callDriverUnavailable,
failure_scenario: Change WaitingForDriver to `onCall: () => launchUrl(Uri(scheme: 'tel', path: driver.phone))`, which dials an unmasked number, or to a no-op. The batch6/phase71 'explicitly unavailable' tests still pass.
suggested_fix: Pump WaitingForDriver with a matched driver (as waiting_external_terminal_test does), tap 'Call driver', and assert the unavailable dialog appears.

title: Custom FCM service worker drops every push while a Movera tab is visible, so web foreground messages never reach onMessage
description: The worker loads no Firebase SDK (the test enforces no importScripts). In the Firebase JS SDK, the page's onMessage only fires when the messaging service worker posts the payload to window clients ({isFirebaseMessaging:true, messageType:'push-received'}). The browser delivers push events only to the service worker, never to the page. This worker sees a visible client and returns undefined. It shows no notification and calls no client.postMessage. The comment's claim that 'A visible Movera tab receives the message through onMessage instead' is false. FirebasePushService._attachInboundStreams subscribes to FirebaseMessaging.onMessage (firebase_push_service.dart:126), and that stream never emits on web, so PushCoordinator never shows the in-app ride update.
failure_scenario: Production/staging web build with MOVERA_FIREBASE_* and VAPID set (as built in batch6-phase78-push.yml). The rider accepted ride updates and has the tab open. The backend sends 'driver arrived'. The SW sees a visible client and returns. No system notification appears, onMessage never fires, and no in-app toast is shown. The update is silently lost. Verified by reading the code; nothing was run.
suggested_fix: When a client is visible, postMessage the payload to the clients in the Firebase internal format, or importScripts the Firebase messaging SW SDK and let it route foreground messages. Otherwise always show the notification.

title: Web notification tap opens the app root and drops the ride id; firebase_messaging_web never emits opened/initial messages
description: The push handler stores payload.data (rideId, type, deepLink) on the notification. notificationclick ignores event.notification.data and opens or focuses './'. On web, firebase_messaging_web.getInitialMessage() always returns null and onMessageOpenedApp is never fed. So PushCoordinator's openRide/openNotifications routing (PushDestination.ride) can never run on web. On web, tapping a ride notification just lands on whatever the cold start restores, never on the notification's ride or on the Notifications screen.
failure_scenario: Web rider with the tab hidden gets a 'trip.completed' or 'ride.driver_assigned' notification for a ride and taps it. The SW focuses the tab, and the data is discarded. The app does not navigate to the ride or to Notifications, unlike Android/iOS, where onMessageOpenedApp routes it. Verified by reading the code.
suggested_fix: In notificationclick, encode the ride id or deep link into the opened URL, or postMessage it to the focused client, and handle it in Dart on web.

title: Safety audio recording stops capturing when the app backgrounds or the 112 dialer opens; no iOS audio background mode or Android foreground service, and the default interruption mode pauses without resume
description: NativeSafetyRecorder starts `record` with a bare RecordConfig. The audioInterruption default is AudioInterruptionMode.pause, which pauses on an interruption such as a phone call and needs a manual resume. Nothing in the app ever resumes. Info.plist UIBackgroundModes holds only remote-notification, not audio, so iOS suspends the recorder when the screen locks or the app leaves the foreground. On Android there is no foreground service (no FOREGROUND_SERVICE/FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE permission, no AndroidRecordConfig service), and since Android 9 a backgrounded app gets silence from the mic. The UI copy says recording continues until Stop or until the kit closes. SafetyAudioService.stop computes durationMs from wall-clock start/end, so the saved record claims the full duration. The Safety Kit and Ride check put 'Record audio' next to 'Call 112', and the 112 button opens the external dialer (backgrounds the app and starts a call), which is exactly the moment audio matters.
failure_scenario: During a ride the rider taps Record audio, then Call 112 (or locks the phone). The dialer or call takes the foreground. iOS suspends or pauses the AVAudioRecorder, and Android delivers silence. When the rider returns, the card still shows 'Recording mm:ss'. Stop saves a file that holds only the seconds before the call, while the record lists the full wall-clock duration. Verified by reading the code and plugin defaults; nothing was run.
suggested_fix: Add the iOS 'audio' background mode and configure the audio session. On Android, record through the plugin's foreground service with FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE. Choose pauseResume, or listen to onStateChange and surface paused state. Compute the duration from the recorder, not the wall clock.

title: Book for later is 'switched off' in staging/production only at the repository; every Home/menu entry still opens the full scheduling flow, which fails at the last step
description: FeatureFlags.release sets enableScheduledRide/enableBookingLater false, and AppScope composes DisabledReservationRepository. ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/backend-readiness-gate.md say Book for later is 'switched off in staging/production'. No UI reads flags.scheduledRides or flags.bookingLater (the only flag consumers are RideSelectionController and wallet.dart's businessProfile). The release build still shows AdvanceBookingCard, the Schedule bottom-nav item, the WhereTo card's schedule action, the side menu 'Later' chip and History's schedule button. Each runs route picker, date/time, Select Ride and Set pickup. Only on Book does createReservation reject with ReservationsUnavailableException ('Booking for later isn't available yet, so nothing was booked.'). The comment in reservation_controller wiring also leaves rulesSource null, so the flow runs on default rules.
failure_scenario: A production rider taps 'Schedule' on Home. They choose a destination, a date and time, a category and a pickup, then tap Book. They get 'Booking for later isn't available yet, so nothing was booked.' The feature the docs say is switched off is fully offered, and the rider wastes the whole flow. Verified by reading the code.
suggested_fix: Gate every Book-for-later entry point (Home card, nav item, WhereTo, side menu, History, plan-return) on AppScope.instance.flags.scheduledRides || bookingLater.

title: 'compile-time release env parser' test exercises AppEnv.parseFlavor, which the app never uses; the real compile-time parser treats unknown or mis-cased flavors as demo
description: AppEnv.current derives the flavor with an exact-match ternary chain on the MOVERA_FLAVOR define. Anything else (e.g. 'Production', 'prod', ' production') silently becomes AppFlavor.demo: in-process mock API, mock payments, NoopPush, and a seeded demo wallet balance in bootstrap. parseFlavor (trim + lowercase) is referenced only by this test, so the test passes while the code path it claims to cover is untested and behaves differently. main.dart (the default `flutter build` target) has no flavor assertion, so a release built with `-t lib/main.dart --dart-define=MOVERA_FLAVOR=Production` ships as demo with every release guard skipped (allowsMockTransport is true for demo).
evidence:
lib/app/config/env.dart:32-41 flavor: _flavorName == 'production' ? AppFlavor.production : _flavorName == 'staging' ? ... : AppFlavor.demo,
lib/app/config/env.dart:59-64 static AppFlavor parseFlavor(String value) { ... flavor.name == value.trim().toLowerCase() ...
test/architecture/phase72_actual_release_composition_test.dart:17-25 test('compile-time release env parser distinguishes demo and production', () { expect(AppEnv.parseFlavor('demo'), ...
lib/main.dart:3-5 void main() { bootstrap(); }
failure_scenario: An operator builds `flutter build apk --release --dart-define=MOVERA_FLAVOR=Production -t lib/main.dart`. The app starts as demo, with mock rides, a fake driver and a seeded wallet, and no composition guard fires. CI's 'compile-time release env parser' test stays green because it never touches AppEnv.current's parser. Worked by hand; nothing was run.
suggested_fix: Build AppEnv.current's flavor from parseFlavor (or reject unknown values), make main.dart refuse a non-demo-looking but unknown define, and test the actual const path.

title: Release transport guard accepts FirebasePushService with no Firebase config, so staging/production builds ship push that can never register
description: TransportComposition rejects NoopPushService/UnavailablePushService as 'Mock/no-op transport' but accepts any FirebasePushService. di.dart always composes FirebasePushService for non-mock flavors, whether or not MOVERA_FIREBASE_* or the VAPID key were passed. With no config, every register() throws PushConfigurationException, which makes it equivalent to the UnavailablePushService the guard forbids. Every production build in CI except phase78/80 has no Firebase defines, including the signed APK in android-release-signing.yml. The PushPermissionGate is still enabled (enabled: !allowsMockTransport), so the rider is offered 'Get ride updates', taps Turn on, and always gets pushFailed.
evidence:
lib/app/config/transport_composition.dart:60 if (push is NoopPushService || push is UnavailablePushService) 'push',
lib/app/di.dart:121-123 push = environment.allowsMockTransport ? NoopPushService() : FirebasePushService(api: api, environment: environment);
lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:199-208 if (!_environment.hasFirebaseConfig) { throw const PushConfigurationException(...)
.github/workflows/android-release-signing.yml:49-52 flutter build apk --release -t lib/main_production.dart --dart-define=MOVERA_FLAVOR=production --dart-define=MOVERA_API_BASE_URL=...
failure_scenario: A production APK is built exactly as the signing workflow does. Composition passes. The rider is shown the push primer, accepts, and sees 'couldn't turn on notifications' every time, so ride updates never arrive. The release guard that exists to catch this never fires. Verified by reading the code.
suggested_fix: In TransportComposition, add 'push' when push is FirebasePushService && !environment.hasFirebaseConfig (and, on web, when the VAPID key is empty).

title: Release base-URL validator only rejects .invalid; the reserved .example/.test/localhost hosts used by every CI production artifact pass
description: releaseApiBaseUrlProblem's documented purpose is to refuse a placeholder host whose every request would fail DNS at runtime. It checks only 'invalid'/'*.invalid'. RFC 2606/6761 reserve .example, .test and .localhost the same way, and they never resolve. All production/staging CI builds, including the signed 'production release APK', use https://api.movera.example or api.staging.movera.example, and the guard waves them through.
evidence:
lib/app/config/transport_composition.dart:26-29 final host = uri.host.toLowerCase(); if (host == 'invalid' || host.endsWith('.invalid')) { return ... }
.github/workflows/android-release-signing.yml:52 --dart-define=MOVERA_API_BASE_URL=https://api.movera.example
failure_scenario: The production APK from the Android release signing workflow starts normally. Then every API call (sign-in OTP, quotes, booking) fails with a DNS error, which is exactly what the guard claims to prevent. Worked by hand.
suggested_fix: Also reject example, test, localhost, local and their subdomains, plus IP literals, for release-like flavors. Give CI a real staging host, or build with an explicit allow flag.

title: Portrait lock is ignored on iPad: TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY includes iPad, Info.plist allows all iPad orientations, and UIRequiresFullScreen is not set
description: bootstrap locks portrait with SystemChrome.setPreferredOrientations. Flutter documents that on iPad this is only respected when multitasking is disabled (UIRequiresFullScreen). The Runner target builds for iPhone and iPad (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2"), and UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad lists both landscapes. So on iPad the phone-only, ScreenUtil-scaled UI rotates to landscape.
failure_scenario: A rider on an iPad holds it in landscape. The app rotates despite the lock, and the frozen portrait layout (map, bottom sheets, ScreenUtil sizing) renders stretched and clipped. Verified by reading the config.
suggested_fix: Set UIRequiresFullScreen=true, or restrict the iPad orientations in Info.plist to portrait, or set TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY to 1.

title: iOS permission purpose strings exist only in English; no sv/fr InfoPlist.strings or CFBundleLocalizations although the app ships sv/fr and defaults Stockholm riders to Swedish
description: The app supports en, fr and sv (lib/l10n/app_*.arb), and the zone default (Q48) picks the language for Stockholm. The OS location and microphone prompts that iOS shows use NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription/NSMicrophoneUsageDescription from Info.plist. There is no sv.lproj/fr.lproj InfoPlist.strings and no CFBundleLocalizations (ios/Runner holds only Base.lproj). So a Swedish rider gets English system prompts in the middle of a Swedish UI, and iOS does not offer the app's languages in per-app Language settings.
evidence:
ios/Runner/Info.plist:5-8 <key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key><string>Movera uses the microphone only when you choose to record audio during a ride.</string> <key>NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription</key><string>Movera uses your location while you use the app to set your pickup point...</string>
(find ios/Runner: only Base.lproj/LaunchScreen.storyboard, Base.lproj/Main.storyboard)
failure_scenario: A rider whose iPhone is set to Swedish opens Movera, which is in Swedish. The location prompt reads 'Movera uses your location while you use the app...' in English, and the same happens when they tap Record audio. Verified by reading the config.
suggested_fix: Add CFBundleLocalizations (en, sv, fr) and sv.lproj/fr.lproj/InfoPlist.strings with translated purpose strings.

title: Approximate-only location (Android 12+ 'Approximate', iOS 'Precise: Off') is accepted as the rider's exact pickup and saved as the 'last good high-accuracy fix'
description: The manifest declares ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION next to FINE, so Android 12+ lets the rider grant only approximate location. iOS 14+ has the same toggle. geolocator then returns fixes with accuracy of several km. detectCurrent never checks Position.accuracy or Geolocator.getLocationAccuracy(), does not request temporary full accuracy, and immediately treats the fix as the 'Current location' pickup, reverse-geocodes it, and calls _rememberGoodFix. The repository describes that fix as 'a successful high-accuracy fix'.
evidence:
android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:4-5 ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION / ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION
lib/features/home/application/home_controller.dart:395-405 final position = await location.getCurrentPosition(locationSettings: const LocationSettings(accuracy: LocationAccuracy.high, ...)).timeout(detectFixTimeout); _accurateFixSeen = true; _rememberGoodFix(position);
lib/core/location/location_repository.dart:71 /// Remembers a successful high-accuracy fix for the next cold start.
(grep: no use of Position.accuracy or getLocationAccuracy anywhere in lib/)
failure_scenario: The rider picks 'Approximate' in the Android 12 permission dialog. Home centres on a point about 1-3 km away and labels it as the current-location pickup with that street's address, and the booking dispatches the driver there unless the rider notices and moves the pin. Verified by reading the code.
suggested_fix: Check getLocationAccuracy() / Position.accuracy, show the 'precise location off' notice, and on iOS request temporary full accuracy (NSLocationTemporaryUsageDescriptionDictionary) before using the fix as a pickup.

title: Re-running the publish workflow for the same commit fails at 'git commit' (nothing to commit) after Pages is already deployed
description: The web-live step commits the build output unconditionally. Fingerprinted names come from GITHUB_SHA[:8], and the rest of the dart2js output is deterministic. A workflow_dispatch or 're-run' on the same SHA therefore produces a tree identical to web-live HEAD. `git commit` then exits 1 under bash -e, the job turns red and no push happens, even though Pages already deployed successfully.
evidence:
.github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:166-170
          cp -a /tmp/movera-web/. .
          touch .nojekyll
          git add -A
          git commit -m "Publish Movera Rider web build"
          git push origin HEAD:web-live
failure_scenario: An operator re-runs 'Publish Rider Web Demo' to retry a flaky Pages deploy. The deploy succeeds, but the job fails with 'nothing to commit, working tree clean', so every re-run of a good build shows as failed. Worked by hand.
suggested_fix: Use `git diff --cached --quiet || git commit ...` (or `git commit --allow-empty`).

title: Telemetry version comment says CI passes MOVERA_APP_VERSION, but no workflow does, so every release-like build reports appVersion 'dev'
description: CrashReporter attaches appVersion to every crash/telemetry record (crash_reporter.dart:24). The constant's contract is that CI passes the pubspec version with --dart-define=MOVERA_APP_VERSION. None of the production/staging builds in .github/workflows (android-release-signing, phase72/73/74/78/80/85, backend-readiness-gate) pass it, so release telemetry can never be told apart by version.
evidence:
lib/core/constants/app_version.dart:1-7 /// ... CI passes the pubspec version with `--dart-define=MOVERA_APP_VERSION=<version>`; local builds report `dev` ... const appVersion = String.fromEnvironment('MOVERA_APP_VERSION', defaultValue: 'dev');
grep MOVERA_APP_VERSION .github -> no matches
failure_scenario: Every crash from the signed production APK is posted to /api/v1/telemetry/crashes with appVersion 'dev', so operators cannot tell which release crashes. Verified by grep.
suggested_fix: Pass --dart-define=MOVERA_APP_VERSION=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml ...) in every release build step, or derive it from package info.

title: Switching to the generic 'Card' row on Set pickup gets past the Add card step, so a card ride is booked with no card saved
description: The Book now path checks for a saved card only once, before Set pickup opens: `if (payment.brand == 'cards' && !_selection.hasSavedCard) { final card = await AddCardPage.open(context); ... }` (line 1463). Set pickup then offers its own payment change through `onChangePayment: () async { await _showPaymentPicker(); ... }` (line 1318). That opens PayWithPage, and with no saved card PayWithPage lists the generic 'cards' row (`rideMethods` only hides it when `hasSavedCards`). Tapping that row pops 'cards', and `_showPaymentPicker` selects it. Back in `_bookNow`, the method is read again (`final chosen = _selection.selectedPaymentItem(); ... payment = _PaymentOption(brand: chosen.brand, ...)`, line 1491) with no second card check. `submitFinding(paymentMethod: payment.brand)` then sends `paymentMethodId: 'cards'`. The in-process mock does not check paymentMethodId on POST /rides, so the ride is created, and Finding, Waiting and History all show 'Card'.
failure_scenario: A rider with no saved card keeps Cash on Select Ride and taps Book. On Set pickup they tap the payment line and pick 'Card'. Set pickup shows Card, they tap Confirm, and the search starts with paymentMethodId 'cards'. No card was ever added, so on a real backend the fare cannot be charged and the rider was never asked for card details.
evidence:
select_ride.dart:1463 `if (payment.brand == 'cards' && !_selection.hasSavedCard) {` (runs only before Set pickup)
select_ride.dart:1318 `onChangePayment: () async { await _showPaymentPicker(); return paymentLine(); },`
select_ride.dart:1491-1498 `final chosen = _selection.selectedPaymentItem(); if (chosen != null) { payment = _PaymentOption(brand: chosen.brand, ...` (no hasSavedCard check)
pay_with_page.dart:199 `.where((m) => !(hasSavedCards && m.brand == 'cards'))` / :254 `onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).pop(method.brand)`
suggested_fix: After Set pickup returns, run the same gate again: if the chosen brand is 'cards' and there is no saved card, open AddCardPage (or refuse to book). A cleaner fix is to make PayWithPage open Add card when the generic Card row is tapped, the way its '+ Add payment method' row does.

title: Wallet part of the fare is never deducted if the rider taps Done before paymentFinalized arrives (and is never deducted for ended-early trips)
description: D-022 says a wallet-paid or wallet-split ride is taken off the local wallet balance once it reaches a charged status. The only place that does this is `_maybeChargeWallet` on the completion screen. It returns early while `_completionRank(_status) < _completionRank(RideStatus.paymentFinalized)` and only runs again from the `_completionSub` listener. The Done and Back buttons are enabled the whole time (`onPressed: _leaving ? null : _closeAndHome`, line 414). Leaving calls `closeCompletedRide`, which clears the snapshot, then pops the screen, and `dispose` cancels `_completionSub`. When paymentFinalized later arrives, nothing is listening, and no other caller of `chargeCompletedRideById` exists in lib/. Ended-early trips have the same gap: `initState` returns at `if (widget.endedEarly != null) return;` (line 102) before `_maybeChargeWallet()` is ever called, and that summary also passes `persistOnDemandState: false`.
failure_scenario: The rider has 100 kr in the wallet with 'Use wallet balance first' on (the default), so a 150 kr trip is booked with walletAmountMinor 10000. The trip completes and the summary shows 'Payment processing'. The rider taps Done right away (in the mock, within the 500 ms + 500 ms before paymentFinalized; on a real server the window can be much longer). History shows the ride as completed, but the wallet still shows 100 kr, and that balance can be spent on the next ride.
evidence:
ride_completed.dart:149-158 `void _maybeChargeWallet() { if (!widget.persistOnDemandState || _walletChargeRequested) return; if (_completionRank(_status) < _completionRank(RideStatus.paymentFinalized)) { return; } ...`
ride_completed.dart:414 `onPressed: _leaving ? null : _closeAndHome,`
ride_completed.dart:102 `if (widget.endedEarly != null) return;`
wallet_controller.dart:238 `chargeCompletedRideById` has one caller (ride_completed.dart:163)
suggested_fix: Do not tie the wallet debit to the completion screen staying open. Charge it from the controller that sees the ride reach a charged status (for example in persistCompletedStatus/closeCompletedRide, or a realtime listener that outlives the screen), or charge it in _leave before closing. Charge the ended-early fare's wallet part as well.

title: Waiting treats the post-trip states `closed` and `paymentFailed` as external terminals: `closed` throws in markExternalTerminal and leaves the screen dead, `paymentFailed` drops the trip from History and skips the receipt
description: `RideStatusWire._afterCompletion` maps a `completed` projection with paymentStatus failed to `RideStatus.paymentFailed`, and one with rating submitted or skipped to `RideStatus.closed`. Both are `isTerminal` but not `isCompletedSurface`. `_onLiveTick` sends any `status.isTerminal && !status.isCompletedSurface` to `_queueStageNavigation`, and from there to `_handleExternalTerminal`. That method sets `_leaving = true`, disposes tracking, then calls `_ride.markExternalTerminal(status)`. For `closed`, markExternalTerminal throws `ArgumentError` (`status == RideStatus.closed`), and nothing catches it because the call runs as `unawaited(_handleExternalTerminal(status))`. Waiting stays on screen with tracking stopped, no completion screen and the snapshot never cleared. For `paymentFailed`, markExternalTerminal archives only its listed cancel statuses, so the completed trip is never written to History. It then clears the snapshot and sends the rider Home with a 'payment failed' sheet, with no receipt and no rating. ApiRideRealtime emits whatever `fromProjection` returns, so one poll that jumps from in-trip to completed+failed, or to completed+captured+skipped (for example when the app was backgrounded through drop-off), reaches this path.
failure_scenario: The app is in the background during drop-off. The server completes the trip, captures payment and marks the rating skipped. On resume, the first poll gives `closed`, and Waiting throws inside `_handleExternalTerminal`: the map is parked and the screen is frozen, with no summary and no route Home. If the poll instead gives completed with paymentStatus failed, the rider is sent Home and the finished trip is missing from History.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:417-419 `if (status.isTerminal && !status.isCompletedSurface) { _queueStageNavigation(status); return; }`
active_ride_controller.dart:337-347 `Future<void> markExternalTerminal(RideStatus status) async { if (!status.isTerminal || status.isCompletedSurface || status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider || status == RideStatus.closed) { throw ArgumentError.value(...` 
trip_status.dart:183 `if (payment == TripPaymentStatus.failed) return RideStatus.paymentFailed;` / `TripRatingStatus.submitted || TripRatingStatus.skipped => RideStatus.closed`
core/contracts/ride_status.dart isTerminal includes closed and paymentFailed; isCompletedSurface does not
suggested_fix: In Waiting, send `closed` and `paymentFailed` (both are trip `completed`, see `tripStatus`) to the completion path (markCompleted plus RideCompleted, or archive as completed), not to markExternalTerminal.

title: Search elapsed time is counted in timer ticks, not from searchStartedAt, so a background pause holds back 'Still looking', the raise-offer card and the server check
description: `start()` works out `elapsedSeconds` from `snapshot.searchStart` once (ARCH-3 / RIDE-5: 'elapsed counts from when this search started'). After that, `_startTick` only adds `elapsedSeconds += 1` each periodic tick. Timers are suspended while a mobile app is in the background, and browsers throttle them in hidden tabs (iOS Safari suspends the tab; Chrome drops to about one tick a minute after 5 minutes). Neither Finding nor its controller has a lifecycle hook (only Home and AppLifecycleObserver observe lifecycle), so after a pause the counter stays behind wall-clock time. Everything gated on it fires late: `isDelayed`/searchDelayed, `showPriceBump` (`elapsedSeconds >= priceBumpAfter.inSeconds`), `_reachSearchTimeout` and the periodic `checkServerSearchState`.
failure_scenario: The rider books, waits 30 s, then switches apps for 4 minutes while the search goes on. When they come back, Finding shows about 30 s elapsed and the early 'searching' copy. 'Still looking for a driver' (3-minute mark) and the server check behind it only appear 2.5 minutes later, although the search has really run 4.5 minutes, so a server-ended 'no driver found' is noticed late too.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:337-340 `final sinceStart = DateTime.now().difference(snapshot.searchStart); elapsedSeconds = sinceStart.isNegative ? 0 : sinceStart.inSeconds;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:418-428 `_tick = Timer.periodic(const Duration(seconds: 1), (timer) { ... elapsedSeconds += 1; _evaluatePhase(); _afterElapsed(1); ...`
suggested_fix: On each tick, recompute elapsed from `_snapshot.searchStart` (`DateTime.now().difference(searchStart).inSeconds`) and pass the real step to `_afterElapsed`, so a resumed tick catches up at once.

title: 'Try again' after no driver found books a fresh server quote that the rider never sees or confirms, dropping a raised offer
description: `_requestAgain` calls `submitFinding(price: ended.price, ...)` without any quote fields. In `BookingCoordinator._resolveQuoteBinding`, `suppliedCount == 0`, so it fetches a new quote and calls `..validate()` without `requestedPrice`. The `ended.price` the rider last saw is never compared. `_prepareFinding` then books `effectivePrice = binding.total.major`, which can be higher or lower. Select Ride stops for `_acceptNewPrice` whenever the price to book differs from the one shown (RIDE-1/2). This path books silently, and the new search starts at whatever the server quotes now. A raised offer the rider made in the previous search is also lost. The new price only appears afterwards, on the payment line.
failure_scenario: The rider raised the offer from 120 kr to 140 kr, the server then answered noDriverFound, and the rider taps 'Try again'. A new ride is created at the fresh quote, say 165 kr in surge, or the plain 120 kr without the raise, with no confirmation step. The rider believes they re-requested the same 140 kr ride.
evidence:
finding_drivers.dart:352-368 `rideId = await (widget.booking ?? BookingController()).submitFinding( ... price: ended.price, quoteCurrency: ended.currency, ...` (no quoteId/quoteSignedPayload/quoteExpiresAt/quoteTotalMinor)
booking_coordinator.dart:567-574 `final binding = _BookingQuoteBinding(... totalMinor: quote.totalMinor, ...)..validate();` (no requestedPrice)
booking_coordinator.dart:409 `final effectivePrice = binding.total.major;`
suggested_fix: Quote first in `_requestAgain`. If the quote differs from `ended.price`, ask the rider to accept the new price, the same prompt as `_acceptNewPrice` on Select Ride. Otherwise pass `requestedPrice` into validation so a changed fare is refused, not silently booked.

title: A Book-now cancel fee the server charges is never recorded, so History shows 'Cancelled' with the full booked price and no fee
description: When the rider cancels on Waiting after the free window, the mock server works out `_riderCancelFee` and stores it as `ride.cancellation.fee` in the cancel response (in_process_mock_client.dart:712, 724-733). `ActiveRideController._requestServerCancel` only reads `fare` from that response (`_chargedFare`, lines 282-285). `_commitCancelled` then archives with `_archive(snapshot, RideStatus.cancelledByRider, ...)`, which has no fee argument. `OnDemandRideHistoryStore.recordFor` (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:184-235) builds the `Reservation` without `cancellationFee`, and so does the server-backed `ApiRideHistoryRepository._record`. History does have a fee display: `ReservationFormat.historyStatus` shows 'Cancelled · fee X', and the detail sheet shows the `cancelFee` line (ride_history.dart:537). Neither ever appears for an on-demand ride. `Reservation.cancellationFee` is only ever set by the reservation repository.
failure_scenario: Economy ride at 245 kr. The driver accepted 3 minutes ago. The rider opens Cancel and the sheet says 'Cancelling now costs 35 kr.' They confirm, and the server stores cancellation.fee = 3500 öre. In History > Cancelled the card says just 'Cancelled', and the detail says 'Movera · Booked price 245 kr' with no fee line. The rider cannot see that they were charged 35 kr, and the screen suggests 245 kr.
evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:232-236 `return (outcome: RideCancelOutcome.confirmed, command: entry.command, charged: _chargedFare(response));` (only `fare`)
active_ride_controller.dart:308-314 `await _archive(snapshot, RideStatus.cancelledByRider, expectedRideId: id, cancellationReason: reasonId, endedEarly: endedEarly);`
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:198-234 `return Reservation(... cancellationReason: ..., endedEarly: ..., chargedFare: charged,);` (no cancellationFee)
in_process_mock_client.dart:733 `'fee': fee?.toJson(),`
ride_history.dart:537 `if (ride.cancellationFee case final fee? when fee.isPositive) ...`
suggested_fix: Parse `projection/ride.cancellation.fee` (Money) from the cancel response and from server trips. Pass it through `_archive` / `archive` / `recordFor` into `Reservation.cancellationFee`.

title: Cancel sheet opened before boarding still sends end_early (a charged trip) if the trip starts while the sheet is open
description: `_confirmCancel` fixes the phase (`CancelPhase.matched`) and the fee note ('free…') when the sheet opens (lines 804-812). Then it awaits two sheets, the confirm sheet and the reason sheet. Nothing closes or re-checks them when the stage changes: `_onLiveTick` only closes the arrived sheet on trip start (lines 396-403). After the rider confirms, `markCancelled` chooses the command from the session status at send time (`onboard = tripRiderOnboardStatuses.contains(...)`, active_ride_controller.dart:207-211). It therefore posts `/end-early`, and the server charges base fare plus distance (`_endEarlyFare`). The app then opens the 'ended early' receipt. Finding has a guard for this exact race (RIDE-15, `driverMatched` closes the sheet); Waiting has none for boarding.
failure_scenario: Demo: the driver reaches pickup, and the mock boards the rider 8 s later (`boardAfter`). The rider taps Cancel while the driver waits and sees 'Cancel ride? … Cancelling is free for less than a minute more.' They pick a reason. Meanwhile tripStarted arrives. On confirm, POST /rides/{id}/end-early runs and the rider lands on an 'Ended early' summary charged the base fare (e.g. 45 kr) for a cancel the app called free.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:804-812 `final feeNote = await _cancelFeeNote(); ... phase: _isInTrip ? CancelPhase.inTrip : CancelPhase.matched, feeNote: feeNote,`
waiting_for_driver.dart:838 `final result = await _ride.markCancelled(`
active_ride_controller.dart:207-211 `final onboard = tripRiderOnboardStatuses.contains(AppScope.instance.ride.status.tripStatus); final command = onboard ? PendingCancelCommand.endEarly : PendingCancelCommand.cancel;`
suggested_fix: Close the cancel and reason sheets when `_isInTrip` changes, as RIDE-15 does on Finding. Or pass the phase the rider confirmed into markCancelled, and refuse or re-ask when the session's onboard state no longer matches it.

title: Free-cancel note overstates the time left by up to a minute and is frozen while the rider goes through two sheets, so a cancel shown as free is charged
description: `LiveCancelFeePreview.of` computes `minutes = elapsed.inMinutes` (floor) and `freeMinutesLeft = rule.freeMin - minutes`, which rounds the time left up. Waiting turns that into 'Cancelling is free for {left} more minutes' (waiting_for_driver.dart:794-796). The note is computed once before the confirm sheet opens and never refreshed. The cancel is sent only after the confirm sheet and the reason sheet both close. The server charges by its own clock at that moment (`CancelFeeCalculator.live(rule, fare, now.difference(accepted).inMinutes)`).
failure_scenario: Economy, freeMin 2, 35 kr fee. The driver accepted at 12:00:00. At 12:00:59 the rider taps Cancel: minutes=0, left=2, and the sheet says 'Cancelling is free for 2 more minutes.' Only 61 s remain. The rider reads the reasons and confirms at 12:02:05, 66 s later and well inside the 2 minutes promised. The server sees minutes=2, not < freeMin, and charges 35 kr.
evidence:
rider_app_config.dart:714-720 `final elapsed = now.difference(acceptedAt); final minutes = elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : elapsed.inMinutes; ... freeMinutesLeft: fee.isPositive ? 0 : rule.freeMin - minutes,`
waiting_for_driver.dart:794-796 `return left <= 1 ? L10n.current.cancelFreeUnderMinute : L10n.current.cancelFreeMinutes('$left');`
waiting_for_driver.dart:804 `final feeNote = await _cancelFeeNote();` (once, before both sheets)
suggested_fix: Compute the remaining free time in seconds and floor it, or show an absolute 'free until HH:MM'. Re-evaluate the fee just before sending; if it changed from free to a fee since the sheet opened, ask the rider to confirm again.

title: A queued (offline) end-early that the server later applies is committed as a plain cancel: no receipt, History shows 'Cancelled · booked price', and the reason is lost
description: When an on-board end-early cannot reach the server, it stays in the outbox (`command: endEarly`). Later the flush, or `_dropIfCancelQueued` on restore, sends it. `_dropIfCancelQueued` deliberately keeps the snapshot for end-early so that 'the restored trip resyncs and shows how the server closed it' (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150). Realtime then reports cancelledByRider, and Waiting's `_handleExternalTerminal` calls `completeServerConfirmedCancel()` (waiting_for_driver.dart:570-576). That method calls `_commitCancelled(rideId)` with no `endedEarly` and no `reasonId`. So there is no `LastCompletedRide`, no ended-early summary, History gets `endedEarly: false` and no `chargedFare`, the stored reason is dropped, and the rider is sent straight Home.
failure_scenario: The rider taps 'End trip here' on board with no connection and gets 'We couldn't reach Movera…'. On reconnect the outbox posts /end-early, and the server sets fare to the distance price, e.g. 80 kr. Polling reports cancelledByRider, and the app goes Home with no receipt. History shows 'Cancelled ride · Movera · Booked price 245 kr' with no 'Ended early' and no reason, although 80 kr was charged.
evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:159-161 `Future<void> completeServerConfirmedCancel() async { await _commitCancelled(AppScope.instance.ride.rideId); }`
waiting_for_driver.dart:570-575 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider && widget.onTerminal == null) { await _ride.completeServerConfirmedCancel(); ... RideNavigator.home(context);`
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150 `// An end-early that went through ends the trip ... the restored trip resyncs and shows how the server closed it.`
suggested_fix: Keep the queued command and reason (or read `cancellation`/`fare`/`endedEarly` from the projection). For an end-early, commit it with an EndedEarlyTrip (charged = projection fare) and open the ended-early summary instead of going Home.

title: Outbox replays a cancel queued while searching against a trip a driver has since accepted, cancelling the matched ride (and charging the live fee) despite the match path promising it cannot
description: `_completeAssigned` says a match that overtakes a queued cancel removes it 'so it cannot cancel the matched ride later' (lines 947-959), and tells the rider 'driver already accepted'. But the flush (`_flushPendingCancels` / `_rereadForReplay`) re-reads the trip and replays the cancel whenever `TripStateMachine.apply(status, 'cancel', rider)` allows it. Rider cancel is allowed from accepted, driver_to_pickup and arrived. The flush also moves the entry onto the current version (`forVersion`), which removes the version check that would have refused it. On cold start `_dropIfCancelQueued` flushes before any screen exists. On reconnect the flush runs in parallel with the realtime match. Either way the cancel reaches the server for an accepted trip. The mock then charges `_riderCancelFee` counted from acceptedAt.
failure_scenario: The rider taps Cancel while searching with no signal and gets 'Cancelling…' (queued, free). They close the app. A driver accepts at 12:00 and drives toward the pickup. At 12:06 the rider reopens the app. The restore flush re-reads `accepted`/`driver_to_pickup`, the state machine allows `cancel`, and the cancel is posted. The server cancels the trip and stores a 35 kr live cancel fee, for a cancel the rider made while it was free.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1559-1577 `final applies = TripStateMachine.apply(status, command, TripActor.rider, ...) != null; if (!applies) { ... stale } return (result: null, version: version);`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1473-1477 `cancel = cancel.forVersion(version);`
finding_driver_controller.dart:948-953 `// ... the stale request leaves the outbox so it cannot cancel the matched ride later. ... PendingCancelStore.remove(id)`
in_process_mock_client.dart:712 `final fee = command == 'cancel' ? _riderCancelFee(ride) : null;`
suggested_fix: When replaying a `cancel` queued during search, drop it as stale once the trip is past searching/offered (accepted or later), or send the version from when it was queued. Report it as refused/stale so the rider decides again with the fee shown.

title: Any 409 refusal of a search cancel is reported as 'a driver already accepted', even when the projection says the search expired
description: `_requestServerCancel` maps every non-version 409 to `SearchCancelResult.driverAccepted` without looking at `error.projection`. The mock refuses `cancel` from `expired` with `409 invalid_transition` (the expiry is applied lazily on GET; `cancel` is not allowed from expired). The outbox path `_refusalResult` re-reads the status, but the in-session path does not. Finding then shows `driverAlreadyAccepted`, and the resync that follows brings the 'No driver found' sheet. The listener's terminal handling is also not blocked while `_cancelInFlight`, so an expiry seen mid-cancel produces the same pair of messages.
failure_scenario: The search passed the server's 3-minute expiry, and a poll or server check marked it expired. The rider taps Cancel request. The POST returns 409 invalid_transition with status 'expired'. A snackbar says 'A driver already accepted your ride', then the 'No driver found' sheet appears.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1205-1210 `final status = error.statusCode; if (status == 404) return SearchCancelResult.confirmed; if (error.isVersionMismatch) return SearchCancelResult.stale; return status == 409 ? SearchCancelResult.driverAccepted : SearchCancelResult.rejected;`
finding_drivers.dart:603-606 `} else if (result == SearchCancelResult.driverAccepted) { _showCancelNotice(context.l10n.driverAlreadyAccepted,`
suggested_fix: Read the projection status from the ApiError. Return driverAccepted only when it is matched, and treat terminal statuses as rejected or ended.

title: Re-tapping cancel after an unreachable attempt reuses the stale outbox entry (old expectedVersion and first reason), so the server refuses it as 'ride just changed' or stores a different reason than History
description: `enqueue` returns the existing entry whenever one with the same command exists, keeping its `expectedVersion` from the first tap and its `reasonId`. `PendingCancel.body(fallback)` prefers the stored reason (`reasonId ?? fallbackReason`). On Waiting a second cancel after `pendingRetry` therefore sends the old version and the old reason. If the trip moved on meanwhile (e.g. assigned → arriving bumps the version), the mock answers 409 version_mismatch, which becomes `stale`, and the rider sees 'ride just changed' and must tap a third time. If it succeeds, the server keeps reason 1 while `_commitCancelled(reasonId: reason2)` archives reason 2 in History.
failure_scenario: The rider cancels with reason 'plans_changed' and gets 'We couldn't reach Movera'. The driver's status advances and the connection returns. The rider taps Cancel again with 'driver_not_suitable'. The POST carries expectedVersion=old and reason 'plans_changed'. The result is 409 version_mismatch and 'Your ride just changed'. On the next try the server stores 'plans_changed' while History says 'driver_not_suitable'.
evidence:
pending_cancel_store.dart:295-300 `final existing = await find(rideId); if (existing != null && existing.command == command && existing.idempotencyKey != null) { return existing; }`
pending_cancel_store.dart:78 `...CancelReasonCodes.riderCancelBody(reasonId ?? fallbackReason),`
active_ride_controller.dart:215-220 `final entry = await PendingCancelStore.enqueue(rideId: id, reasonId: reasonId, command: command, expectedVersion: session.projectionVersionOf(id));`
suggested_fix: On a new rider tap, refresh the entry with the current version and reason (new key, since the body changed), as the flush does with `forVersion`.

title: History stores English reason labels for server-ended searches and terminals; the detail sheet shows them untranslated in fr/sv
description: `_endedSearchReason` writes literal English strings ('No driver found', 'Request expired', 'Cancelled by Movera', 'No-show', …) into `cancellationReason` for new records. The History detail renders them through `ReservationFormat.reasonLabel`, which translates only reason codes (`system_no_driver` etc.). Any other value that does not match the snake_case pattern is returned as it is. The comment there says only 'older records' hold labels, but every new noDriverFound/expired/admin/no-show archive still writes one.
failure_scenario: App language Swedish. The search ends with noDriverFound and is archived. History > Cancelled > detail shows 'Orsak: No driver found' in English.
evidence:
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:261-271 `RideStatus.noDriverFound => 'No driver found', RideStatus.bookingExpired => 'Request expired', ... RideStatus.noShow => 'No-show',`
reservation_format.dart reasonLabel: `final known = _reasonLabels[value]; ... if (RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(_[a-z0-9]+)+$').hasMatch(value)) {...} return value;`
suggested_fix: Store the contract codes (`system_no_driver`, `rider_no_show`, `admin_*`, …) and let `reasonLabel` translate them.

title: A terminal or completed status that arrives while a Waiting cancel is in flight is dropped, not queued, and nothing re-drains after the cancel is refused
description: `_confirmCancel` sets `_leaving = true` before awaiting `markCancelled`. `_queueStageNavigation` returns early when `_leaving` is set, without storing `_pendingStageStatus`. If the server refuses the cancel because the ride just ended (409 → rejected), `_leaving` is reset to false but nothing replays the dropped status. The rider stays on Waiting with 'This ride can no longer be cancelled', and the terminal or completion surface opens only when some later tick (for example a staleness flip) calls `_onLiveTick` again.
failure_scenario: Near the destination the rider taps 'End trip here'. While the request is out, realtime delivers tripCompleted, which `_queueStageNavigation` drops because `_leaving` is true. The server answers 409 because the trip already completed, and the app shows 'This ride can no longer be cancelled.' The rider is left on the in-trip Waiting screen instead of the completion screen until another event happens to arrive.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:514-518 `void _queueStageNavigation(RideStatus status) { if (!mounted || _leaving || _completedOpened) return; _pendingStageStatus = status; _drainStageNavigation(); }`
waiting_for_driver.dart:828-829 `_leaving = true; setState(() {});`
waiting_for_driver.dart:846-852 `if (result != RideCancelOutcome.confirmed) { setState(() { _cancelling = false; _leaving = false; }); _showCancelProblem(result); return; }`
suggested_fix: Store the pending status even while leaving. After a non-confirmed cancel outcome, call `_onLiveTick()` / `_drainStageNavigation()` so the current tracked status is acted on.

title: Polling transport misses driver drops: a drop is only detected when one _RidePoll sees `searching` right after a matched status, and that poll state is thrown away at every screen handover
description: ApiRideRealtime reports a driver drop only when `status.isSearching && (poll.lastStatus?.isMatched ?? false)` (lines 193-199). `poll.lastStatus` lives on the per-subscription `_RidePoll`, and `onCancel` (lines 78-84) removes that poll as soon as its only listener cancels. Every handover cancels the only listener: Finding `_openWaiting` calls `_match.dispose()`, which cancels `_sub` (finding_driver_controller.dart:1682), before Waiting subscribes again. `_retryLiveFeed` does the same. So Waiting's tracking always starts with a new poll whose `lastStatus` is null. (a) When the driver drops in the 'just assigned' stage, before Waiting's first poll returns, that first projection is `searching`, `reassigned` is false, and the event goes out as plain `findingDriver`. The first poll can be late because it fails and backs off for 1, 2, 4... s. DriverTrackingController accepts it. Waiting `_onLiveTick` (waiting_for_driver.dart:410-433) only re-dispatches on `cancelledByDriver`, so Waiting stays up with the dropped driver's card. (b) Even inside one poll, a drop is missed when driver B accepts before the next successful poll: every 2 s, or a backgrounded app whose timers paused. The stream then goes straight from driverArriving/driverWaiting(A) to driverAssigned(B). Nothing compares driver ids, so no notice is shown.
failure_scenario: Release build on the polling transport. The rider is at the 'driver waiting' stage, the arrived sheet showing driver A (Elin, plate MVR 204) is up, and the phone is pocketed so the app is backgrounded. A drops and dispatch matches B within a minute. On resume, the first poll returns `accepted` with driver B. Waiting swaps the card to B with no 'your driver cancelled' notice. The arrived sheet with A's name and plate stays on top, because it closes only on trip start (line 396). B's arrival is never announced, because `_arrivalAnnounced` is already true (line 452). Variant (a): A accepts and drops within about 1 s. Waiting shows 'Driver found / leave now, Elin' while the server is searching. If no one accepts, `expired` reaches Waiting as noDriverFound and `markExternalTerminal` clears it without archiving (noDriverFound is not in the archive list at active_ride_controller.dart:353-358). The rider is also never offered RIDE-19 'Try again'.
evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:193-199: `final reassigned = status.isSearching && (poll.lastStatus?.isMatched ?? false); ... if (reassigned) status = RideStatus.cancelledByDriver;`
api_ride_realtime.dart:78-84: `onCancel: () { poll.timer?.cancel(); ... if (identical(_rides[id], poll)) _rides.remove(id); ... controller.close()`
finding_drivers.dart:528: `_match.dispose();` (before pushing Waiting)
waiting_for_driver.dart:410-415: only `status == RideStatus.cancelledByDriver` triggers `_researchAfterDriverCancel`
waiting_for_driver.dart:452: `_arrivalAnnounced ||` (never reset for a new driver)
suggested_fix: Keep reassignment state (last lifecycle status and driver id) per ride id, outside the per-subscription poll, for example in a map like `_sequences`. Also treat a change of `driver.id` between two matched projections as a driver-cancelled reassignment, so Waiting re-dispatches or at least shows the notice, closes the old arrived sheet and resets `_arrivalAnnounced`.

title: A driver drop or no-show that arrives while Waiting's cancel request is in flight is dropped for good when the cancel is rejected or queued
description: From the moment the rider confirms the cancel sheet, `_confirmCancel` sets `_leaving = true` (line 820) and awaits `markCancelled`. While `_leaving` is true: a `cancelledByDriver` tick is ignored (lines 410-415, guarded by `!_leaving`); `_queueStageNavigation` returns without storing the status (line 515); and `_drainStageNavigation` returns without consuming one stored earlier (lines 521-526). When the server refuses (`rejected` / `stale`) or cannot be reached (`pendingRetry`), lines 847-853 set `_leaving = false` and show a snackbar. They never re-check `_tracking.status` or call `_drainStageNavigation`. After a terminal status the realtime gate passes only payment/rating events, so no later tick replays it. A sheet pop drains in a post-frame callback, but `_confirmCancel` resumes in a microtask and sets `_leaving` first, so that drain is lost as well.
failure_scenario: The driver has waited 5 minutes at pickup. The rider opens Cancel ride and confirms, and in the same moment the driver marks no-show, so the server trip is `no_show`. Tracking gets noShow, but `_queueStageNavigation` drops it because `_leaving` is true. The rider's POST /cancel gets 409 invalid_transition, so the outcome is `rejected`. The rider sees 'This ride can no longer be cancelled', and Waiting stays up as if the driver were still waiting. The no-show sheet is never shown, the ride is not archived and the snapshot is not cleared until the rider happens to navigate or reload. Same pattern for a driver drop during an offline (pendingRetry) cancel: the re-dispatch is skipped, Waiting keeps the dropped driver, and the next driver later appears silently on the same screen.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:410-415: `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByDriver) { if (!_leaving && !_completedOpened) { unawaited(_researchAfterDriverCancel()); } return; }`
515: `if (!mounted || _leaving || _completedOpened) return;`
521-526: `if (!mounted || _leaving || ... ) { return; }`
847-853: `if (result != RideCancelOutcome.confirmed) { setState(() { _cancelling = false; _leaving = false; }); _showCancelProblem(result); return; }`
suggested_fix: After resetting `_leaving` on a non-confirmed outcome (and in the catch block), re-run the stage logic: call `_onLiveTick()`, or queue `_tracking.status` when it is terminal or cancelledByDriver. Alternatively, record the pending status in `_queueStageNavigation` even while `_leaving` is true.

title: On-demand cancel and no-show fees are never recorded: History shows the full booked fare with no fee line, though the app says the fee is on the History receipt
description: When a matched ride is cancelled late, the server puts the fee in `projection.cancellation.fee`. The in-process mock does this through `_riderCancelFee` (in_process_mock_client.dart:711, 724-733). `_requestServerCancel` reads only `fare` (via `_chargedFare`, used for end-early) and ignores `cancellation.fee`. `_commitCancelled` then archives with no fee (lines 308-314), and `markExternalTerminal` archives no-show with no fee either (line 359). `OnDemandRideHistoryStore.recordFor` has no fee parameter and never sets `Reservation.cancellationFee` (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:184-234). Server-backed History builds records through the same `recordFor` (ride_history_repositories.dart:59). So History's 'Cancelled · fee' chip (reservation_format.dart:29-32) and the fee line in the detail view (ride_history.dart:537) never appear for Book Now rides. The no-show sheet tells the rider 'You can see any fee on your receipt in History' (app_en.arb termNoShowNote).
failure_scenario: Economy ride (SEK live rule: 2 free minutes, then a fixed 35 kr). The driver accepted 4 minutes ago. The rider taps Cancel, sees 'Cancelling now costs kr 35', and confirms. The mock answers 200 with `cancellation.fee = {amountMinor: 3500}`. Waiting goes Home. In History the ride reads 'Cancelled ride', 'Booked Economy · kr <full fare>', with no fee chip and no fee line. A rider charged 35 kr, or charged a no-show fee by a real backend, cannot see it, and the record shows the full fare as if it were the amount involved.
evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:282-285: `static Money? _chargedFare(...) { ... return ride is Map ? Money.fromWire(ride['fare']) : null; }` (only fare)
active_ride_controller.dart:308-314: `await _archive(snapshot, RideStatus.cancelledByRider, expectedRideId: id, cancellationReason: reasonId, endedEarly: endedEarly);`
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:198-234: `Reservation(... price: snapshot.price, ... chargedFare: charged,)` — no `cancellationFee`
in_process_mock_client.dart:729-733: `'fee': fee?.toJson(),`
suggested_fix: Parse `cancellation.fee` from the cancel response, and from the terminal projection for no-show and other external terminals. Pass it through `_archive` into `recordFor`, and set `cancellationFee` there. Make `ApiRideHistoryRepository._record` read the same field.

title: History stores English labels ('No-show', 'No driver found', 'Cancelled by Movera', ...) as the cancel reason, so they show untranslated in sv/fr
description: `_endedSearchReason` writes English literals into `cancellationReason` for no-show, no driver, admin, system, failed and driver-ended rides. The History detail shows it through `ReservationFormat.reasonLabel`. That function translates contract codes (`rider_no_show` -> reasonNoShow, `system_no_driver` -> termNoDriverFound) and snake_case codes, and returns anything else verbatim. 'No-show' matches neither the code map nor the snake_case regex, so a Swedish or French rider sees the English text. reasonLabel's comment says verbatim labels are only for older records, but every new archive still writes them.
failure_scenario: The app language is Swedish. The driver marks no-show, Waiting calls `markExternalTerminal(noShow)`, and the archive stores `cancellationReason: 'No-show'`. The History detail shows 'Orsak: No-show' instead of the localized reasonNoShow text. The same happens for 'No driver found' (Finding archive, RIDE-5) and 'Cancelled by Movera'.
evidence:
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:261-271: `RideStatus.noShow => 'No-show', ... RideStatus.noDriverFound => 'No driver found', RideStatus.cancelledByAdmin => 'Cancelled by Movera',`
reservation_format.dart: `'rider_no_show': L10n.current.reasonNoShow, 'system_no_driver': L10n.current.termNoDriverFound,` ... `return value;`
suggested_fix: Store the contract reason codes (`rider_no_show`, `system_no_driver`, `admin_...`) that `reasonLabel` already translates, not English text.

title: A no-show or other pre-trip terminal status stays hidden behind the 'Your driver has arrived' sheet until the rider dismisses it
description: The arrived sheet opens when the driver reaches the pickup (`_maybeAnnounceArrival`) and is closed in code only when the trip starts (lines 396-403). Terminal statuses go through `_queueStageNavigation` / `_drainStageNavigation`, which refuse to act while `!_routeIsCurrent` (line 525), and the arrived sheet is a modal route above Waiting. No-show is the terminal that by definition happens while the driver is waiting at the pickup, which is exactly when this sheet is up. The rider therefore keeps seeing 'Your driver has arrived', with the driver's name and plate, after the server has closed the trip. History archival and the snapshot clear are also held back until dismissal.
failure_scenario: The driver arrives and the arrived sheet opens. The rider does not come out. After 5 minutes the driver marks no-show, and tracking reports noShow, which is queued because the route is not current. The rider looks at the phone and sees 'Your driver has arrived · MVR 204', with no hint that the ride has ended as a no-show and may carry a fee. Only after swiping the sheet away do the no-show sheet and Home appear.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:396-403: `if (_arrivedSheetShowing && DriverEta.isInTrip(status)) { ... closeRouteByReference(route); }` (trip start only)
417-419: `if (status.isTerminal && !status.isCompletedSurface) { _queueStageNavigation(status); return; }`
521-526: `if (... || !_routeIsCurrent) { return; }`
suggested_fix: Also close `_arrivedSheetRoute` (by reference, as for trip start) when a terminal or cancelledByDriver status arrives, then drain the stage navigation.

title: Re-dispatched search keeps the first search's 'Arrive by HH:MM' and 'N min' map pins, so an impossible arrival time is shown after a driver drop
description: `_prepareMapVisuals` runs once, from initState. It bakes into the pickup and destination pin bitmaps `widget.etaMinutes` and an absolute clock time, `DateTime.now() + eta + tripMinutes` worked out from the original route. When a driver drops, `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` (lines 292-314) adopts the stored route, possibly changed on Waiting, and restarts matching, but it only calls `_loadMapBits`, which reuses the cached `_riderPuck` / `_destinationPin` icons. The re-dispatched search therefore still shows the arrival time computed when the rider first booked, and for the original destination.
failure_scenario: Booked at 14:00 with ETA 5 min and a 20 min trip, so the pins read '5 min' and 'Arrive by 14:25'. Driver A accepts, drives for 10 minutes, then drops at 14:12, and Finding resumes. The pins still say 'Arrive by 14:25' and '5 min', although no driver has been found and 14:25 can no longer be reached. If the rider had changed the destination on Waiting, the time is also for the old route.
evidence:
finding_drivers.dart:485-495: `eta == null ? RouteEndpointMarker.createIcon(pickup: false) : RouteTimeMarker.createIcon(pickup: false, label: context.l10n.arriveBy(clockTime(DateTime.now().add(Duration(minutes: eta + tripMinutes)))))`
finding_drivers.dart:292-314: `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` ... `_startMatching(price: effectivePrice, searchStartedAt: DateTime.now()); _loadMapBits();` (no `_prepareMapVisuals`)
suggested_fix: On a re-dispatch (and after `_adoptRoute`), rebuild the pins, using plain endpoint markers once the original estimate no longer holds.

title: Home says 'Your ride search was interrupted. Book again' after a cancel the rider made, and before a ride that is then restored
description: Every snapshot save calls markSearchLive() (ride_snapshot_store.dart:381, 462), which writes sessionStorage 'movera_search_live'. Only RideRestoreCoordinator.goHome (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:229) and UserDataWipe clear that flag. RideSnapshotStore.clear() and OnDemandRideHistoryStore.archiveCancelledThenClear (on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:102) do not. Home reads the flag on every mount: `SearchInterruptedNotice.shared.take() | takeWebSearchInterrupted()` and shows homeSearchInterrupted for 8 s. The comment above it says the web snapshot is gone before Flutter starts. That stopped being true with R-web: the flag now means 'a ride was saved in this tab and goHome never ran', not 'a live ride was dropped'. Three real paths: (1) Cancel-first on Finding commits the cancel (archive + clear) and then opens the why-sheet (finding_drivers.dart:621-635). ARCHITECTURE.md says a reload there lands on Home, and Home then says the search was interrupted. (2) An on-board end-early commits and clears, then shows the ended-early summary; a reload there lands on Home with the same toast. (3) On a cold start, _dropIfCancelQueued confirms a queued cancel and returns null, so Home opens with the toast for a ride the rider cancelled. A fourth case: enterMoveraApp (auth_navigation.dart:20-26) mounts Home first, which shows the toast, and only then calls resumeIfNeeded, which restores the ride the toast just called interrupted.
evidence:
home.dart:190-191 `final interrupted = SearchInterruptedNotice.shared.take() | takeWebSearchInterrupted();`
ride_snapshot_store.dart:381 `markSearchLive();` (every live save)
on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:102 `await RideSnapshotStore.clear();` (no clearSearchLive)
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:229 `clearSearchLive();` (only in goHome)
finding_drivers.dart:627-635 why-sheet shown after commit, RideNavigator.home only after it closes
failure_scenario: On the public web demo the rider books, taps Cancel request, the server confirms, and the 'Why did you cancel?' sheet opens. The rider reloads the tab. Home opens with the toast 'Your ride search was interrupted. Book again when you are ready.', although the rider cancelled on purpose and the ride is archived as cancelled in History.
suggested_fix: Clear the session flag wherever the live snapshot is cleared on purpose (RideSnapshotStore.clear, or archiveCancelledThenClear / the commit paths). In enterMoveraApp, decide on the notice only after resumeIfNeeded has run.

title: Reload while the driver is waiting at pickup regresses the ride to 'driver arriving' with the car about 800 m away
description: pageFor primes the mock with the snapshot status (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:339-344). For any matched status that is not on board, subscribe() takes the pre-trip branch: it places the driver at `pickup + 0.0072 / -0.0048` and starts _startGps(). It does this for driverWaiting too. The first GPS tick 3 s later moves only 18% toward pickup, so the distance is still far over 50 m. It then sets `status = RideStatus.driverArriving` and emits it with a higher sequence. DriverTrackingController accepts it, because the version is newer than the seeded one. _persistLiveStatus then saves driverArriving: _wouldRegress allows a lower stage when the incoming version is greater. Waiting goes back to 'driver on the way'. About 15 ticks (roughly 45 s) later the driver 'arrives' a second time and the arrived sheet and the boarding timer run again.
evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:206-211 `// The remaining isMatched statuses are the pre-trip approach: driverAssigned, driverArriving, driverWaiting.` `lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; lastLng ??= _pickupLng! - 0.0048; _startGps();`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:401-412 `var status = RideStatus.driverArriving; ... if (distance < 50) status = RideStatus.driverWaiting; lastStatus = status; _emit(status);`
driver_tracking_controller.dart:233-241 `_wouldRegress` returns false when incoming version > stored version
failure_scenario: Demo build: the driver reaches pickup (Waiting shows 'Your driver has arrived'). The rider reloads, or Safari kills the tab. Waiting comes back as driverWaiting, and 3 s later it switches to 'driver arriving' with the car drawn about 800 m away. The stored snapshot is overwritten with driverArriving. The car then drives back and announces its arrival again.
suggested_fix: On resume with driverWaiting, put the driver at pickup and call _startTrip() instead of _startGps(). Never emit an approach status lower than the primed one.

title: On public Pages a reload restores the ride screen, but the in-process server has forgotten the ride, so rating/tip, offer raise and route change all fail
description: DECISIONS R-web requires a live ride to survive a reload on public Pages. The UI does survive it: RideSnapshotStore restores Finding, Waiting or RideCompleted. But the demo's 'server' is InProcessMockClient, whose `rides` map is in memory only.
