Safety state is persisted (`persistSafety: true`); rides are not, and nothing re-seeds the server from the snapshot. After a reload every ride call answers 404. Feedback: POST /rides/:id/feedback returns 404, RideFeedbackRepository.submit throws, and RideCompleted._leave shows feedbackSaveFailed and stays on screen. The rider can only leave by backing out without the rating or tip. Also, PATCH offer raise and route-quote fail, GET nearby is empty, and the mock's own status commits are silently refused.
evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:82 `final Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> rides = {};` (only written at :609 by POST /rides)
in_process_mock_client.dart:617-620 `final ride = rides[parts[4]]; ... if (ride == null) { status = 404; ...`
api_client.dart:30 `InProcessMockClient(persistSafety: true)` (safety persisted, rides not)
ride_completed.dart:226-244 submitFeedback inside try; the catch sets `_submitError = context.l10n.feedbackSaveFailed`
failure_scenario: Public demo: the trip completes and the rating screen shows. The rider reloads, and the completion screen is restored at ratingPending. The rider picks 5 stars and a tip and taps Done. The screen shows 'feedback could not be saved' every time. The only way out is back plus 'Leave without sending', which drops the rating and tip.
suggested_fix: Persist the mock rides map the way safety state is persisted, or re-seed the ride from the restored snapshot. Then a restored ride's commands reach a server that knows it.

title: A queued end-early that lands after a reload (or after reconnecting) is committed as a plain cancel: no receipt, no rating, History not marked 'Ended early'
description: The rider ends the trip on board while offline. markCancelled returns pendingRetry and the end_early command stays in the outbox. On reload, _dropIfCancelQueued deliberately keeps the snapshot for endEarly. Its comment says 'the restored trip resyncs and shows how the server closed it' (ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150). The launch flush then sends end_early, and the server projection becomes cancelled_by_rider, which RideStatusWire maps to RideStatus.cancelledByRider. Waiting's _handleExternalTerminal treats every cancelledByRider as a plain queued cancel: completeServerConfirmedCancel() runs _commitCancelled with endedEarly == null. History is archived with endedEarly:false and charged:null, LastCompletedRide is not set, and the rider goes Home. R-O6 says an ended-early trip gets the normal trip-end screen with rating and tip. The same happens without a reload when the reconnect flush delivers it.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:570-576 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider && widget.onTerminal == null) { await _ride.completeServerConfirmedCancel(); ... RideNavigator.home(context); return; }`
active_ride_controller.dart:159-161 `completeServerConfirmedCancel() async { await _commitCancelled(AppScope.instance.ride.rideId); }` (no endedEarly)
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:144-150 endEarly kept for the restored trip to 'show how the server closed it'
trip_transitions.dart:209 `end_early` → `cancelled_by_rider`
failure_scenario: On board with no signal, the rider taps End trip, and the request is queued. The phone browser reloads when signal returns. The flush sends end_early and the server bills the distance driven. The restored Waiting then sees cancelled_by_rider and drops the rider on Home without the trip summary or a chance to rate. History lists it as a cancelled ride with no fare.
suggested_fix: When the outbox reports a sent endEarly for this ride, or the projection carries endedBy 'end_early', open the ended-early summary (EndedEarlyTrip with the projection's fare) instead of completeServerConfirmedCancel.

title: A restored Waiting that receives a 'closed' projection throws in markExternalTerminal and leaves a dead screen that comes back on every reload
description: RideStatusWire maps completed + captured + rating submitted/skipped to RideStatus.closed. closed is terminal and not a completed surface. Waiting therefore sends it to _handleExternalTerminal, which sets `_leaving = true`, disposes tracking and calls `_ride.markExternalTerminal(closed)`. markExternalTerminal explicitly throws ArgumentError for closed. The future is unawaited, so the error goes to the zone. Waiting stays mounted with `_leaving == true` (every action returns early) and no live feed. The snapshot is never cleared, so each reload restores Waiting and gets stuck again until the 6 h freshness window runs out.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:417-419 `if (status.isTerminal && !status.isCompletedSurface) { _queueStageNavigation(status); ...`
waiting_for_driver.dart:563-565 `_leaving = true; setState(() {}); _tracking.dispose();`
waiting_for_driver.dart:589 `await _ride.markExternalTerminal(status);`
active_ride_controller.dart:338-347 `if (!status.isTerminal || status.isCompletedSurface || status == RideStatus.cancelledByRider || status == RideStatus.closed) { throw ArgumentError.value(...)`
trip_status.dart:186-188 `TripRatingStatus.submitted || TripRatingStatus.skipped => RideStatus.closed`
failure_scenario: Release build: the phone dies mid-trip. The trip completes, payment is captured, and the server marks the rating skipped (or the rider rated from another device). The rider reopens the PWA within 6 h. Waiting is restored at tripInProgress, the first poll returns closed, and the screen freezes with no updates and dead buttons. Reloading brings back the same frozen screen.
suggested_fix: Handle closed (and other settled completion states) in _handleExternalTerminal: archive it as completed, clear the snapshot and go Home, or open RideCompleted, instead of calling markExternalTerminal.

title: resumeIfNeeded swaps the root to Home without setting `showing`, so the coordinator keeps reporting a ride surface
description: When the snapshot is gone or stale on resume and the root shows a restored ride, resumeIfNeeded builds `_gatedHome()` and calls onReplaceRoot. Unlike goHome and replaceRootSurface, it never sets `showing = RestoredSurface.home` or reports the surface. Several things read `showing`. RideRestoreGate._lockHomeIfRoot and HomeHistoryObserver compute `setWebHomeLock(atRoot && home)` as false, so the browser-tab back-swipe sentinel is off on Home. Every later resume finds `next (home) != showing` and replaces the root Home again (map/controller churn, Home initState re-runs). RideNavigator.home's `rootWasRestoredRide` is wrongly true, which causes the double root replacement its own comment warns about.
evidence:
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:599-602 `final next = surfaceFor(snapshot); if (next == showing) return null; final page = next == RestoredSurface.home ? _gatedHome() : pageFor(snapshot); onReplaceRoot?.call(page);`
ride_restore_gate.dart:47-49 `final home = RideRestoreCoordinator.instance.showing == RestoredSurface.home; setWebHomeLock(atRoot && home);`
failure_scenario: A cold-restored Finding is at the root. The tab is hidden for more than 20 minutes (the search snapshot window). On return, resumeIfNeeded shows Home, but `showing` stays 'finding'. The Home history lock is off, so a horizontal overscroll on Home can trigger browser back. Each later tab switch rebuilds Home from scratch.
suggested_fix: In the home branch, set `showing = RestoredSurface.home` and call reportRestoreSurface (or call goHome()) before replacing the root.

title: A restored completion screen does not prime the mock transport, which restarts a whole fake ride (search, assignment, trip) for the finished trip
description: pageFor calls primeResume only for the waiting surface (`surface == RestoredSurface.waiting && snapshot.status.isMatched`). For RestoredSurface.complete, RideCompleted subscribes to the fresh MockRideRealtime with nothing primed. subscribe() resets to findingDriver, arms the 25 s assignment, then walks the GPS approach, boarding and trip ticks. It POSTs accepted, driver_to_pickup and so on to /rides/:id/status for a completed trip. RideCompleted ignores the non-completion events, so a completion screen restored at tripCompleted, paymentProcessing or paymentFinalized gets no ratingPending (rating stays locked, the wallet charge is delayed) until the fake ride ends about 100 s later. The timers also keep running after the rider taps Done, because closeCompletedRide never cancels the transport.
evidence:
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:332-346 primeResume only `if (surface == RestoredSurface.waiting)` and `snapshot.status.isMatched`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:216-226 unprimed subscribe: `lastStatus = RideStatus.findingDriver; ... _armAssignment(rideId);`
ride_completed.dart:131-136 events with `!status.isCompletedSurface` are ignored
failure_scenario: Demo: the rider reloads right after 'Trip complete' appears, before payment settles. The restored summary sits at tripCompleted with no rating control for about 1.5 minutes while the mock re-runs a search and a trip in the background.
suggested_fix: For a completed-surface restore, prime the mock to resume the post-trip flow (_startPostTripFlow from the stored stage), or have RideCompleted use a resync that never restarts dispatch.

title: Bootstrap's own outbox flush races the restore's queued-cancel check; if it wins, a ride the rider cancelled is restored as live
description: bootstrap fires `unawaited(FindingDriverController.flushPendingCancels())` before runApp. _flushPendingCancels sends the queued cancel and then calls `PendingCancelStore.remove(cancel.rideId)`. The gate's root() runs later, on the first frame: it reads the snapshot and only then asks `_pendingCancel(id)`. If the flush has already removed the entry, `queued == null` and _dropIfCancelQueued returns the snapshot unchanged. The RC-03 path that archives and clears is skipped, and the cancelled ride is restored as Finding. With the in-process mock (zero latency, a 404 answered as 'gone') the flush can finish before the first frame. The restored Finding's mock transport then assigns a driver to the cancelled ride. With ApiRideRealtime the ride later reaches cancelledByRider through _completeTerminal, which does not archive cancelledByRider, so History loses it.
evidence:
bootstrap.dart:131 `unawaited(FindingDriverController.flushPendingCancels());`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1498 `await PendingCancelStore.remove(cancel.rideId);`
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:124-130 `queued = await _pendingCancel(id); ... if (queued == null) return snapshot;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1027-1034 cancelledByRider not in the archive list
failure_scenario: The rider taps Cancel request and the tab reloads while the cancel is still in the outbox. The launch flush sends it and removes the entry before the gate reads it. The app reopens on 'Finding a driver' for the cancelled ride (demo: a driver is assigned 25 s later), and the cancelled ride never reaches History.
suggested_fix: Have root() use the launch flush's result map (await the in-flight flush and check results[rideId]) instead of re-reading the outbox, or move the bootstrap flush after the first root() resolves.

title: 'Driver has arrived' modal pops up again after every reload during the waiting stage
description: _maybeAnnounceArrival is documented as 'say it once and never again for this ride', but `_arrivalAnnounced` lives only in State memory. A restored Waiting starts tracking at driverWaiting (via _knownStatus). The first live tick passes `_tracking.status == RideStatus.driverWaiting`, so the arrived sheet opens again on top of the restored screen, even though the rider already dismissed it before the reload.
evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:447-463 `/// ... say it once and never again for this ride.` ... `if (!explicitArrival && _tracking.status != RideStatus.driverWaiting) return; _arrivalAnnounced = true;`
failure_scenario: The driver arrives, and the rider dismisses the arrived sheet and walks out. The phone browser reloads. The 'Your driver has arrived' sheet opens again over Waiting, and again after each later reload.
suggested_fix: Persist the announced flag per rideId (for example in the snapshot or session storage) and check it before showing the sheet.

title: Wallet-paid ride: a cheaper route change is refunded to the wallet twice (credited now and again at completion)
description: When a route change makes the trip cheaper and the rider keeps the default 'Movera Wallet' refund, `_creditWallet` credits `-quote.differenceKr` to the local wallet ledger straight away. `apply` has already saved the snapshot with the new, lower `price`. When the trip completes, `WalletController.chargeCompletedRide` debits a wallet-paid ride for `snapshot.price`, which is already the reduced fare. So the reduction is counted twice: once as the wallet credit and once because the debit is smaller. The 'use wallet first' split has the same problem when the new fare is below `walletAmountMinor`, because the debit is `min(walletAmountMinor, fare)`.
failure_scenario: Wallet ride booked at 300 kr. In the trip the rider removes a stop and the new price is 250 kr. Refund goes to Wallet, so +50 kr is credited now. At completion the wallet is debited 250 kr. In total the wallet pays 200 kr for a 250 kr trip.
suggested_fix: For wallet-paid rides, do not credit the wallet locally, or charge the booked price minus the refunds already credited at completion. One ledger rule must own the difference.

title: Route-change pricing starts from the pre-offer booked fare, so the rider's accepted offer raise is silently refunded
description: `_routeChangePricing` builds the new total from `_bookedMinor(ride)`, the fare at booking before offers (`bookedFare` is never updated). The difference is then taken against the current `fare`, which includes `offerIncrease` (PATCH sets `_setFare(ride, fare + increase)` at :993). Any route change after a raise therefore drops the raise: it is refunded to the rider and taken away from the driver, who accepted at the raised price. `_setFare(ride, newMinor)` at :893 also overwrites the fare for good.
failure_scenario: Booked at 200 kr. The rider raises the offer by +20 kr (fare 220) and a driver accepts. The rider changes the destination to one 1 km farther: newMinor = 20000 + 1×1200 = 21200. The sheet shows 'New price 212 kr, 8 kr less, returned to Visa', and 8 kr is refunded for a longer trip.
suggested_fix: Price route changes from the current agreed fare (booked + offer increases), or keep the offer increase as its own fare line and add it to newMinor.

title: In-trip map route ignores stops; that stopless route also feeds Ride check, which fires a false 'off route' alert when the driver goes to an added stop
description: During the trip `_routeEndpoints` returns only driver → destination, and `_refreshRoadRoute` asks `roadRoutePolyline(from,to)` for those two points, so the drawn route never passes the rider's stops (the stop markers sit off the line). The same polyline goes to `RideCheckController.setPlannedRoute` through `onTripRoute`. `RideCheckMonitor._offRoute` measures distance only against `_route`; stops are not excluded. After the rider adds a stop more than `offRouteKm` (2 km) from the direct road, a driver correctly heading to the stop triggers an offRoute Ride check card. `replan` on route change resets `_route`, but the next route it gets is again stopless.
failure_scenario: Trip Sergels torg → Odenplan. In the trip the rider adds a stop at Liljeholmen, about 4 km south. The map keeps drawing the line straight to Odenplan. As the driver heads south to the stop, Ride check opens 'Your driver seems off route'.
suggested_fix: Route driver → remaining stops → destination (a waypoint route), and give Ride check that route; or drop the planned route when stops exist and use the per-stop plan only.

title: Mock realtime sends the ETA to the pickup during the trip, so the in-trip 'Arrive by' moves later as the car nears the destination
description: `_emit` attaches `_etaSeconds()` to every event, including the in-trip `tripInProgress` ticks (line 600). `_etaSeconds` always measures from the driver to `_pickupLat/_pickupLng`. `DriverEta.fromFix` prefers a supplied `etaSeconds` over its own destination distance (`seconds = etaSeconds ?? secondsForDistance(distance)`). So `_tripHeadline` shows 'Arrive by now + time back to the pickup', and the destination time pin does the same. A destination change mid-trip has no effect on it. Ride check also seeds `_expectedSeconds` from this value.
failure_scenario: Demo build, 5 km trip. At boarding the sheet shows 'Arrive by <now+20s>'. On the last tick before drop-off it shows 'Arrive by <now+~8 min>' (about 4.2 km back to the pickup at 8.3 m/s), the opposite of the real progress.
suggested_fix: While on board, measure to the destination (through the remaining stops) in `_etaSeconds`, or send no etaSeconds so DriverEta uses the destination distance.

title: A stop picked on the map or from a suggestion loses its coordinates and is forward-geocoded from its label (in demo: a made-up point)
description: In the route picker, choosing a stop keeps only the text: `_choose` in the 'stop' branch drops `point`. `openRouteChange` also passes `selection.stops` to `preview` without any `stopPoints`. `preview` then geocodes each new stop by its label. The mock geocoder returns a hash-derived point within about ±6/±8 km of Stockholm Central for any label that is not a demo place. A map-pick label ('Pickup location' fallback, a reverse-geocoded street) can also fail with 'Address not found'. That wrong point is priced (25 kr + km), saved, drawn and sent to the driver.
evidence:
route_change_flow.dart:91-97 changes.preview(..., destinationPoint: selection.destinationPoint, stops: selection.stops,  // no stopPoints
route_picker_page.dart:376-378 } else if (_active == 'stop') { setState(() => _activeController.text = _show(address)); ... return;   // point ignored
route_change_controller.dart:180-183 (i < stopPoints.length ? stopPoints[i] : null) ?? (known ...) ?? await _locate(address);
in_process_mock_client.dart:363-370 deterministic made-up latitude/longitude for unknown queries
failure_scenario: In the trip the rider taps Add stop, uses 'Pick on map' and drops the pin at a friend's door. The confirmed label is re-geocoded, the stop lands several km away, and the price, the orange stop marker and the driver's stop all point to the wrong place.
suggested_fix: Keep a point per stop in RoutePickerSelection (as for pickup/destination) and pass them as `stopPoints` to preview.

title: A destination or pickup moved on the map is discarded when its label matches the current address; the rider is told the route was updated
description: `preview` picks the coordinates by comparing the address string: if the new destination text equals `ride.destinationAddress`, it uses the old point and ignores the `destinationPoint` the picker passed. The pickup is handled the same way at :153. ConfirmPickupSpot often returns the same label after a pin move: it keeps `initialAddress` until the reverse geocode settles, a nearby pin resolves to the same street address, and an unresolvable point gives the 'Pickup location' fallback. In those cases the moved point is thrown away, the server prices and applies the old route ('Same price'), and Waiting shows 'Route updated · driver told'.
evidence:
route_change_controller.dart:172-174
    final destinationAt = destination == ride.destinationAddress
        ? GeoPoint(ride.destinationLat, ride.destinationLng)
        : destinationPoint ?? await _locate(destination);
:153-155 same for pickupAt
confirm_pickup_spot.dart:134 _address = widget.initialAddress; :300 confirmedPickupAddress(_address, position)
failure_scenario: Destination 'Mall of Scandinavia'. The rider opens 'Pick on map', drags the pin 400 m to the other entrance and confirms before the label changes (or it resolves to the same name). The sheet shows 'Same price', the rider confirms and gets 'Route updated, driver told', but the destination coordinates did not change.
suggested_fix: Use the explicit point whenever one was given (`destinationPoint ?? (same label ? old point : locate)`), and the same for pickup.

title: Change route is offered on scheduled live rides (device-only reservation id), but every attempt ends in 'route update failed'
description: ReservationLiveRide reuses WaitingForDriver with `rideId: ride.reservationId` and `persistRideSnapshot: false`. Reservations are device-only: the local repository makes the ids, and no `/api/v1/rides` record exists. `_routeEditable` does not consider this, so the three-dots action and the cancel sheet's 'change destination instead' both open the route picker. `_currentRide()` finds no stored snapshot and builds one with the reservation id. `preview` POSTs `/api/v1/rides/<reservationId>/route-quote`, the mock answers 404 `not_found`, and `_send` maps that to `RouteChangeFailure.network`.
evidence:
reservation_live_ride.dart:75-77 rideId: ride.reservationId, realtime: realtime, persistRideSnapshot: false,
waiting_for_driver.dart:1004 bool get _routeEditable => !_tracking.status.isTerminal && !_completedOpened;
:1032-1046 return RideSnapshot(... rideId: rideId, ...)
route_change_controller.dart:201 '/api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote'
:348 _ => RouteChangeFailure.network,
failure_scenario: A scheduled ride starts and the driver is on the way. The rider taps the ride card's More, picks a new destination and taps 'See new price'. The result is always the 'Couldn't update the route' snackbar; the rider can never change it, even though the screen offers it.
suggested_fix: Hide or disable route editing when `widget.persistRideSnapshot` is false or a custom realtime/onCancel is supplied, or route reservation changes through ReservationController.

title: Q40 pickup-move limit is measured from the current pickup, so repeated small moves take the pickup any distance after accept
description: After accept, the pickup may move only `maxPickupMoveMeters`. Both the client (`preview`: `ride.pickupLat` vs the new point) and the server (`_pickupMoveMeters`: `ride['pickupLat']` vs the body) measure from the pickup as it stands now, and each applied change overwrites it. The pickup the driver accepted is never kept, so repeating the change moves the pickup by the limit each time with no total cap.
failure_scenario: With a 300 m limit and the driver on the way, the rider moves the pickup 290 m four times in a row. Each move is accepted, and the driver is sent about 1.2 km from the accepted pickup without the 'that's a new ride' refusal.
suggested_fix: Store the pickup at accept (`acceptedPickupLat/Lng`) and measure every later move from it, on both client and server.

title: Pre-trip 'Arrive by' destination pin ignores the stops the rider added
description: Before boarding, `_syncTimePins` computes the arrival as now + minutes to pickup + `estimatedTripMinutes(pickup, destination)`, a straight pickup-to-destination estimate. `widget.stops` is not used, so adding a stop (or several) never moves the shown arrival time.
evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:2228-2243 now.add(Duration(minutes: toPickupMin + estimatedTripMinutes(GeoPoint(widget.pickupPosition...), GeoPoint(widget.destinationPosition...))))
failure_scenario: While the driver is on the way, the rider adds a stop 5 km off the direct line. The 'Arrive by 08:19' pin over the destination stays at 08:19.
suggested_fix: Sum the estimate over pickup → stops → destination.

title: Sheet and confirmation show a locally computed difference, not the server's differenceMinor that is actually charged or refunded
description: `differenceKr` is `newPriceKr - oldPriceKr`, where `oldPriceKr` is the device's `_price`. The server charges `differenceMinor = newMinor - current fare`. The client parses that value into `quote.differenceMinor` but never shows it, and `showRouteUpdated` uses `updated.price - ride.price` as well. When the device price lags the server, the rider is shown a wrong charge. This happens when a PATCH reached the server but its response was lost: `_send` reports `network`, Waiting keeps the old route and price, and it never reads the route back from the projection.
evidence:
route_change_controller.dart:66 double get differenceKr => newPriceKr - oldPriceKr;
:213 oldPriceKr: ride.price,
waiting_for_driver.dart:1091 differenceKr: updated.price - ride.price,
in_process_mock_client.dart:2091 'differenceMinor': newMinor - currentMinor,
failure_scenario: A first destination change times out on the client after the server applied it and captured +49 kr. The rider sees 'Couldn't update route' and tries again. The second quote's sheet says '+49 kr charged now to Visa' and the snackbar repeats it, but the server's difference is 0 and nothing is charged.
suggested_fix: Show `quote.differenceMinor` (the server's), and after a lost PATCH response re-read the trip projection before offering another change.

title: Reconnect flush sends a queued Finding cancel to a ride a driver accepted during the outage, after Finding told the rider it was not cancelled
description: RC-03 says that when a driver accepts before a queued cancel reaches the server, the match wins: `_completeAssigned` removes the outbox entry and tells the rider 'A driver already accepted your ride, so it wasn't cancelled'. The reconnect flush follows a different rule. `_rereadForReplay` asks `TripStateMachine.apply(status, 'cancel', rider)`, and rider `cancel` is allowed from accepted/driver_to_pickup/arrived (trip_transitions.dart:101), so it sends the cancel. On reconnect the flush wins the race. In `ApiRideRealtime._poll` the accepted event is added to an async broadcast controller (line 227) and then `connection.markConnected()` runs (line 256). The `states` stream is `sync: true`, so the watcher (lines 1434-1438) starts `_flushPendingCancels` at once, and it reads the outbox (`PendingCancelStore.all()`, line 1458) before Finding's listener runs `_completeAssigned` and its unawaited `PendingCancelStore.remove`. Both chains go through the same number of `await SharedPreferences.getInstance()` hops, and the flush started first, so it reads the entry before it is removed. The trip version moved with the accept, so `forVersion` mints a new key and `PendingCancelStore.add(cancel)` (line 1477) writes back the entry Finding just deleted. Then it POSTs `/cancel`. Even if that POST fails, the re-added entry will cancel the matched ride on a later reconnect or launch.
failure_scenario: Release build. Rider is on Finding and the network drops. They tap Cancel request, get 'We'll cancel your ride as soon as you're back online', and the ride stays live with the cancel queued. During the outage a driver accepts. When the network returns, the first successful poll brings `accepted`. Finding shows 'A driver already accepted your ride, so it wasn't cancelled' and opens Waiting with the driver. Meanwhile the flush has re-read the trip (accepted, cancel applies) and POSTs /cancel. The server cancels the matched ride, Waiting gets cancelledByRider, and the rider is sent Home. The driver who was heading to them is cancelled on. Worked out by reading the microtask order, not by running it.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:947-958 `if (_cancelQueued) { // RC-03: a driver accepted before the queued cancel reached the server ... the stale request leaves the outbox so it cannot cancel the matched ride later. _cancelQueued = false; ... unawaited(PendingCancelStore.remove(id)); ... _onCancelRefused?.call(); }`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1458 `final pending = await PendingCancelStore.all();`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1473-1477 `if (version != null && version != cancel.expectedVersion) { cancel = cancel.forVersion(version); await PendingCancelStore.add(cancel); }`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1559-1565 `final applies = TripStateMachine.apply(status, command, TripActor.rider, ...) != null;`
api_ride_realtime.dart:227 `poll.controller?.add(RideRealtimeEvent(` ... 256 `connection.markConnected();`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1434-1438 `_reconnectFlush = connection.states.listen((state) { if (state == RealtimeState.connected) { if (wasDown) { ... unawaited(flushPendingCancels(...`
suggested_fix: Decide once whether a match overrides a queued search cancel. If it does (RC-03), store the stage the cancel was queued in (for example `queuedWhileSearching`) and have `_rereadForReplay` return `stale` for such an entry when the trip is already matched. Never re-add an entry in the flush after re-reading: compare-and-set against the stored list, or skip `add` when the entry no longer exists.

title: A booking that may have been created is not checked against the server before a retry gets a fresh key, so a retry books a second live ride
description: RC-09 accepts that a timeout, dropped connection or 5xx may still have created the ride. `_sendOrRecover` recovers only inside the same call (one replay plus `GET /rider/trips/active`), and when the network is down that recovery fails too. The rider is then told `bookingUncertain` ('Check your connection and try again'). The kept `BookingAttempt` is reused only when the next intent matches exactly and less than 5 minutes have passed since the first tap (`matches` uses `startedAt`). The intent includes pickup and destination rounded to 1e-4 degrees, so a pin a metre away across a cell edge, a GPS-preselected pickup that moved, or a retry after 5 minutes all produce a new `BookingAttempt` with a new idempotency key. Nothing calls `_adoptActiveTrip` or `fetchActive` before that new key is sent. The server has no one-live-trip rule (the mock `POST /rides` just creates another ride, and the contract defines none). So the ghost ride from the first attempt stays live on the server with no screen watching it, and a second ride is created.
failure_scenario: Rider taps Book now. The POST reaches the server and creates ride R1, then the connection drops before the answer arrives. The replay and the active-trip lookup also fail offline, and the rider sees 'We couldn't confirm your booking. Check your connection and try again.' The network comes back after 5 minutes, and the rider taps Book now again (or after 10 seconds, with the pickup pin re-confirmed a few metres away). `_attemptFor` creates a new attempt with a new key, `POST /rides` creates R2, and Finding opens for R2. R1 is still searching on the server and can be matched with a second driver. Two rides are booked. Traced by hand through booking_coordinator.dart, booking_attempt.dart and the in-process mock.
evidence:
booking_attempt.dart:31-33 `bool matches(String otherIntentKey, {DateTime? now}) => intentKey == otherIntentKey && (now ?? DateTime.now()).difference(startedAt) < reuseWindow;`
booking_coordinator.dart:52-58 `if (current != null && current.matches(intentKey)) return current; final next = BookingAttempt(intentKey: intentKey); _attempt = next;`
booking_coordinator.dart:208-211 `return [(lat * 1e4).round(), (lng * 1e4).round()];`
booking_coordinator.dart:451-453 `final adopted = await _adoptActiveTrip(destinationLat, destinationLng); if (adopted != null) return adopted; rethrow;`
in_process_mock_client.dart:597-610 `} else if (path == '/api/v1/rides' && method == 'POST') { ... final ride = _ride(body, requestId); rides[ride['id'] as String] = ride;`
suggested_fix: When the previous attempt ended 'maybe created' (an attempt with a replay that never succeeded or was refused), call `_adoptActiveTrip`/`fetchActive` before minting a new key for any intent, and adopt or block if the server already has a live trip. Alternatively keep the uncertain key until the server has been asked.

title: A queued search cancel is never retried while the connection stays up, so the rider stays on 'Cancelling…' and is told they are offline
description: `_requestServerCancel` tries twice back to back. Any non-permanent error (5xx, 429, a POST-only timeout) returns `queued`. After that only two things send it again: the reconnect watcher, which fires only on a failed/disconnected to connected change, and the Finding listener at line 382, which fires only when an event with a searching status arrives. While a ride is searching its projection does not change, and `ApiRideRealtime` drops the repeated eventId without emitting (lines 125-128). So when GET polls keep succeeding, the connection never leaves `connected`, no event arrives, and the queued cancel just sits there. The search tick is stopped, the copy says 'Cancelling your ride…' and 'We'll confirm it with Movera as soon as you're back online' though the rider is online. If a driver accepts meanwhile, the rider is told 'A driver already accepted your ride, so it wasn't cancelled', even though the cancel was never sent again. Waiting's `pendingRetry` (active_ride_controller.dart:273) has the same gap. The immediate second try also ignores a 429 `Retry-After`.
failure_scenario: Rider on Finding taps Cancel request. POST /cancel returns 500 twice (a transient backend fault) while GET /rides/{id} keeps working. The result is `queued`, the screen shows 'Cancelling your ride… We'll confirm it with Movera as soon as you're back online', and nothing is sent again. After about 25 s a driver accepts. The rider is moved to Waiting and told the ride wasn't cancelled, though no retry was ever made. Traced by reading the code.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:1182-1216 `for (var attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt += 1) { try { ... } catch (error) { ... if (isPermanentCancelFailure(error)) {...} } } // Still unreachable ... return SearchCancelResult.queued;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:382 `if (_cancelQueued && event.status.isSearching) _flushQueuedCancel();`
api_ride_realtime.dart:125-128 `if (eventId != null && poll.seenEventIds.contains(eventId)) { connection.markConnected(); return; }`
finding_driver_controller.dart:1440-1443 `} else if (state == RealtimeState.failed || state == RealtimeState.disconnected || state == RealtimeState.reconnecting) { wasDown = true; }`
suggested_fix: While `_cancelQueued` is set, schedule a backoff timer that calls `_flushQueuedCancel` (respecting `retryAfter`), independent of connection state changes. Tell the rider 'server problem' rather than 'offline' when the kind is `serverTrouble` or `rateLimited`.

title: 'Try again' after no driver found reports a may-have-booked failure as a plain failure and sends the rider Home while the new ride may exist
description: `_requestAgain` catches every error with `rebookFailed` ('We couldn't request a new ride. Choose your route and try again.') and returns false, and `_handleTerminal` then goes Home. It never checks `BookingController.mayHaveBooked(error)`, which Select Ride uses (RC-09) for exactly this case. A timeout or dropped connection after the POST may have created the ride. The rider is told it failed and is told to rebook from Home, so the ghost ride stays live with no screen. If the rider rebooks with any different intent, that books a second ride (see the BookingAttempt finding).
failure_scenario: The search ends with no driver found and the rider taps Try again. The POST /rides creates the ride but the connection drops before the answer. The replay and adopt fail, and the rider sees 'We couldn't request a new ride. Choose your route and try again.' and lands on Home. The server ride keeps searching, may be matched with a driver who comes to an empty pickup, or the rider books again and has two rides. Traced by reading the code.
evidence:
finding_drivers.dart:370-375 `} catch (_) { _showCancelNotice( L10n.current.rebookFailed, ); return false; }`
finding_drivers.dart:340-344 `if (choice == NoDriverChoice.tryAgain && await _requestAgain(ended)) { return; } if (!mounted) return; RideNavigator.home(context, status: status);`
select_ride.dart:1558 `final uncertain = BookingController.mayHaveBooked(error);`
suggested_fix: When `BookingController.mayHaveBooked(error)` is true, show `bookingUncertain`, stay on the screen, and try `fetchActive` to adopt the ride (or offer Retry, which reuses the same attempt) instead of sending the rider Home.

title: Ride check 'long stop' fires when the rider's own connection drops mid-trip, because `connectionDegraded` is never set on the polling transport
description: The 15-second stillness timer is meant to run only 'while the trip is under way and the live feed is up', and it uses `_tracking.connectionDegraded` as that check. `DriverTrackingController` sets that flag only from the stream's `onError`/`onDone`. `ApiRideRealtime._poll` never adds an error to the stream: a failed poll only calls `connection.markFailed()` and backs off. So when the rider's phone loses network during the trip, no new fixes arrive, `connectionDegraded` stays false, and `RideCheckMonitor.checkStill(now)` measures the time since the last fix as a stop. After admin's `longStop` minutes (4 by default) it opens the 'long stop' Ride check card, though the car may be driving normally.
failure_scenario: Release build, trip in progress. The rider's phone loses network for 5 minutes, for example in a tunnel or a dead zone, while the car keeps moving. About 4 minutes after the last fix the Ride check card opens asking whether everything is OK because the car 'stopped for 4 minutes'. The rider is alarmed by a false alert, and an answer may be posted to admin's Ride check log. Traced by reading the code.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:1105-1115 `/// ... While the trip is under way and the live feed is up, check the long stop against the clock as well.` ... `if (!mounted || _tracking.connectionDegraded) return; if (!DriverEta.isInTrip(_tracking.status)) return; RideCheckController.shared.checkStill(rideId);`
driver_tracking_controller.dart:186-193 `onError: (Object error) { connectionDegraded = true; ...}, onDone: () { connectionDegraded = true; ...}`
api_ride_realtime.dart:257-272 `} catch (error) { ... connection.markFailed(); ... poll.retryAt = _clock().add(connection.nextBackoff()); }`
ride_check_monitor.dart:188-197 `RideCheckDetection? checkStill(DateTime now) { ... return _stoppedFor(anchor, now.difference(since)); }`
suggested_fix: Also skip `checkStill` while `AppScope.instance.realtime.state != RealtimeState.connected`, or have the poller mark the tracking feed degraded on failure. Reset the still anchor when the feed returns.

title: A retry within 5 minutes resends the first quote while Finding and the snapshot show the newly confirmed price; an expired first quote fails the retry with 'Check the fare'
description: After a may-have-booked failure, Select Ride makes the rider go through Set pickup again and books with a fresh quote (`_quoteAfterPickup`, possibly after `_acceptNewPrice`). `_prepareFinding` then ignores that quote: with `attempt.replay != null` it resends the first body (RC-04), with the old quote, fare and wallet split. Select Ride still opens Finding with `price: authoritativePrice`, `currency: quote.currency` and `walletAmountMinor: walletSplit.walletMinor` from the new quote, and `FindingDriverController.startFrom` writes that price into its `_snapshot`, which later saves overwrite into the store. So the fare shown on Finding and Waiting is not the fare the server booked. If the first quote has expired (quotes last 2 minutes and the window is 5), the replay is refused with 409 quote_expired and the rider gets `bookingFailed` ('We could not book this ride. Check the fare and try again.') for a fare they had just confirmed.
failure_scenario: First Book now with quote Q1 at kr 259 fails offline. Ninety seconds later the rider retries, Set pickup reprices to kr 279 (Q2), and the rider accepts the new price. The coordinator replays Q1, so the server books kr 259 while Finding and Waiting show kr 279 and the new wallet split. Or, 3 minutes later, the replay of the expired Q1 is refused and the rider sees 'We could not book this ride. Check the fare and try again.', and must tap again. Traced by reading the code.
evidence:
booking_coordinator.dart:358-361 `final replay = attempt.replay; String id; if (replay != null) { id = await _sendOrRecover(attempt, replay, destinationLat, destinationLng);`
booking_coordinator.dart:628-630 `// A replay may carry a quote that expired meanwhile ... (!isReplay && !quoteExpiresAt.isAfter(DateTime.now()))`
select_ride.dart:1539-1545 `price: authoritativePrice, ... quoteId: quote.id, ...` and 1613-1616 `price: authoritativePrice, currency: quote.currency, paymentMethod: payment.name, walletAmountMinor: walletSplit.walletMinor,`
suggested_fix: Return the replayed booking's fare and wallet part from `submitFinding` (or read them from the saved snapshot) and open Finding with those values. If the first attempt's quote has expired, ask the server (`fetchActive`) before replaying, and reset the attempt when no ride exists.

title: An offer raise whose answer was lost is shown as failed, and the screen never picks up the higher fare the server applied
description: A timeout or dropped connection on `PATCH /rides/{id}` with `offerIncrease` sets `editFeedback` to 'Couldn't update offer. Try again.' and leaves `_snapshot.price` unchanged. If the server applied the raise, nothing ever corrects the price: realtime events carry no fare, and `checkServerSearchState` reads only the status. Finding and then Waiting (`price: _match.currentPrice`) keep showing the old fare, while the trip is priced at the raised fare. A retry with the same amount reuses the key and fixes it, but a rider who takes 'failed' at its word does not retry.
failure_scenario: Rider raises the offer by kr 20 and the PATCH times out after the server applied it. The rider sees 'Couldn't update offer', the screen shows kr 259, the driver accepts at kr 279, and the rider is charged kr 279 at the end. Traced by reading the code.
evidence:
finding_driver_controller.dart:875-878 `} catch (error) { editFeedback = _staleEdit(error, _priceMutation) ? rideJustChangedMessage : L10n.current.editOfferFailed;`
finding_driver_controller.dart:510-515 `final raw = tripProjectionOf(json); ... final status = RideStatusWire.fromProjection(raw); if (status == null || status.isSearching) return;`
suggested_fix: On a retryable error (`ApiError.isRetryable` or `ClientException`), say the result is unconfirmed and re-read `GET /rides/{id}` to adopt the server's `fare` into the snapshot.

title: A route change whose answer was lost is reported as 'Couldn't update the route' and Waiting keeps the old route, though the server and the driver have the new one
description: `apply` maps any non-ApiError (ClientException) and any retryable ApiError (TIMEOUT, NETWORK, 5xx) to `RouteChangeFailure.network`. Waiting's snapshot, map, destination and price stay as before. The PATCH may have been applied: the server changed the destination, notified the driver and charged the difference. Realtime projections are never read for the route, so Waiting keeps showing the old destination and price for the rest of the ride unless the rider retries.
failure_scenario: In trip, the rider changes the destination and confirms +kr 60. The PATCH lands but the response is lost, and the rider sees 'Couldn't update the route. Try again.' and closes the picker. The driver drives to the new destination and the card is charged kr 60, while the rider's map and price still show the old trip. Traced by reading the code.
evidence:
route_change_controller.dart:339-351 `throw RouteChangeException(switch (error.detail) { ... _ => RouteChangeFailure.network, }); } catch (_) { throw const RouteChangeException(RouteChangeFailure.network); }`
route_change_flow.dart:118-122 `} on RouteChangeException catch (error) { messenger ... showSnackBar(SnackBar(content: Text(error.message))); return null; }`
suggested_fix: For a retryable apply failure, re-send the same request (the key is stable) or re-read the projection and adopt the server's route and fare before telling the rider it failed.

title: The duplicate-ride stand-down cancel is sent once and never queued, so a failure leaves two live rides
description: When a booking response arrives while another Finding owns a ride, `_standDownIfFindingOwned` POSTs `/cancel` for the duplicate directly. It does not go through the pending-cancel outbox. If that POST fails (offline or 5xx), the exception escapes `_submitFinding`. `_sendOrRecover` treats it as may-have-booked and replays, the replay hits the same stand-down, and the error finally reaches Select Ride as `bookingUncertain`. Nothing remembers that the duplicate must be cancelled, so it stays live on the server. Long network stalls on Book now (up to 15 s plus 15 s plus a 30 s GET) widen the window for this race.
failure_scenario: A Book now request is stuck on a flaky network. Meanwhile another Finding for a different ride becomes active (restore or push). The booking response arrives and the stand-down cancel fails on the same bad network. The rider sees 'couldn't confirm your booking' while two rides are live on the server. Traced by reading the code.
evidence: booking_coordinator.dart:774-782 `// The race-losing backend ride must be explicitly stood down; never leave two live rides. final cancelIntent = createdRideId; await _client.post('/api/v1/rides/$createdRideId/cancel', ... idempotencyKey: _duplicateCancelMutation.keyFor(cancelIntent),);`
suggested_fix: Enqueue the stand-down through `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` before sending, so the outbox flush retries it, and do not treat the stand-down's failure as a booking failure.

title: The completion screen ignores paymentFailed, so a declined card shows 'Payment processing' until the rider taps Done, and the trip is filed as Completed
description: Release realtime is ApiRideRealtime. A card declined at the end of a trip arrives as status completed plus paymentStatus failed. RideStatusWire._afterCompletion (core/contracts/trip_status.dart:183) maps that to RideStatus.paymentFailed. paymentFailed is isTerminal but not isCompletedSurface (core/contracts/ride_status.dart:65,85). Once Waiting has pushed RideCompleted, its tracker is disposed, and RideCompleted's own subscription is the only listener. That listener throws away every event whose status is not a completion surface. The decline is never reconciled into RideSession, never persisted and never shown. _CompletionSpec has no paymentFailed case, and the paymentFailed terminal sheet in ride_terminal_state_sheet.dart:287 is only reachable from Waiting. The rider stays on 'Trip complete / Payment processing' with rating locked ('rating after payment'). Done then runs closeCompletedRide: OnDemandRideHistoryStore.archive gets the snapshot status (paymentProcessing, a completion surface), so History lists the trip as Completed, and the session moves to closed. The payment is still outstanding and nothing tells the rider. Handoff race: if the decline lands while Waiting parks the map (active_ride_controller markCompleted, then waiting_for_driver.dart:717), the tracker has already set the session to paymentFailed. RideCompleted's initState accepts only completion-surface session statuses (line 114), so it starts at tripCompleted. Done then calls localTransition(closed) from the terminal paymentFailed, transitionRide throws InvalidRideTransition, and the rider is trapped on 'feedback could not be saved'.
failure_scenario: Release build. A rider pays with a card. The trip completes, RideCompleted opens, the server reports payment authorized (Payment processing), then the card is declined (paymentStatus failed). The screen stays on 'Payment processing' indefinitely, and the decline also survives a reload because the snapshot keeps paymentProcessing. The rider taps Done, History shows the ride as Completed, and the rider gets no 'payment could not be completed / review your payment method' message. If the decline arrives during the Waiting-to-Completed handoff, Done instead fails with 'feedback could not be saved' every time.
suggested_fix: Handle paymentFailed (and other terminal non-completion statuses) in the RideCompleted listener and in initState's session check. Reconcile it into RideSession, persist it, and show the payment-failed state or terminal sheet with a path to change the payment method. In closeCompletedRide, do not call localTransition(closed) when the session is already terminal.

title: In release, the default chosen on the Payments tab is saved only to device prefs and is never sent to the server default that Select Ride reads
description: In release, DI composes defaultPayment = ApiPaymentMethodRepository (di.dart:151-154). Select Ride restores and persists the default through that repository (select_ride.dart:274, then RideSelectionController.restoreDefaultPayment and _persistSelectedBrand), which uses GET/PATCH /api/v1/payment-methods/default. The Payments tab (WalletAndPaymentsScreen, tab 1, reachable from the Home payment tab and the side menu in every build) saves the rider's 'make default' choice through WalletController.savePayments. That call goes to WalletStore.savePayments, which writes only the SharedPreferences key 'movera_default_payment'. The tab also reads its 'Default for rides' tick back from that key (_restorePaymentSettings, line 761). In release nothing else reads that key, so the two screens use different sources of truth.
evidence:
wallet.dart:774-781
  Future<void> _savePaymentSettings() async {
    await _wallet.savePayments(
      WalletPaymentSettings(
        defaultMethod: _selectedMethod, ...
wallet_repository.dart:114  await prefs.setString('movera_default_payment', ...)
di.dart:150-154  if (release) { final methods = ApiPaymentMethodRepository(api: api); payments = methods; defaultPayment = methods; ...
select_ride.dart:274  paymentStore: AppScope.instance.defaultPayment,
failure_scenario: Production build. The rider opens Payments, taps Apple Pay and sees 'Default for rides' on it. They start a booking: Select Ride reads the server's defaultMethodId (for example cash) and preselects Cash. If the rider then picks a method in Select Ride (PATCHed to the server), the Payments tab still marks the old prefs value as the default.
suggested_fix: Have the Payments tab read and write the default through AppScope.instance.defaultPayment (or PaymentRepository.setDefault) instead of WalletStore's private prefs key.

title: A wallet-paid ride is never debited if the rider taps Done before payment is finalized
description: D-022 wallet deduction runs only from _maybeChargeWallet, inside RideCompleted. It fires only once _status reaches paymentFinalized or later (lines 149-158). chargeCompletedRideById is called from nowhere else (grep: ride_completed.dart:163 only). Done is enabled from the first frame, including tripCompleted and paymentProcessing. Tapping it runs closeCompletedRide, which clears the completion snapshot, and dispose cancels the subscription. The later paymentFinalized event therefore never reaches a charging listener, and no restore will bring the screen back because the snapshot is gone. In the demo transport, paymentProcessing comes 500 ms after completion and paymentFinalized 500 ms after that (mock_ride_realtime.dart:32-33), so a quick Done skips the debit. The same applies to the wallet part of a 'use wallet first' split.
failure_scenario: Demo build, wallet balance 300 kr. The rider pays a 129 kr trip with Movera Wallet. The completion screen appears and they tap Done within about one second, while the status is tripCompleted or paymentProcessing. They land on Home and the wallet still shows 300 kr, permanently, so the ride was free.
suggested_fix: Run the wallet debit from a place that outlives the screen, for example the realtime or session layer or closeCompletedRide when the ride is wallet-paid and payment later settles. Alternatively keep listening (or keep the snapshot) until the payment reaches a settled state.

title: A wallet-paid trip that the rider ends early is never debited from the wallet
description: An ended-early trip opens RideCompleted with endedEarly set and persistOnDemandState: false (waiting_for_driver.dart:895-899). initState returns at line 102 before the subscription and before _maybeChargeWallet. _maybeChargeWallet would also bail out on !persistOnDemandState. The server's charged fare (EndedEarlyTrip.charged, shown on the receipt as 'You pay X') is never taken off the local wallet ledger for a wallet-paid ride, and no other code calls chargeCompletedRide/chargeRide. The result is a receipt that says the rider pays X while the wallet balance stays the same.
failure_scenario: Demo build. The rider books with Movera Wallet (balance 200 kr) and ends the trip on board after 3 km. The summary says 'You pay 74 kr'. They tap Done, and the wallet still shows 200 kr.
suggested_fix: When an ended-early trip was paid by wallet (or had a wallet part), debit EndedEarlyTrip.charged (capped at the wallet part) once, using the same chargedRidesKey dedupe.

title: The completion receipt shows the payment method untranslated ('Movera Wallet', 'Card'); only Cash is localized
description: The snapshot stores the English label of the chosen method (RideSelectionRepository: 'Movera Wallet', 'Card'), and TripReceiptRepository.last copies it into TripReceipt.method. The receipt localizes only cash and prints any other value as stored. The helper paymentLabelFor in payments/presentation/payment_labels.dart translates these exact stored names, but the receipt does not use it. This is a different screen from the known History-detail finding (ride_history.dart:552).
evidence:
trip_detail.dart:75-80
  _detailRow(
    context.l10n.paymentMethod,
    L10n.isCashLabel(trip.method)
        ? context.l10n.payCash
        : trip.method,
  ),
ride_selection_repository.dart:171  name: 'Movera Wallet',
payment_labels.dart:307-312 paymentLabelFor maps 'Card' / 'Movera Wallet' to l10n
failure_scenario: App language set to Swedish or French. The rider completes a ride paid with Movera Wallet, and the completion screen's Trip details shows 'Payment method: Movera Wallet' in English.
suggested_fix: Use paymentLabelFor(trip.method) for the receipt row.

title: Book for later lets the rider add stops and charges for them, but the reservation drops the stops
description: `_stopsSupported` is `true`, but its own comment says stops are 'silently dropped — ReservationDraft has no stops' and should stay hidden. The stops the rider types go into `ScheduledRideSession.stops`. From there `openScheduledCategorySelector` passes them to `SelectRide(stops: ...)` (scheduled_category_gate.dart:52). SelectRide quotes the route through those stops: `_loadQuotes` passes `stops:` (select_ride.dart:465-472), and the mock's `_routedMeters` prices pickup → stops → destination. `ScheduledRideCheckout.draftFrom` / `ScheduledRideBooking.confirm` then build a `ReservationDraft` / `ReservationPatch` that has no stops field. The booked price includes the detour, but the stored ride, the Upcoming page, the live ride (`ReservationLiveRide.pageFor` passes no stops) and the driver never see the stops.
failure_scenario: Rider schedules tomorrow 07:15 Home → Stop 'Odenplan' → Arlanda. Select Ride shows and books the price for the longer route through Odenplan. The reservation is saved as Home → Arlanda only. The live trip never goes via Odenplan, and the rider pays for the stop anyway.
evidence:
schedule_ride.dart:50-55 `/// ... stops typed here reached ScheduledRideSession.stops → SelectRide(stops:) and were then silently dropped — ReservationDraft has no stops ... Hidden until ...` / `static const bool _stopsSupported = true;`
scheduled_category_gate.dart:52 `stops: List<String>.from(session.stops),`
select_ride.dart:465-470 `final stops = await _routeStops(); ... await _selection.loadQuotes(stops: stops, ...`
scheduled_ride_checkout.dart:170-184 `return ReservationDraft(scheduledPickupAt: when, ... pickup: pickup, destination: destination, ... price: price ?? ScheduledRideBooking.quotedPrice(selection, ride.id), ...` (no stops)
suggested_fix: Set `_stopsSupported` to false for Book for later, as the comment intends. Otherwise add stops to ReservationDraft/Patch/Reservation and carry them through to the live ride.

title: Scheduled-ride completion screen shows the previous Book Now ride's driver and receipt (or 'unavailable')
description: When a reservation completes, `onCompleted` pushes `RideCompleted(persistOnDemandState: false, ...)`. That screen always renders `RideCompletedDriverInfo` and `RideCompletedTripDetail`. Both read `LastCompletedRide.value` (DriverRepository.current / TripReceiptRepository.last). Only Book Now paths (`ActiveRideController.markCompleted`, `_commitCancelled`, restore) ever call `LastCompletedRide.remember`. A normal Book Now close (`closeCompletedRide`) does not clear it. So the reservation's own driver, addresses, price and payment are never shown. The screen shows the last Book Now ride of the session instead, or the 'details unavailable' empty states. The tip options (`_tripCurrency`) also come from that stale ride.
failure_scenario: Rider takes a Book Now ride Slussen → Kista (kr 189, driver Ali) in the morning. Later the scheduled 23:50 ride Home → Arlanda (kr 450, driver Erik) completes. The completion screen says driver Ali, Slussen → Kista, total kr 189. With no earlier Book Now ride, it shows 'Driver details unavailable' / 'Trip details unavailable' for a ride that just finished.
evidence:
reservation_live_ride.dart:102-109 `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement(RideStageTransition(RideCompleted(status: status, rideId: ride.reservationId, realtime: completionRealtime, persistOnDemandState: false, feedbackAvailableOnCompletion: true, ...`
ride_completed.dart:387-391 `child: const RideCompletedDriverInfo(), ... child: RideCompletedTripDetail(controller: _controller, ...`
driver_repository.dart:106 `final ride = LastCompletedRide.value;` (also :40 for the driver)
active_ride_controller.dart:105-108 LastCompletedRide.clear() only in leaveEndedEarlySummary
suggested_fix: Before opening RideCompleted for a reservation, build a RideSnapshot from the Reservation and call LastCompletedRide.remember. Or pass the receipt/driver explicitly to RideCompleted.

title: Rating or tipping a completed scheduled ride always fails: feedback is posted to a ride id the server never had
description: The reservation completion screen turns on rating (`feedbackAvailableOnCompletion: true`, so `canRate` is true at tripCompleted). On Done, `_leave` calls `_controller.submitFeedback(rideId: <reservationId>)`, which POSTs `/api/v1/rides/rsv_.../feedback`. Reservations are device-only (`LocalReservationRepository`; API_V1_MOCK: 'Reservations themselves stay device-only'), so the mock's `rides[parts[4]]` is null and it answers 404. ApiClient throws, `_leave` catches it and shows 'feedback could not be saved', and the rider stays on the screen. Done can never succeed while a star or tip is selected. The only way out is back plus 'Leave without sending'.
failure_scenario: The scheduled ride finishes. The rider taps 5 stars and kr 20 tip, then Done. The request returns 404 NOT_FOUND, the screen shows the feedback error and stays. Each retry fails the same way. The rating and tip are lost.
evidence:
reservation_live_ride.dart:108-109 `persistOnDemandState: false, feedbackAvailableOnCompletion: true,`
ride_completed.dart:236 `await _controller.submitFeedback(rideId: id, ...`
ride_feedback_repository.dart:29-30 `await _api.post('/api/v1/rides/${Uri.encodeComponent(rideId)}/feedback', ...`
in_process_mock_client.dart:617-621 `final ride = rides[parts[4]]; ... if (ride == null) { status = 404; payload = _error('not_found', requestId);`
suggested_fix: Do not offer feedback for device-only reservations (feedbackAvailableOnCompletion false). Or store the rating locally on the reservation until a server reservation resource exists.

title: Cancel confirmed on a stale ride overwrites a ride that already went live or completed, and records a late fee
description: `_cancel(ride)` uses the `ride` captured at build time and works out `terms` before the two cancel sheets open. After the sheets it calls `_reservations.cancel(...)` without re-reading the ride or checking `status.canCancel`. `LocalReservationRepository.cancelReservation` has no status guard either: it always sets `status: cancelled`, `cancellationActor: rider`, `cancelledAt` and the fee. While the sheets are open, the Home chrono tick keeps running `startLiveIfDue`, which moves the ride driverAssigned → driverEnRoute, and the mock trip then runs to completed in about 46 s. `_handoffIfLive` does not fire because the page route is not current while a sheet is up.
failure_scenario: At 23:47 the rider opens Cancel on the 23:50 ride and lingers on the reason sheet. At 23:48 the ride goes en route, and about 46 s later it is completed. The rider then taps a reason. The completed ride is rewritten as cancelled by the rider with a 'Cancelled · fee kr 50' chip. It moves from History › Completed to Cancelled, and a fee is recorded for a trip that was delivered.
evidence:
upcoming_reservation.dart:131-142 `final terms = _reservations.cancelTermsFor(ride); final outcome = await showCancelReservationFlow(context, ride, terms: terms); if (!outcome.cancelled) return; await _reservations.cancel(ride.reservationId, reason: outcome.reasonId, fee: terms.fee);`
local_reservation_repository.dart:227-234 `final current = _require(reservationId); final next = current.copyWith(status: ReservationStatus.cancelled, ... cancellationFee: fee != null && fee.isPositive ? fee : null);`
suggested_fix: In cancelReservation (or the controller), re-read the ride and refuse when `!current.status.canCancel`. In the page, re-read `byId` after the sheets and abort when the status changed.

title: Queued dispatch/lifecycle writes resurrect a ride the rider just cancelled (no status check inside the serialized change)
description: `_oneAtATime` serializes changes, but each change re-applies a status decided from an older snapshot. `startLiveIfDue` picks `ride` from `upcoming()` before its awaits, then calls `_store.assignDriver(id)` (→ driverAssignmentPending/driverAssigned) or `_store.updateReservation(... driverEnRoute)`. The mock trip's writeStep checks `current.status != from` synchronously and then queues `update(id, ReservationPatch(status: to))`. If a rider cancel is already queued in `_oneAtATime` (its prefs write in flight), these later changes run after it. Neither `assignDriver` nor `updateReservation` checks that the ride is still upcoming, so a cancelled ride gets its status overwritten. `cancellationActor`, `cancelledAt` and `cancellationFee` stay set.
failure_scenario: On the live scheduled ride the rider taps Cancel at the moment the 20 s 'arrived' timer fires. writeStep sees driverEnRoute (the cancel is not committed yet) and queues driverEnRoute→driverArrived behind the cancel. The cancel commits, then the update sets driverArrived. The ride is 'upcoming' again, the trip continues to completed, and the rider was already sent Home.
evidence:
local_reservation_repository.dart:266-287 `final current = _require(reservationId); ... : current.copyWith(status: ReservationStatus.driverAssigned, driver: driver, ...); await _commit(...)` (no isUpcoming check); :193-214 updateReservation likewise.
reservation_controller.dart:405-408 `if (current == null || current.status != from || current.driver == null) { return false; } await update(id, ReservationPatch(status: to));`
reservation_controller.dart:375-378 `if (ride.status == ReservationStatus.scheduled) { await _store.assignDriver(ride.reservationId);`
suggested_fix: Inside the serialized change, re-check the current status (e.g. assignDriver/updateReservation status patches refuse when `!current.status.isUpcoming`, or take an expected `from` status) and return the current record unchanged.

title: Booking screen promises free cancellation before a driver is assigned and terms before booking; neither is true
description: The date/time step shows `cancelBeforeAssigned`: 'You can cancel without a fee before a driver is assigned. Final terms are shown before booking.' The fee actually charged (`ScheduledRideRules.cancelTermsFor`) depends only on minutes before pickup (free while `minutesBeforePickup >= freeMin`, default 60 or the zone's per-category rule). Driver assignment does not matter; the only exception is a missed pickup. Nothing in the scheduled SelectRide/checkout path shows the cancel terms before booking: `cancelTermsFor`/`cancelRule` are only used on the Upcoming and Terms pages.
failure_scenario: At 23:15 the rider books the 23:50 ride (pickup 35 min away, inside the 60 min window) and immediately taps Cancel, before any driver is assigned. The sheet says 'Cancelling costs kr 50' and the fee is recorded. The booking screen had promised a free cancel before assignment, and no terms were shown before booking.
evidence:
app_en.arb:1667 `"cancelBeforeAssigned": "You can cancel without a fee before a driver is assigned. Final terms are shown before booking."`
select_date_time.dart:532 `context.l10n.cancelBeforeAssigned,`
scheduled_ride_rules.dart:100-104 `final fee = CancelFeeCalculator.reservation(rule, fare, ride.scheduledPickupAt.difference(now).inMinutes);`
cancel_fee.dart:73-76 `minutesBeforePickup >= rule.freeMin ? Money(0, ...) : _charge(rule, fare)`
suggested_fix: Replace the copy with the actual rule (`ReservationFormat.cancelRule` / cancelTermsFor on a draft). Show the cancel terms on the scheduled Select Ride CTA before booking.

title: Scheduled-ride terms page states the single 1 h / kr 50 rule while Premium/XL/Comfort reservations are charged the zone's category rule
description: `ReservationController.cancelTermsFor` prefers the zone config's per-category rule. di.dart passes `config: SeedRiderConfigRepository.seed`, so a SEK ride always gets `_configFor` → config → `reservationFeeFor(categoryId)`. The Stockholm seed has comfort: 60 min / 6000 öre and premium/xl: 120 min / 25% (min 8000, max 30000 öre). The Terms page (opened from 'View terms' on the Upcoming page) renders only `ReservationFormat.cancelRule(rules)`, the single admin rule (60 min / 5000 öre).
failure_scenario: Rider books a Premium ride for tomorrow 07:15 at kr 600. The Terms page says cancelling is free until 1 h before pickup, then kr 50. Cancelling at 05:30 (1 h 45 min before) is charged 25% = kr 150. The 'Things to know' card on the same ride also disagrees with the Terms page.
evidence:
scheduled_ride_terms.dart:57-58 `context.l10n.resTermsOtherFees(ReservationFormat.cancelRule(rules),`
reservation_controller.dart:117-124 `_rules.cancelTermsFor(ride, now ?? _clock(), categoryRule: _configFor(ride.currency)?.reservationFeeFor(ride.categoryId));`
di.dart:175 `config: SeedRiderConfigRepository.seed,`
rider_app_config.dart:672-684 `'comfort': {'freeMin': 60, 'type': 'fixed', 'value': 6000 ...}, 'premium': {'freeMin': 120, 'type': 'percent', 'value': 25, 'min': {'amountMinor': 8000 ...`
suggested_fix: Show the rule that applies to the ride (pass the Reservation and use cancelTermsFor / the category FeeRule), or list the per-category rules.

title: Driver name is shown on accept even when admin turned off showDriverOnAccept
description: `ScheduledRideRules.showDriverOnAccept = false` means the rider sees the driver 'only once on the way' (`showsDriverOf`). UpcomingReservationPage hides the driver card in that case, but the status banner body still uses `ReservationFormat.statusBody`. For driverAssigned that body interpolates `driver.firstName` with no rules check. The 'driver left' banner (upcoming_reservation.dart:306-316) also prints `previousDriver`'s name unconditionally, even though that driver was never revealed.
failure_scenario: Admin sets showDriverOnAccept=false. The mock assigns Erik 15 s after booking. The card is hidden and the page says 'Driver details appear when your driver is on the way', but the banner directly above it reads 'Erik is assigned to this reservation.' After the handover, 'Erik left…' names a driver the rider was never meant to see.
evidence:
reservation_format.dart:184-192 `case ReservationStatus.driverAssigned: ... final driver = ride.driver; ... return L10n.current.resBodyNameAssigned(driver.firstName);`
upcoming_reservation.dart:288-291 `body: ReservationFormat.statusBody(ride, assignmentDisclaimer: ...)` and :306-314 `else if (ride.driver == null && previousDriver != null ...) ReservationStatusBanner(... body: ReservationFormat.driverLeftBody(previousDriver)`
scheduled_ride_rules.dart:121-125 `if (ride.revealsDriver) return true; return showDriverOnAccept && ride.driverAssigned;`
suggested_fix: Pass `showsDriverOf(ride)` into statusBody and use `resBodyDriverAssigned` (no name) when false. Gate the driver-left banner the same way.

title: Scheduled live ride's cancel-fee note and waiting terms come from the Book Now session's category, not the reservation
description: For a reservation, `ReservationLiveRide.pageFor` mounts WaitingForDriver. `_cancelFeeNote` and `_loadWaitingTerms` take the category from `AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId ?? RouteChangeController.storedRide()?.categoryId`. Those belong to the global Book Now session and snapshot, not to the reservation (whose `categoryId` is not passed in). The note then applies the LIVE fee rule (`LiveCancelFeePreview`, minutes since accept), not the reservation's late-cancel terms. With no Book Now ride the category is null, so the sheet shows no fee at all. With a stale Book Now session it shows another category's live fee. This differs from the known finding that the live-screen cancel records no fee: here the fee line the rider confirms against is wrong.
failure_scenario: The 23:50 Comfort reservation goes en route (inside the late window, so a kr 60 fee applies under the reservation rules). The rider taps Cancel on the live screen. With no Book Now session the sheet shows no fee line, so it reads as free. If an older Economy Book Now session is still in memory, it shows 'Free to cancel for 2 more minutes' from the live economy rule.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:772-776 `final stored = await RouteChangeController.storedRide(); final category = AppScope.instance.ride.bookedCategoryId ?? stored?.categoryId; if (category == null) return null;`
:782-787 `final preview = LiveCancelFeePreview.of(config, categoryId: category, ..., acceptedAt: _acceptedAt, ...`
:294-296 same lookup for `_loadWaitingTerms`.
suggested_fix: Pass the reservation's categoryId (and a fee-note provider using ReservationController.cancelTermsFor) into WaitingForDriver from ReservationLiveRide.pageFor.

title: Route change is offered on a scheduled live ride but always fails (route-quote for a device-only reservation id)
description: `_routeEditable` only checks that the status is not terminal, so the three-dots 'change route' and the cancel sheet's 'change destination instead' are offered on the reservation live screen. `_currentRide()` builds a snapshot with `rideId: <reservationId>`, and `RouteChangeController` POSTs `/api/v1/rides/rsv_.../route-quote`, which the mock answers 404 because reservations never exist server-side. Even if it succeeded, nothing writes the change back to the Reservation.
failure_scenario: On the live 07:15 scheduled ride the rider taps the ride card's three dots and picks a new destination. 'See new price' fails every time, because the server has no such ride. Picking 'change destination instead' in the cancel sheet leads to the same failure.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:1004 `bool get _routeEditable => !_tracking.status.isTerminal && !_completedOpened;`
waiting_for_driver.dart:1032-1047 `return RideSnapshot(... rideId: rideId, ...` (reservation id)
route_change_controller.dart:200-201 `_api.post('/api/v1/rides/$id/route-quote', ...`
suggested_fix: Add a `routeEditable`/`allowRouteChange` flag to WaitingForDriver and set it false from ReservationLiveRide until reservations are server-backed.

title: A completed reservation opens as 'Upcoming ride'; ended reservations from notifications are opened instead of routed to History
description: The page title only distinguishes cancelled from everything else, so a completed reservation (opened from History › Completed via `_openHistoryRide`, or from a push via `_openReservation`) is headed 'Upcoming ride' with 'Your ride is reserved for …'. `_openReservation` in notification_navigation returns true for any reservation id it finds, whatever its status. FLOW-18's 'This ride has ended' + open History path (`openNotificationRide` onEnded) therefore never runs for ended scheduled rides.
failure_scenario: The rider finishes the 07:15 scheduled ride and opens it from History › Completed. The page says 'Upcoming ride — Your ride is reserved for Thu, 22 Oct at 07:15' above a 'Completed' banner.
evidence:
upcoming_reservation.dart:235-237 `ride.status.isCancelled ? context.l10n.resCancelledReservation : context.l10n.resUpcomingRide,`
notification_navigation.dart:129-135 `final reservation = AppScope.instance.reservations.byId(id); if (reservation == null || id.startsWith('ondemand-')) return false; return pushPageOnce(...UpcomingReservationPage...`
suggested_fix: Title by status (completed → completed-ride heading). In `_openReservation`, return false when `!reservation.status.isUpcoming` so the ended-ride path runs.

title: Live ride notes for a reservation are guessed by substring, so the rider's own words set flags and 'Bags 3+' loses its level
description: `notesOf` turns the free-text `note` into RideNotes with `note.contains('Bags'|'Pet'|'Baby'|'Child')`. The note is the rider's text joined with the chip labels (`_driverNote`), so any rider text containing those substrings sets the flag. 'Bags 3+' sets `bags` but not `manyBags`, so the live screen shows 1–2 bags.
failure_scenario: The note is 'Petra will meet you at gate B'. The live scheduled ride shows a Pet preference to the rider and driver card. A rider who chose 3+ bags sees plain 'Bags' on the live screen.
evidence: reservation_live_ride.dart:34-41 `final note = ride.note ?? ''; return RideNotes(bags: note.contains('Bags'), pet: note.contains('Pet'), baby: note.contains('Baby'), child: note.contains('Child'));`
suggested_fix: Parse the ' · ' / ', ' separated tokens and match them exactly against RideNotes.selected labels, including 'Bags 3+'. Better, store RideNotes structurally on the reservation.

title: 'We'll notify you as soon as a driver is assigned' — nothing ever notifies on reservation assignment
description: After booking, RideScheduledPage promises a notification on assignment (`resNotifyAssigned`). Assignment (`assignMockDriver` / `applyDriverAssignment`) only updates the store and calls notifyListeners. Nothing posts to NotificationsRepository, and no toast, local notification or push is produced. The only signal is the chrono badge changing colour if the rider happens to be looking at Home.
failure_scenario: The rider books tomorrow 07:15 and leaves the app or stays in another screen. The driver accepts 15 s later and then hands over to another driver. No notification or notice is shown; Notifications stays 'All caught up'.
evidence:
ride_scheduled.dart:163-164 `Text(ReservationFormat.notifyWhenAssigned,`
reservation_format.dart:92 `static String get notifyWhenAssigned => L10n.current.resNotifyAssigned;`
reservation_controller.dart:275-287 assignMockDriver only `_store.assignDriver(...)` + `notifyListeners()`
suggested_fix: Ingest an in-app notification (NotificationsRepository) or show a toast on assignment/driver change, or change the copy.

title: Upcoming tab lists reservations in booking order, not pickup order
description: `_upcoming()` shows `_reservations.upcoming()` as stored. `createReservation` prepends (`[created, ..._items]`), so the list is newest-booked first. The Home chrono sorts by `scheduledPickupAt`; History does not.
failure_scenario: Book tomorrow 07:15, then book today 23:50. History › Upcoming shows the 23:50 ride below tomorrow 07:15, although it is the next ride.
evidence:
ride_history.dart:268 `final upcoming = _reservations.upcoming();` (no sort)
local_reservation_repository.dart:183 `await _commit([created, ..._items]);`
suggested_fix: Sort by scheduledPickupAt ascending before building the list.

title: Driver card screen-reader label hard-codes English 'plate'
description: The Semantics label of ReservationDriverCard joins a translated driver phrase with a literal English 'plate ${driver.plate}', so fr/sv screen readers hear an English word mid-sentence. (A different site from the known ride_restore_coordinator finding.)
failure_scenario: With the app in Svenska and TalkBack on, the driver card reads 'Din förare Erik, Svart Volvo XC40, plate ABC123'.
evidence: upcoming_reservation.dart:503-507 `label: [context.l10n.resYourDriverName(driver.displayFirstName), if (car != null) car, if (driver.plate != null) 'plate ${driver.plate}',].join(', '),`
suggested_fix: Use a localized ARB string for the plate phrase.

title: Finding and Waiting ride cards show the stored English payment name ('Cash', 'Movera Wallet', 'Card') in sv/fr
description: The snapshot and the screens keep the payment method under its English catalog name: select_ride passes `paymentMethod: payment.name` / `paymentMethodLabel: payment.name` (select_ride.dart:1547, 1615), and booking_coordinator.dart:728 saves `paymentMethod: paymentMethodLabel ?? paymentMethod`. payment_labels.dart says that name 'stays the method's identity; only what is shown is translated', but `bookedPaymentLine` puts it into the line as it is. That line is the payment row on both live ride cards: FindingDrivers (finding_drivers.dart:1130) and WaitingForDriver (waiting_sheet_bits.dart:162). The same raw name also goes into the route-change sentences: route_change_sheet.dart:132/134 `context.l10n.moreCharged(_kr(diff), paymentMethod)` / `lessReturned` and route_change_flow.dart:188/192 `chargedTo(kr, paymentMethod)` / `refundedToDays`. A ride restored from a server projection that has no label shows the raw id ('cash', 'card:…') instead (ride_projection.dart:62). paymentLabelFor / paymentNameFor exist for this, and the reservation pages use them, but these paths do not.
failure_scenario: Rider books a cash ride in English, then switches to Svenska during the search or the ride. The ride card reads 'Cash · 259 kr' instead of 'Kontant · 259 kr'. In French, a route change with Movera Wallet reads '+30 kr de plus, débité sur Movera Wallet.' instead of 'Portefeuille Movera'.
evidence: wallet_split.dart:110 `return '$paymentMethod$separator${formatMoney(fare, whole: true)}';` and :115 `return '$paymentMethod ${split.remainderLabel}$separator'`; waiting_sheet_bits.dart:162-163 `bookedPaymentLine(paymentMethod: paymentMethod, ...)`; finding_drivers.dart:1130-1131 `bookedPaymentLine(paymentMethod: widget.paymentMethod,`; route_change_sheet.dart:132 `priceNote = context.l10n.moreCharged(_kr(diff), paymentMethod);`; payment_labels.dart:24 `String paymentLabelFor(String stored) => switch (stored.trim()) { 'Cash' => L10n.current.payCash, ...`
suggested_fix: Pass the stored name through paymentLabelFor (and map ids such as 'cash', 'wallet', 'card:*' too) inside bookedPaymentLine and before the moreCharged/lessReturned/chargedTo/refundedToDays calls.

title: Set pickup shows the payment method name and detail in English ('Cash' / 'Pay the driver in cash') in every language
description: SelectRide builds the SetPickupPayment from the raw catalog item: `name: item?.name ?? context.l10n.payCash, detail: item?.detail ?? ''` (select_ride.dart:1286-1289).
