The catalog item holds English text (ride_selection_repository.dart:184-189: 'Cash', 'Pay the driver in cash', 'Movera Wallet', 'Pay from your balance', 'Pays when the search starts'). Select Ride's own payment button translates these with paymentNameFor/paymentDetailFor (select_ride.dart:2572, 2586). Set pickup prints `_payment.name` and `_payment.detail` as they are, and also uses `_payment.name` as the remainder label of a wallet split.
failure_scenario: App in Svenska, rider books a cash ride. Select Ride shows 'Kontant', then the Set pickup sheet (always shown before Book now) shows 'Cash' / 'Pay the driver in cash'. With a wallet split, the remainder row reads 'Cash  209 kr'. The same happens in French.
evidence: set_pickup_page.dart:1431 `Text(_payment.name, style: _text(14.5, weight: FontWeight.w600)),` :1432-1433 `if (_payment.detail.trim().isNotEmpty) Text(_payment.detail, ...)`; :1394 `fare.split.paidByWallet ? context.l10n.nothingMoreToPay : _payment.name,`; select_ride.dart:2572 `paymentNameFor(method.brand, method.name),`
suggested_fix: Render `paymentNameFor(_payment.brand, _payment.name)` and `paymentDetailFor(_payment.brand, _payment.detail)` in Set pickup, or pass the translated strings from SelectRide.

title: History saves English end-of-ride reasons ('No driver found', 'Request expired', ...) and shows them untranslated in sv/fr
description: When a Book-now ride ends without a rider reason, recordFor stores `_endedSearchReason(terminalStatus)` as `cancellationReason`, and that is an English sentence. ride_history.dart:561 shows it through ReservationFormat.reasonLabel. reasonLabel only translates known reason ids and snake_case codes; anything else is 'shown as they are' (reservation_format.dart:47-64). These English labels are never translated in any language. The status code (or a code such as 'system_no_driver', which reasonLabel already maps) should be stored instead.
failure_scenario: App in French, a search ends with no driver (RideStatus.noDriverFound) and is archived. History › Cancelled › detail shows 'Raison : No driver found'. For an admin cancel it shows 'Cancelled by Movera', for an expired request 'Request expired', for a no-show 'No-show'.
evidence: on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:228-231 `cancellationReason: cancellationReason ?? snapshot.cancellationReason ?? _endedSearchReason(terminalStatus),`; :261-269 `RideStatus.noDriverFound => 'No driver found', RideStatus.bookingExpired => 'Request expired', RideStatus.cancelledByAdmin => 'Cancelled by Movera', ...`; reservation_format.dart:64 `return value;`; ride_history.dart:561 `context.l10n.reasonLine(ReservationFormat.reasonLabel(ride.cancellationReason!))`
suggested_fix: Store a reason code (for example 'system_no_driver', 'booking_expired', 'admin_other', 'rider_no_show') and translate it in reasonLabel. Map the English labels already saved on devices to their codes when reading.

title: Reservation reasons the app itself writes ('no_driver_found', 'rider_cancelled_live') are shown as English text in every language
description: ReservationController.resolveNoDriverFound stores `noDriverFoundReason = 'no_driver_found'` (reservation_controller.dart:302, 325), and the live scheduled ride stores `'rider_cancelled_live'` when the rider cancels without a reason (reservation_live_ride.dart:81, reservation_ride_realtime.dart:148). Neither is a CancellationReason id or a key of `_reasonLabels`: the map has 'system_no_driver', not 'no_driver_found'. Both fall through to the snake_case regex, which turns them into English words. The result appears in the History detail ('Reason: …') and in the cancelled-reservation status body.
failure_scenario: App in Svenska, a reservation times out without a driver and the rider taps the No-driver sheet (home_reservation_chrono.dart:124). The reservation then reads 'Avbokad. No driver found' and History reads 'Anledning: No driver found'. Cancelling a live scheduled ride and skipping the reason sheet shows 'Anledning: Rider cancelled live'.
evidence: reservation_format.dart:39-45 `'rider_no_show': ..., 'system_no_driver': L10n.current.termNoDriverFound, ...`; :60-62 `if (RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(_[a-z0-9]+)+$').hasMatch(value)) { final words = value.replaceAll('_', ' '); return '${words[0].toUpperCase()}${words.substring(1)}'; }`; reservation_controller.dart:302 `static const noDriverFoundReason = 'no_driver_found';`; reservation_live_ride.dart:81 `reason: reasonId ?? 'rider_cancelled_live',`
suggested_fix: Add 'no_driver_found' (-> termNoDriverFound) and 'rider_cancelled_live' (-> a translated 'Cancelled by you' label) to the reason map, or store contract codes that are already mapped.

title: Share trip contact list shows the stored English relationship ('Family', 'Friend') untranslated
description: Emergency contacts keep their relationship in English, as the server has it ('Partner', 'Family', 'Friend', 'Colleague', 'Other'). emergency_contacts_page.dart:422-429 provides relationshipLabel to translate it and uses it in the contacts list (line 190). The trip share page, reachable during a ride from WaitingShareButton and the safety kit, prints `shareable[i].relationship` directly, although it already imports emergency_contacts_page.dart.
failure_scenario: App in French, rider in a trip opens Partager le trajet. Every contact's subtitle reads 'Family' / 'Friend' instead of 'Famille' / 'Ami(e)'.
evidence: trip_share_page.dart:160-161 `subtitle: Text(shareable[i].relationship,`; emergency_contacts_page.dart:424 `String relationshipLabel(String value) => switch (value) { 'Partner' => L10n.current.relationshipPartner, 'Family' => L10n.current.relationshipFamily, ...`
suggested_fix: Use `relationshipLabel(shareable[i].relationship)`.

title: Ride-completed receipt translates only 'Cash'; 'Movera Wallet', 'Card' and the 'Current location' pickup stay English
description: The receipt's method is `ride.paymentMethod`, the stored English name (driver_repository.dart:116). trip_detail translates only Cash, through isCashLabel. Wallet and the generic card show 'Movera Wallet' / 'Card' in sv/fr, although paymentLabelFor covers them. The pickup row prints `trip.pickup` raw, while every other ride screen passes the address through L10n.place / shortenPlace. A ride whose pickup kept the 'Current location' stand-in therefore reads English on the receipt. This is the same class of defect as the known History-detail finding, but in a different screen and file.
failure_scenario: Svenska, a ride paid from Movera Wallet completes. Trip details shows 'Betalningsmetod: Movera Wallet' instead of 'Movera Plånbok'. Pickup shows 'Current location' when that stand-in was the booked pickup.
evidence: trip_detail.dart:76-79 `context.l10n.paymentMethod, L10n.isCashLabel(trip.method) ? context.l10n.payCash : trip.method,`; trip_detail.dart:60 `_detailRow(context.l10n.pickupLocation, trip.pickup),`; driver_repository.dart:116 `method: ride.paymentMethod,`
suggested_fix: Use paymentLabelFor(trip.method) and L10n.place(trip.pickup) / shortenPlace for the receipt rows.

title: Notification day labels are fixed in the language active at ingest and do not follow a language change
description: ingest() saves the finished label `time: _formatTime(at)` into AppNotification. _formatTime uses L10n.current.notifYesterday and L10n.formatDate(time, 'd MMM'), so the stored string holds the weekday/month words of the language in use at that moment. LanguageRebuild rebuilds the Notifications list, but it prints `notification.time`, so older items keep the old language. This has the same root as the known 'frozen at ingest' finding; the facet here is that the language of the label is frozen too, which goes against the Q48 promise in l10n.dart that nothing keeps showing the old language.
failure_scenario: Swedish app with notifications from yesterday and last week ('I går 14:05', '3 okt. 14:05'). The rider switches to French: the list still says 'I går 14:05' and '3 okt. 14:05' instead of 'Hier 14:05' / '3 oct. 14:05'.
evidence: notifications_repository.dart:53 `time: _formatTime(at),`; :97 `if (daysAgo == 1) return L10n.current.notifYesterday(clock);` :98 `final date = L10n.formatDate(time, 'd MMM');`; notifications.dart:190 `text: notification.time,`
suggested_fix: Store only `at` and format the label in the widget's build from `at`, using the current language and the current day.

title: Finding's destination pin bitmap 'Arrive by HH:MM' is drawn once in initState and keeps the old language
description: _prepareMapVisuals is called only from initState (line 171). It renders the destination time pin into a BitmapDescriptor with `context.l10n.arriveBy(...)` and stores it in `_destinationPin`. LanguageRebuild rebuilds the widget but never re-renders the bitmap, so the map label stays in the language of the moment the search started. Waiting regenerates its pins when the label key changes; Finding never does.
failure_scenario: Rider starts a search in English, goes to Home and switches to Français while the search continues. The search card text is French, but the map pin still reads 'Arrive by 14:32' (Swedish: should be 'Framme 14:32').
evidence: finding_drivers.dart:171 `unawaited(_prepareMapVisuals());` (initState); :491-496 `RouteTimeMarker.createIcon(pickup: false, label: context.l10n.arriveBy(clockTime(DateTime.now().add(Duration(minutes: eta + tripMinutes)))),`; :499 `_destinationPin = icons[2];`
suggested_fix: Re-create the time-pin icons when the language code (or label) changes, for example keyed like Waiting's `_timePinKey`.

title: Upcoming reservation and History card print the raw pickup label, so the stored 'Current location' stand-in shows in English
description: A scheduled booking with an unchanged pickup is saved with the English stand-in label: scheduled_category_gate.dart:21-23 falls back to 'Current location', the session default is 'Current location' (scheduled_rides_controller.dart:6), and with `pickupAlreadyConfirmed: true` Set pickup is skipped, so ScheduledRideCheckout stores `label: _pickupAddress`. L10n.place translates that stand-in, and ride_scheduled.dart:208 uses shortPlace (L10n.place). The Upcoming reservation 'Pickup at' fact and the History reservation card print `ride.pickup.label` unmodified.
failure_scenario: Rider books for later from the current location, then switches to Svenska. Upcoming reservation reads 'Upphämtning vid: Current location' and the History card reads 'Current location → Odenplan'. Ride scheduled already shows the translated text for the same reservation.
evidence: upcoming_reservation.dart:340-342 `ReservationFact(asset: AppAssets.gps, label: context.l10n.resPickupAt, value: ride.pickup.label,)`; reservation_widgets.dart:387 `'${ride.pickup.label} → ${ride.destination.label}',`; scheduled_category_gate.dart:21-23 `final pickupLabel = session.pickup.trim().isEmpty ? 'Current location' : session.pickup.trim();`
suggested_fix: Pass place labels through L10n.place (or ReservationFormat.shortPlace) on these two screens.

title: Language picker ignores the zone config's `languages.available` list it is documented to honour
description: AppLanguages.available is documented as 'what the user may pick' (zone_settings.dart:27-28), and readAppLanguages parses and keeps it. pickAppLanguage always offers every shipped language, and AppLanguageController.choose saves any supported code. Neither reads `document.languages.available`, so an admin restriction of a zone's languages has no effect on the rider app.
failure_scenario: An operator sets a zone's `languages.available` to ['fr','en']. A rider in that zone still sees and can pick 'SV · Svenska', and that choice wins over the zone forever.
evidence: language_picker.dart:21 `options: [for (final l in L10n.languages) l.code],`; zone_settings.dart:27 `/// App languages (`languages`, owner Q48/Q49): what the user may pick, and`; app_language_controller.dart:58 `_zoneDefault = L10n.supported(document.languages.rider);` (available never read)
suggested_fix: Keep the zone's available list in AppLanguageController, filter the picker options by it, and fall back to the zone default when a saved choice is not available.

title: Sign-out wipe deletes the recording index but leaves the previous rider's Safety audio files on disk
description: UserDataWipe.run says it removes everything a rider left on this device. It removes `movera_safety_cache_v1`, which is the list of recordings, and resets the Safety mock. It never deletes the audio files themselves. NativeSafetyRecorder writes every Safety Kit and Ride check (RC5, 'saved only on this phone') recording to `<documents>/safety_recordings/<id>.m4a`. The only code that deletes a file is SafetyAudioService.delete, and it needs the AudioRecording entry that the wipe has just thrown away. After sign-out, or after another rider signs in (enterSessionAs -> run), the previous rider's cabin audio stays on the device for good, and nothing in the UI can reach it to remove it.
failure_scenario: Rider A records audio from the Safety Kit or a Ride check card during a trip, then signs out. Rider B signs in on the same phone. Rider A's .m4a files are still in the app's documents/safety_recordings folder (device backups and file-sharing tools can reach them), and the app can no longer list or delete them.
suggested_fix: In UserDataWipe.run, delete the safety_recordings directory (on native only), or delete every localPath found in the safety cache before removing the key.

title: Wipe disposes the Safety and Ride check controllers without stopping a running recording, so the microphone keeps recording with no owner
description: UserDataWipe.resetInMemory calls SafetyController.resetShared(). That calls RideCheckController.resetShared() (dispose only sets _disposed and clears the QA owner), then `_shared?.dispose()`. SafetyController does not override dispose, so this is plain ChangeNotifier.dispose. Neither path calls `audio.stopIfRecording`. An RC5 recording started from the Ride check card is not stopped when WaitingForDriver is torn down either: its dispose only calls `RideCheckController.shared.detachTrip(rideId)`, which nulls the monitor. When the session expires mid-trip, showMoveraRoot(SignIn) pops the trip screen and the recording keeps running behind Sign in. When the next rider signs in, enterSessionAs -> run -> resetShared drops the only reference to that SafetyAudioService. Nothing can ever stop the recorder again before the process dies.
failure_scenario: Rider A is in a trip, a Ride check opens and A taps 'Record audio'. The session expires (refresh rejected), so Sign in replaces the trip screen and the microphone is still recording. Rider B signs in: the wipe replaces the controllers, and the microphone stays on recording into A's file with no Stop button anywhere, until the app is killed.
suggested_fix: In resetShared (or in UserDataWipe.resetInMemory, before resetting), await or fire `_shared?.audio.stopIfRecording(reason: 'session_end')` and delete the result. Also stop the recording when the trip screen is disposed by a forced Sign in.

title: A brand-new install on iOS signs in as the previous owner: Keychain tokens survive uninstall and nothing clears them on first launch
description: Tokens (and the ride PIN, SecureRidePinStore) live in the iOS Keychain through flutter_secure_storage with default options. iOS keeps Keychain items after the app is uninstalled, but it wipes SharedPreferences, including `movera_rider_fingerprint`. Nothing records a first run and clears the secure store on first launch. On a 'fresh' install, RideRestoreCoordinator._root -> _shouldRequireSignIn -> _hasSession() reads the surviving access and refresh tokens and skips Sign in. It then calls adoptServerActiveTrip() and opens Home, or the previous rider's live trip, under that rider's account. The fingerprint is gone too, so enterSessionAs can never notice that the rider changed.
evidence:
secure_token_store.dart:38-43 return _NativeSecureStore(const FlutterSecureStorage(aOptions: AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true))); (no first-run reset)
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:171-175 _defaultHasSession reads tokens; 444-453 no sign-in when a session exists -> pageFor(snapshot ?? await adoptServerActiveTrip())
user_data_wipe.dart:167-169 previous fingerprint read from prefs (gone after reinstall) -> no wipe
failure_scenario: Rider A uses the app on a family iPad and uninstalls it without signing out. Rider B installs Movera and opens it for the first time. There is no Sign in screen: B lands on Home signed in as A, with A's server-side history, payment methods and any live trip, and can book on A's account.
suggested_fix: Keep a first-run marker in SharedPreferences. When it is missing at bootstrap, clear the secure token store and the ride PIN before the restore gate reads the session.

title: OTP expiry is checked against the device clock, so a phone whose clock runs more than 5 minutes fast can never verify a code
description: The server sends `expiresAt` as an absolute timestamp (the mock sets now + 5 min). OtpChallenge.isExpired compares it with `DateTime.now().toUtc()` on the device. PhoneVerification._verify refuses locally with 'code expired' and AuthRepository.verifyOtp throws, both before anything is sent to the server. If the device clock is ahead of the server by more than the validity window, every fresh challenge is 'expired' the moment it arrives. Resend returns a new challenge with the same skew, so the rider is stuck. The server is the only party that can decide expiry, and the client also gets retryAfterSeconds as a relative value, which would allow a relative local deadline.
failure_scenario: A rider's phone clock is set manually 10 minutes fast. They enter their number and type the correct 4-digit code, and Verify immediately shows 'Code expired'. Resend and retry give the same result, so they cannot sign up or sign in.
suggested_fix: Turn expiry into a local monotonic deadline when the challenge is received (receivedAt + (expiresAt - serverNow), or a duration from the server), or drop the client-side check and let the server's otp_expired answer decide.

title: Rider change after session expiry wipes local data but keeps the previous rider's push registration, so their ride notifications can reach the new rider
description: On explicit sign-out, AuthController.signOut calls push.unregister(), which unregisters the token on the server and calls FirebaseMessaging.deleteToken, so 'a signed-out Rider cannot keep receiving notifications for that session'. On session expiry, ApiClient._expireSession only clears tokens and opens Sign in. When a different rider then signs in, _enterSession -> enterSessionAs wipes local data but does nothing about push. FirebasePushService keeps `_registeredToken` and its inbound streams. _registerPushBestEffort -> register() gets the same FCM token, and `_replaceToken` skips unregistering because previous == token. The device token is never rotated, so the backend binding for the previous rider stays valid, and that rider's ride is usually still live (the DI comment says the ride goes on server-side).
evidence:
auth_controller.dart:92-105 signOut: await AppScope.instance.push.unregister(); (only on explicit sign-out)
api_client.dart:220-225 _expireSession: await _tokens?.clear(); await _onSessionExpired?.call(); (no push unregister)
user_data_wipe.dart:165-176 enterSessionAs: if (wipe) await run(); (no push.unregister/deleteToken)
firebase_push_service.dart _replaceToken: if (previous != null && previous != token) await _unregisterToken(previous);
failure_scenario: Rider A's session expires mid-ride on a shared phone. Rider B signs in on the same phone. The FCM token is still registered for A, so A's 'Driver arriving' and receipt pushes (driver name, plate, places) keep landing on B's phone, and B can tap them.
suggested_fix: When enterSessionAs detects a rider change, call push.deleteToken() (or a local-only unregister) before registering push for the new rider, so a fresh device token is minted.

title: Sign-out abandons the pending-cancel flush after 5 s, and the still-running flush can write the previous rider's queued cancels back after the wipe
description: UserDataWipe.flushPendingCancels wraps FindingDriverController.flushPendingCancels() in `.timeout(5 s)`. A timeout only stops the wait; the flush keeps running in the background while signOut goes on to clear tokens and run() removes `movera_pending_cancels`. The flush loop uses the list it read at the start. For each entry it re-reads the trip with a GET (up to 2 x 15 s). When the version moved on it calls `PendingCancelStore.add(cancel.forVersion(version))`, which writes the key again. It then POSTs: with the tokens gone that is a 401 with no access token, which is not a permanent failure, so `continue` keeps the entry. The previous rider's cancel now sits in the outbox, and the next session's reconnect or launch flush sends it with the new rider's token. The doc block says that must not happen ('sending them later with another rider's session would cancel nothing or the wrong thing'). `_flushInFlight` also stays set, so a new flush started meanwhile joins the stale run.
failure_scenario: On a slow network, rider A signs out with a queued end-early or cancel. The GET re-read takes about 7 s, past the 5 s budget, so sign-out clears the tokens and wipes storage. The GET then answers with a newer version, the entry is re-added, and the POST fails 401. Rider B signs in, and every reconnect retries A's cancel under B's session.
suggested_fix: Give the flush a cancellation token or a session generation that the wipe bumps. Make PendingCancelStore.add a no-op once the session it started under is over, and clear `_flushInFlight` in the wipe.

title: RideSession.reset() keeps the previous rider's booked category, payment method id and offer ceiling, and they carry into the next rider's adopted ride
description: reset() is documented as 'Back to "no ride" at the end of a rider's session'. It clears rideId, status, versions and quote, but not bookedCategoryId, bookedPaymentMethodId or bookedMaxOfferMinor. backendReconcile clears these fields only when both the current and the incoming ride id are non-null and differ. After reset, rideId is null, so the next ride never clears them. RideRestoreCoordinator._adoptBookingIds and BookingCoordinator's active-trip adoption then fall back to the stale session values whenever the server projection omits a field (`snapshot.maxOfferMinor ?? session.bookedMaxOfferMinor`). FindingDriverController.start writes them into the new snapshot, and WaitingForDriver prefers `ride.bookedCategoryId` over the stored category for the waiting-fee terms.
evidence:
ride_session.dart:205-217 reset() { ... rideId = null; ... } (booked* untouched)
ride_session.dart:106-122 isNewRide requires currentRideId != null to clear booked*
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:396-400 session.bookedMaxOfferMinor = snapshot.maxOfferMinor ?? session.bookedMaxOfferMinor;
finding_driver_controller.dart:275-277 categoryId/paymentMethodId/maxOfferMinor from session into the snapshot
failure_scenario: Rider A books a Premium ride (ceiling 600 kr, card_A), then signs out. Rider B signs in and opens a ride B booked on another device, adopted from GET /rider/trips/active, whose projection has no maxOfferMinor. B's search is stored and priced with A's 600 kr offer ceiling and A's payment method id, and Waiting loads waiting terms for A's category.
suggested_fix: Clear bookedCategoryId, bookedPaymentMethodId and bookedMaxOfferMinor in reset().

title: After location is revoked and then allowed again, Home never restarts live tracking; the puck freezes while the state says 'live'
description: When the position stream errors with PermissionDeniedException, startTracking cancels the subscription, sets permissionRequired and returns without arranging a resubscribe. When the rider allows location again and returns to the app, Home.didChangeAppLifecycleState calls resumeLiveUpdates(). That only asks for one fix (_refreshAfterResume -> latestFix) and sets the state to live. The resume handler restarts tracking only for `temporarilyUnavailable` (recoverLiveLocation) or when `_currentLatLng == null` (a fresh detect). A rider who had a fix before the revoke matches neither branch. The stream is never subscribed again, so the puck and the pickup label stop following the rider, although the location notice has cleared.
failure_scenario: On iOS, Home is showing the rider's position. The rider switches location to 'Never' in Settings: the stream errors and Home shows 'location denied'. The rider then sets 'While using' and comes back. Home shows one fresh fix and the notice clears, but as the rider walks the blue puck and 'Current location' pickup no longer move. Bookings start from the stale point until Home is rebuilt.
suggested_fix: On resume, when the controller has no active _positionSub and permission is granted, call startTracking again (for example through recoverLiveLocation), not only for temporarilyUnavailable.

title: Leaving Delete account while the request is in flight signs the rider out and wipes the device but never shows Sign in
description: While `_sending`, the main Delete account view has no PopScope, and its AccountScaffold back button calls Navigator.pop. If the rider leaves during the request, AccountDeletionController.requestDeletion still completes: it calls signOutLocally, which clears the tokens and runs UserDataWipe. Then `if (!mounted) return;` skips everything, including the _sentView whose Done and back buttons are the only way to reach showSignInRoot. The rider is left on Account/Home with no session and wiped data. In release builds every API call then fails without a token (no 401 refresh path, because there is no access token), and no Sign in screen appears until a cold start.
failure_scenario: Rider taps Delete my account, confirms, and taps back while the spinner shows. The server accepts with 202: tokens are cleared and local data wiped, but the rider stays on Account and Home looking signed in. Booking or loading anything fails with errors, and Sign in only appears after the app is restarted.
suggested_fix: Block pop while _sending, or call showSignInRoot from the controller path when the page is no longer mounted (the root navigator is available through moveraNavigatorKey).

title: The new-rider name step is decided once from isNewRider; a reload or kill on that step skips it forever
description: verifyOtp saves the session tokens first. Only then does PhoneVerification show RiderNameScreen as the root, and only when that one response says isNewRider. Nothing stores 'name still missing', and nothing checks for an empty profile name later. If the app is killed or the web page reloads on the name screen, the next cold start finds a session and opens Home directly: RiderRestoreCoordinator._root has no name check. The server will not say isNewRider again, because the rider is now known. The rider ends up with no name, which the screen itself says 'the driver will look for'.
failure_scenario: A brand-new rider verifies their code on the web demo and reloads the tab on 'What should we call you?'. They land on Home with 'Welcome to Movera', are never asked for a name again, and drivers see no rider name.
suggested_fix: Persist a 'name pending' flag with the session, or show RiderNameScreen whenever a signed-in profile has an empty name.

title: Successful code verification waits for push registration (Firebase init, permission, getToken, POST) before the rider enters the app
description: verifyOtp, and signIn for a linked provider, `await _registerPushBestEffort()` before returning. PhoneVerification keeps the Verify button busy and does not navigate until verifyOtp returns. For a consented rider, register() runs Firebase initialize, requestPermission, ensureAppleTransportReady, getToken and a POST /push/devices (15 s timeout), all on the critical path of entering the app. Consent is stored under `movera.push_consent.v1`, which the sign-out wipe does not remove because of its 'movera_' prefix filter. So even a different rider signing in on the device gets this delay. Errors are caught, so the cost is latency, up to tens of seconds on a poor network, after the code was already accepted. This is the sign-in counterpart of the known bootstrap finding, at a different call site.
failure_scenario: A returning rider with push consent and a weak connection enters a correct code. The button spins until getToken and the push-device POST time out (around 15 s or more), and only then does Home open.
suggested_fix: Fire push registration unawaited after navigation (for example from enterMoveraApp's post-frame callback), as the bootstrap path intends.

title: Sign-out has no busy state: Home and the menu stay interactive during the flush, push unregister and server sign-out
description: After the confirm dialog closes, confirmAndSignOut awaits signOutAndShowSignIn and shows no progress or barrier. The sequence is: flushPendingCancels (up to 5 s), push.unregister (POST, 15 s timeout, plus deleteToken), POST /auth/sign-out (15 s timeout), and the wipe. On a slow network that can take 30 s or more. The menu, Account and Home remain usable throughout, so the rider can tap Sign out again (a second dialog and a concurrent second signOut and wipe) or start a booking with the still-valid token. That booking is then wiped locally (snapshot cleared, FindingDriverController disposed) while the server ride stays searching.
failure_scenario: On a weak connection the rider confirms Sign out, sees nothing happen, goes back to Home and books a ride. POST /rides succeeds with the old token and Finding opens. Seconds later the wipe disposes the search and Sign in appears, while the server ride keeps looking for a driver for a rider who has left.
suggested_fix: Show a modal progress barrier (or disable navigation) from the confirm until showSignInRoot, and ignore repeated sign-out taps while one is running.

title: After a reload, a Ride check whose alert failed or was still sending says 'Movera safety team alerted' and never sends the alert
description: `resume()` rebuilds the card from the event saved on the device. It sets `alertState` to `sent` only when `payload['alertId']` exists, and to `none` otherwise. It sets `called112` from the saved answers. An alert that failed (offline) or was still in flight when the page reloaded or the app was killed has no alertId, so the card comes back with `called112: true` and `alertState: none`. `_AlertBanner` maps `none` to the same text as `sent` (ride_check_card.dart:909-912), so the main step shows 'Movera safety team alerted · Trip, driver and rider details were sent.' The banner can only be tapped to retry in the `failed` state (ride_check_card.dart:962-963), and `retryAlert()` returns unless the state is `failed` (controller:574). When the rider then taps Done, `_close` sends the final submission with `alert: closing.alertState != RideCheckAlertState.none`, which is false (controller:697). The mock answers endpoint only alerts when `body['alert'] == true` or an alert already exists (safety_mock_api.dart:452), so nobody is ever alerted. DECISIONS R-web requires a live ride to survive a reload or PWA eviction, so this resume path is a main path.
failure_scenario: In-trip long stop opens the card. The rider is in a tunnel with no network and taps Call 112: the dialer opens and the alert POST fails. Opening the dialer evicts the Safari/PWA page and it reloads (or the app is killed). The card comes back on the trip screen saying 'Movera safety team alerted · Trip, driver and rider details were sent.' The rider taps Done. The final submission goes out with alert:false and no alert ever reaches the safety team. A red-row alert that was 'sending' at reload is dropped the same way.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:440-455: `final alertId = event.payload['alertId']; ... alertState: alertId is String ? RideCheckAlertState.sent : RideCheckAlertState.none, called112: record.answers.any((answer) => answer.kind == RideCheckAnswerKind.call112),`
ride_check_card.dart:908-912: `RideCheckAlertState.sent || RideCheckAlertState.none => (context.l10n.rcAlertSentTitle, context.l10n.rcAlertSentBody),`
ride_check_controller.dart:697: `alert: closing.alertState != RideCheckAlertState.none,`
ride_check_controller.dart:574: `if (current == null || current.alertState != RideCheckAlertState.failed) { return; }`
suggested_fix: On resume, set alertState to `failed` (not `none`) when the saved answers include call_112 or a red row but no alertId exists, so the banner offers retry and the final submission carries alert:true. Never map `none` to the 'alerted' copy.

title: Share trip sends to the stale tripShareContactIds list and ignores contacts marked 'Share trips' or later disabled or deleted
description: The Safety Kit decides whether sharing is possible from `contact.isEnabled && (tripShareContactIds.contains(id) || contact.shareTrips)` (ride_safety_kit.dart:214-217). TripSharePage shows a contact as selected on the same OR (trip_share_page.dart:150-154). `SafetyController.startShare`, however, sends `preferences.tripShareContactIds` as the recipient list whenever that list is non-empty. It falls back to the `shareTrips && isEnabled` filter in SafetyStore.startShare only when the list is empty. Nothing removes ids from `tripShareContactIds` when a contact is deleted (safety_store.dart:223-238) or disabled in the contact editor. So the real recipients differ from what the rider sees ticked: contacts added with 'Share trips with this person' are left out, and disabled or deleted contacts are included. The toast then counts those ids: 'Trip sharing started for N trusted contacts'.
failure_scenario: The rider ticks Anna on the Trip share page (list = [Anna]). Later they add Bo with 'Share trips with this person' on, and switch Anna off as a contact. The Trip share page shows only Bo, ticked. During the trip, Safety Kit › Share trip calls startShare(contactIds: [Anna]). The share goes to the disabled Anna, not Bo, and the toast says 'Trip sharing started for 1 trusted contact.'
evidence:
safety_controller.dart:297-303: `final share = await _session.startShare(rideId, contactIds: preferences.tripShareContactIds.isEmpty ? null : preferences.tripShareContactIds,);`
ride_safety_kit.dart:215-217: `!_ctl.contacts.any((contact) => contact.isEnabled && (_ctl.preferences.tripShareContactIds.contains(contact.id) || contact.shareTrips))`
safety_store.dart:257-258: `final ids = contactIds ?? _cache.contacts.where((c) => c.shareTrips && c.isEnabled).map((c) => c.id).toList();`
suggested_fix: Build the recipient list in one place, matching what the UI shows: enabled contacts that are in tripShareContactIds or have shareTrips. Prune tripShareContactIds when a contact is deleted or disabled.

title: A Ride check left open when the trip ends externally (admin cancel or failed) stays as the session forever, and no later trip can open a Ride check
description: Only imOk()/done() clear `_session` (via `_close`). When a trip with an open card ends in a non-completed terminal status, `_handleExternalTerminal` calls markExternalTerminal and goes Home (waiting_for_driver.dart:548-596). Statuses that do this include cancelledByAdmin and failed. Home and later screens host no RideCheckLayer for that ride, so the card can never be answered. `_session` still holds ride X, so every later `open()` returns `busy` at line 379, and `resume()` returns early at line 426. On ride Y in the same process, `sessionFor(Y)` is null, so nothing shows and nothing blocks: long stop, off-route, crash and dropped-far are all silently dropped (the monitor marks them fired). This lasts until the app process restarts.
failure_scenario: Ride 1: a long-stop card is open and unanswered when the admin cancels the trip. The rider lands on Home and the card is gone. Ride 2, same app session: the car stands still for 10 minutes at a non-planned spot. RideCheckController.open returns busy and no card ever appears. The Safety › RideCheck demo also reports 'busy'.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:379: `if (_session != null) return RideCheckOpenResult.busy;`
ride_check_controller.dart:426: `if (_session != null) return;`
waiting_for_driver.dart:589-595: `await _ride.markExternalTerminal(status); ... RideNavigator.home(context, status: status);` (no Ride check close)
suggested_fix: When a ride ends without a completion surface, close or park the session for that ride (save it as unanswered on the event). Scope the `busy` check to the visible ride, so a stale session for another ride does not block new trips.

title: A trigger detected while another card is open is used up and never shown or posted (for example dropped-far at trip end while the long-stop card is unanswered)
description: `RideCheckMonitor._fire` adds the trigger to `_fired` before the controller tries to show it. The controller then calls `open()`, which returns `busy` when a card is already up. The detection is neither queued nor posted as a safety event, and because the monitor already marks it fired it can never trigger again for this trip. In this journey, the rider has not answered the long-stop card. The driver taps Finish 3.6 km from the drop-off. `tripEnded` makes the monitor fire droppedFar and `open()` returns busy. The dropped-far check never opens, is never recorded on the trip and never reaches the server. The same happens to a long stop that is detected while an off-route or crash card is still up.
failure_scenario: Long stop card shows mid-trip and the rider does not answer. The trip is then finished 3.6 km from the drop-off. On the summary the rider answers the long-stop card ('I'm OK'). No 'Driver finished far from drop-off' check ever appears and no droppedFar safety event is posted, though the admin trigger is on.
evidence:
ride_check_monitor.dart:251-253: `RideCheckDetection _fire(...) { _fired.add(trigger); return RideCheckDetection(trigger, reason); }`
ride_check_controller.dart:304-306: `final hit = monitor.tripEnded(end); if (hit == null) return RideCheckOpenResult.noTrigger; return open(hit.trigger, reason: hit.reason, rideId: rideId);`
ride_check_controller.dart:379: `if (_session != null) return RideCheckOpenResult.busy;`
suggested_fix: Queue detections that arrive while a card is open and show them after it closes, or at least post their safety event. Alternatively, only mark a trigger fired once it has actually been shown.

title: Trip completion silently stops a Ride check recording while the card, with its Stop control, is still open on the summary
description: `markCompleted` (called from Waiting._openCompleted, waiting_for_driver.dart:712) always calls `_stopSafetyRecording()`, which calls `SafetyController.stopRecordingForRideEnd()` → `audio.stopIfRecording`. The audio service is shared with RideCheckController (`RideCheckController.forSafety` uses `safety.audio`), so a deviceOnly Ride check recording is stopped too. The FLOW-6 rationale (lines 464-466: 'once the ride is over the rider can no longer reach Stop audio') does not hold for Ride check. The unanswered card moves to RideCompleted (RideCheckLayer at ride_completed.dart:443) and keeps its Record/Stop row. The rider gets no note. The row just flips from 'Recording 1:42 · Tap to stop' back to 'Record audio', in the middle of the incident the card is about.
failure_scenario: Off-route card is up and the rider taps Record audio. The driver then taps Finish (an 'asked to leave the car' situation). markCompleted stops and saves the recording. The card on the summary now shows 'Record audio' with no message, and anything said after Finish is not recorded.
evidence:
active_ride_controller.dart:364-371: `Future<void> markCompleted(RideStatus status) async { ... _stopSafetyRecording();`
safety_controller.dart:63-65: `static Future<void> stopRecordingForRideEnd() async { await _shared?.audio.stopIfRecording(reason: 'ride_ended'); }`
ride_check_controller.dart:154-158: `RideCheckController.forSafety(SafetyController safety) => RideCheckController(..., audio: safety.audio);`
suggested_fix: Skip the ride-end stop for a deviceOnly recording while a Ride check card is open for that ride; let `_close` stop it. Or set a recordingNote telling the rider the recording was stopped and saved.

title: Opening a Ride check card pops the Safety Kit sheet, which silently stops the rider's ongoing Safety Kit recording
description: `_comeToFront` pops every route above the trip screen when a card opens. The Safety Kit tells the rider the recording keeps going until they tap Stop audio or close the kit ('safetyKitRecording'), so a rider who wants to keep recording leaves the kit open. When a trigger fires, popUntil closes the kit. The kit's dispose then calls `stopIfRecording(reason: 'sheet_closed')`. The recording ends at the moment the app has just detected something wrong, and neither the kit (now gone) nor the card says so. The card's Record row now shows 'Record audio'.
failure_scenario: The rider feels uneasy, opens the Safety Kit and taps Record audio, leaving the sheet open. Two minutes later the car stops off-route and the long-stop card opens. The kit is popped and the recording is stopped and saved. The rider sees the card with 'Record audio' and has to notice and tap again. Nothing was recorded in between.
evidence:
ride_check_card.dart:212-217: `void _comeToFront() { ... Navigator.of(context).popUntil((other) => other == route); }`
ride_safety_kit.dart:141-147: `void dispose() { ... unawaited(_ctl.audio.stopIfRecording(reason: 'sheet_closed'));`
suggested_fix: Do not stop the recording when the kit is closed programmatically by the Ride check, or hand the running recording over to the card (the same audio service), so the card shows it as still recording.

title: The 'not in traffic' exemption for long stops is dead: samples never set inTraffic, so stops in a traffic queue open Ride check
description: RideCheckMonitor skips stops in traffic only when `sample.inTraffic` is true (ride_check_monitor.dart:175 and 192). The only producer of live samples builds `RideCheckSample(point: point, at: at, etaSeconds: eta?.seconds)`, which leaves inTraffic at its default of false. No other code sets it (a grep finds no traffic signal anywhere). The rider-facing RideCheck page promises 'The car stops for more than {minutes} min, not at a planned stop or in traffic.' (app_en.arb:1991). In practice any queue where the car moves less than 25 m for more than longStopMinutes (default 2) opens the blocking 'Is everything OK?' card.
failure_scenario: In a jam on Essingeleden the car creeps less than 25 m in 2 min 15 s. The 15-second checkStill timer fires a long stop and the non-dismissible card covers the trip screen, although the page says stops in traffic are excluded.
evidence:
waiting_for_driver.dart:1210-1213: `rideCheck.addSample(rideId, RideCheckSample(point: point, at: at, etaSeconds: eta?.seconds),);`
ride_check_monitor.dart:174-176: `if (anchor == null || sample.inTraffic || _meters(anchor, sample.point) > stillRadiusMeters) {`
suggested_fix: Feed a traffic signal into RideCheckSample, for example from server ETA growth or speed versus the route's expected speed, or a server-provided flag. Otherwise remove 'or in traffic' from the copy.

title: 'Automatically share every ride' can be switched on and Safety shows 'Every ride', but nothing ever starts a share when a ride starts
description: TripSharePage lets the rider set `tripShareMode` to auto ('When a ride starts, selected contacts can follow it.'), and the Safety Hub status reads 'Every ride' (safety_controller.dart:105-107). No code reads `TripShareMode.auto` to call startShare: the only startShare caller is the manual Safety Kit button (ride_safety_kit.dart:225). The in-process mock server only stores the preference (safety_mock_api.dart:184-185), so in the shipped demo no share is ever created automatically. Trusted contacts are not following the ride the rider believes is being shared.
failure_scenario: The rider turns on 'Automatically share every ride' with two contacts ticked and books a ride. The trip starts and nobody gets a link or share. The rider only finds out if they open Safety Kit › Share trip.
evidence:
trip_share_page.dart:94: `value: prefs.tripShareMode == TripShareMode.auto,`
safety_controller.dart:105-107: `return preferences.tripShareMode == TripShareMode.auto ? L10n.current.safetyShareEveryRide : ...`
(grep: TripShareMode.auto is not used anywhere else)
suggested_fix: When a ride reaches in-trip (or accepted) with tripShareEnabled and mode auto, call SafetyController.startShare once per ride. Otherwise document it as server-side and make the mock do it.

title: A trip share is never stopped: no caller of stopShare, so the live link stays active after the trip ends
description: `SafetyController.stopShare` / `TripShareRepository.stop` / `SafetyStore.stopShare` exist but nothing calls them. The ride-end paths (markCompleted, markExternalTerminal, _commitCancelled, closeCompletedRide) only stop the audio recording (`_stopSafetyRecording`). The share created from the Safety Kit stays `isActive: true` locally and on the server until its 6-hour expiry (safety_store.dart:267, safety_mock_api.dart:270). The rider also has no control anywhere to stop sharing. The Trip share copy promises 'Share your active ride'.
failure_scenario: The rider shares the trip from the Safety Kit, then the trip completes at their home address. For up to six hours afterwards the contacts' live link still reports an active share for that ride, with its final location, and the rider cannot turn it off.
evidence:
safety_controller.dart:309-312: `Future<void> stopShare(String rideId) async { await _session.stopShare(rideId); ... }` (no callers)
active_ride_controller.dart:467-469: `void _stopSafetyRecording() { unawaited(SafetyController.stopRecordingForRideEnd()); }` (only the audio is stopped)
safety_store.dart:267: `expiresAt: now.add(const Duration(hours: 6)),`
suggested_fix: Stop the ride's share (best effort) wherever the ride ends (markCompleted / markExternalTerminal / cancel commit), and offer a Stop sharing action in the kit.

title: Sign-out wipe leaves the rider's safety audio files on disk (Documents/safety_recordings) and drops their only index
description: UserDataWipe promises 'Removes everything a rider left on this device'. Safety recordings are written by NativeSafetyRecorder to `<ApplicationDocuments>/safety_recordings/<id>.m4a` (safety_recorder_native.dart:26-33). Their metadata lives in `movera_safety_cache_v1.recordings`. The wipe removes that prefs key and resets SafetyController, but never deletes the files. Nothing else in the app deletes them either: `SafetyAudioService.delete` has no caller and no screen lists recordings. Every Ride check and Safety Kit recording therefore stays on the phone after sign-out, now unreferenced, and is available to whoever signs in next on the app's storage. On iOS the Documents directory is also included in device backups, contrary to 'saved only on this phone'.
failure_scenario: Rider A records a 4-minute Ride check audio during an incident and later signs out. Rider B signs in on the same phone. A's m4a files are still in the app's Documents/safety_recordings and no app flow will ever remove them.
evidence:
user_data_wipe.dart:19: `/// Removes everything a rider left on this device (FLOW-1, ARCH-15).`
user_data_wipe.dart:135: `SafetyController.resetShared();` (no recording file cleanup)
safety_recorder_native.dart:26-32: `final directory = Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/safety_recordings'); ... path: '${directory.path}/$recordingId.m4a',`
suggested_fix: In UserDataWipe.run, delete the safety_recordings directory (and the files of any cached recordings). Consider storing recordings in a non-backed-up location (Application Support with excludeFromBackup).

title: The card and Kit keep showing 'Recording m:ss' after the OS has interrupted capture (112 call or app in background); the app has no background audio mode
description: `isRecording` only reflects the service's own `_active` field. Nothing listens to the recorder's state or interruptions. The app declares no background audio (Info.plist UIBackgroundModes has only remote-notification, and the Android manifest has no microphone foreground service). So when the rider follows the journey and taps Call 112, the dialer takes the foreground and the call takes the microphone: iOS interrupts and suspends the recording, and Android 9+ records silence for a backgrounded app. Back in the app, the card's ticker still counts 'Recording 3:12 · Tap to stop' as if everything since the call had been captured.
failure_scenario: The rider starts a Ride check recording, then taps Call 112 and talks to the operator for 3 minutes. Returning to the app, the card shows 'Recording 3:40'. The saved file has no audio after the dialer opened, which the rider learns only if they ever find the file.
evidence:
safety_audio_service.dart:30: `bool get isRecording => _active?.isRecording == true;`
ride_check_card.dart:999-1006: `final recording = widget.controller.recording; ... final elapsed = ... DateTime.now().toUtc().difference(since.toUtc());`
ios/Runner/Info.plist:48-51: `<key>UIBackgroundModes</key><array><string>remote-notification</string></array>`
suggested_fix: Subscribe to the recorder's state/interruption stream and update the card (stop, or show 'paused by call'). Declare background audio (iOS) or a microphone foreground service (Android) if recording must survive a call or a locked screen.

title: A failed stop (no audio or save failed) leaves an orphan recording entry and audio file that nothing ever cleans up
description: `start()` registers the recording in the cache (`initDeviceAudio` / `initAudio`) before capture. In `stop()`, when the recorder returns null (missing or 0-byte file) the service throws NO_AUDIO without deleting that cache entry. The native recorder also leaves the 0-byte file on disk, because it only checks the file and returns null (safety_recorder_native.dart:39-41). When completeDeviceAudio/completeAudio throws, SAVE_FAILED leaves the captured m4a on disk with no localPath recorded anywhere. A recording interrupted by an app kill likewise stays as an entry with endedAt == null (isRecording == true) forever. These entries and files accumulate in `movera_safety_cache_v1` and Documents.
failure_scenario: The rider taps Record and then Stop within a fraction of a second, so the encoder writes 0 bytes. The card says 'No audio file was captured.' The cache keeps a recording with no file and an endedAt timestamp, and the empty .m4a stays in safety_recordings. Repeating this grows both.
evidence:
safety_audio_service.dart:87-91: `final path = await _recorder.stop(); _active = null; if (path == null) { throw SafetyAudioException('NO_AUDIO', L10n.current.audioNoFile); }`
safety_audio_service.dart:102-104: `} catch (_) { throw SafetyAudioException('SAVE_FAILED', L10n.current.audioSaveFailed); }`
safety_recorder_native.dart:39-41: `if (path == null || !await File(path).exists() || await File(path).length() == 0) { return null; }`
suggested_fix: On NO_AUDIO, delete the store entry and the empty file. On SAVE_FAILED, keep the localPath in memory and retry, or delete the file.

title: Safety Kit recording cannot start offline (server init is required) and a successful init leaves a duplicate optimistic entry stuck as 'recording'
description: The Kit records with `deviceOnly: false`, so `start()` awaits `_store.initAudio`, a `_write` that must reach POST /safety-audio/init. Offline, the remote fails, `_write` reverts and rethrows, and the Kit shows 'recording failed': a rider in a dead zone cannot record from the Safety Kit at all, although the file is saved locally. When init succeeds, the server returns its own id (`aud_$requestId` in the mock), not the optimistic id. `apply(confirmed)` only removes entries with the confirmed id, so the optimistic entry with the local id stays in the cache forever with endedAt == null.
failure_scenario: Offline in a tunnel, the rider opens the Safety Kit and taps Record audio. The note says recording failed and the microphone never starts. Online, every Kit recording adds two cache entries, one of which is never completed.
evidence:
safety_store.dart:494-507: `final rec = AudioRecording(id: 'aud_${newRequestId()}', ...); return _write(() => _remote.initAudio(rideId: rideId), rec, (value) { _cache.recordings = [..._cache.recordings.where((r) => r.id != value.id), value]; },);`
safety_mock_api.dart:363: `'id': 'aud_$requestId',`
suggested_fix: Start capture locally first and register with the server best effort (queue the init when offline). In apply, replace the optimistic entry by its local id.

title: A card the rider closed comes back after a quick reload when its close was queued behind a slow alert send
description: `_close` clears `_session` immediately, but the local save that marks the event resolved happens inside the queued 'close' job. Jobs run one after another (`_enqueue`). If an earlier alert job is still waiting on the API (up to the 15 s ApiClient timeout when offline), the close job and its local `keep(status: resolved)` have not run yet. If the page reloads or the app is killed in that window, the event is still pending/acknowledged on disk, so `unanswered()` returns it and the non-dismissible card reopens. The rider's final answer (for example 'I'm OK' or the note) was never saved.
failure_scenario: Offline: the rider taps a red row (the alert POST hangs), then taps Done within a few seconds and the card folds away. The browser reloads before the 15 s timeout. The card is back on the trip screen, blocking it, and the Done/note answer is lost.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:681-693: `void _close(RideCheckSession closing) { _session = null; ... _changed(); ... _enqueue('close', () async { await _service.submitAnswers(...` 
ride_check_controller.dart:731-732: `final previous = _queue; _queue = previous == null ? run() : previous.then((_) => run());`
suggested_fix: Save the closing answers and resolved status to the local cache synchronously in `_close`, before enqueueing the network part.

title: Ride check distances use '.' as decimal separator in Swedish/French ('1.2 km')
description: `formatRideCheckDistance` builds the bold part of the card's reason line with `toStringAsFixed`, which always uses '.'. RideCheckPage and the demo page format admin's km the same way (ride_check_page.dart:44-50, ride_check_demo_page.dart:158-159). Swedish and French need ','. This code is separate from lib/shared/formatters/money.dart (the known finding), so fixing that file does not fix these strings.
failure_scenario: Swedish UI: the dropped-far card reads 'Resan slutade 3.6 km från …' and the RideCheck page shows 'mer än 2.5 km' instead of '3,6 km' / '2,5 km'.
evidence:
ride_check_trigger.dart:243-244: `final km = meters / 1000; return '${km.toStringAsFixed(km >= 10 ? 0 : 1)} km';`
ride_check_page.dart:44-46: `t.offRouteKm.toStringAsFixed(0) : t.offRouteKm.toStringAsFixed(1);`
suggested_fix: Format with NumberFormat for the current locale (the same helper the money formatter fix will use).

title: Ride check recording keeps the microphone on after session expiry replaces the trip screen with Sign in
description: The only things that stop a Ride check recording are answering the card (`_close`) and the ride-end paths in ActiveRideController. On session expiry, `onSessionExpired` re-roots to Sign in and keeps the ride (di.dart:104-116). Waiting and the card's layer are disposed, but RideCheckController keeps `_session` and the audio service keeps `_active`, so the recorder keeps capturing on the Sign in screen with no Stop control. If a different rider then signs in, `enterSessionAs` wipes and `SafetyController.resetShared()` discards the service, so the recorder can no longer be stopped by any code path.
failure_scenario: During an unanswered card the rider records. The alert POST gets a 401 and the token refresh fails, so the app shows Sign in. The microphone indicator stays on and the recording grows until the process dies, or until the same rider signs back in and returns to the card.
evidence:
di.dart:104-115: `onSessionExpired: () async { ... AppScope.showSignInOnSessionExpired?.call(); }` (no audio stop)
safety_controller.dart:71-77: `static void resetShared() { RideCheckController.resetShared(); _shared?.dispose(); _shared = null; ...` (audio not stopped)
suggested_fix: Call `audio.stopIfRecording` on session expiry and in SafetyController.resetShared before discarding the service.

title: Long stop demo shows an off-route 'trip taking 50% longer' card when admin's longStopMinutes is 15 or more
description: playDemo(longStop) feeds samples into a real monitor for (longStopMinutes + 1) minutes. The monitor checks `_tooLong` (off-route by time) on the same samples, against the demo plan's straight-line expectation. That is 4.69 km / 8.3 m/s ≈ 565 s, with a limit of 1.5 × 565 = 847.5 s, so it fires at the 850 s sample. The long stop fires at longStopMinutes × 60 + 5 s. For longStopMinutes ≥ 15 (905 s > 850 s) the off-route detection wins and the loop stops at the first hit. The 'Long stop' demo then opens an off-route card ('50% longer than expected'). Worked by hand: haversine of (59.3303, 18.0586) to (59.36, 18.0) ≈ 4687 m.
failure_scenario: The admin sets 'Unexpected long stop' to 15 min. The rider taps Safety › RideCheck › Try it › Long stop and the card shows the off-route reason instead of 'Stopped for 15 min'.
evidence:
ride_check_controller.dart:349-354: `final seconds = (settings.longStopMinutes + 1) * 60; for (var s = 0; s <= seconds && hit == null; s += 5) { hit = monitor.addSample(...); }`
ride_check_monitor.dart:131-135: `_crash(speed, gap) ?? _longStop(sample) ?? _offRoute(sample) ?? _tooLong(sample);`
suggested_fix: Use a monitor with only the long-stop trigger enabled for the demo (settings.copyWith(offRouteEnabled: false, possibleCrashEnabled: false)), or a plan whose expected time exceeds the demo length.

title: The server profile is never read, so the first save from an empty cache overwrites the rider's name with '' and resets their consents to the defaults
description: SyncedProfileRepository is described as 'the profile the server knows', but it has no GET. hydrate() only reads the device cache (`await _cache.hydrate(); if (_syncPending) await _sync(...)`). Every save sends the full body built from that cache: name, language and all three consents. Two cases leave the cache empty or at defaults for a rider who already has a server profile: (a) sign-out, where UserDataWipe removes `movera_profile_v1` and clearLocal() resets the cache to RiderProfileData.defaults(); (b) a fresh device or browser. Nothing on the sign-in path fills the cache from the server: enterMoveraApp only shows Home, and RiderNameScreen is shown only for isNewRider. The returning rider's first profile write is any Privacy switch, a language pick or a gender pick. It PATCHes `{name: '', language: ..., consents: {rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: true, promotions: false}}` (the defaults, apart from the one switch they changed). The mock and the proposed contract accept an empty name and merge the consents, so the server-side name (which the driver app shows) is erased. A rider who opted out of e-mail updates on another device is silently opted back in. Account also shows 'Add your name' to a rider who has one.
failure_scenario: A rider whose server profile is {name: 'Anna Berg', emailUpdates: false} signs out and back in (or signs in on a new phone). Account shows 'Add your name'. They pick Svenska under Language, and pickAppLanguage -> ProfileController.update -> PATCH /api/v1/rider/profile {name:'', language:'sv', consents:{rideUpdates:true, emailUpdates:true, promotions:false}}. The server's name is now empty, so the driver sees no rider name, and the e-mail consent is flipped back to true without the rider asking.
evidence:
synced_profile_repository.dart:42-45 `Future<void> hydrate() async { await _cache.hydrate(); if (_syncPending) await _sync(_cache.current); }` (no server read)
synced_profile_repository.dart:60-68 `static Map<String, dynamic> body(RiderProfileData profile) => { 'name': profile.name.trim(), 'language': profile.language, 'consents': { 'rideUpdates': ..., 'emailUpdates': ..., 'promotions': ... } };`
profile.dart:190-199 defaults(): name '', and rideUpdates/emailUpdates default to true
user_data_wipe.dart:127 `scope.profile.clearLocal();` plus removal of the movera_profile_v1 key
language_picker.dart:29 `await owner.update(owner.profile.copyWith(language: next));`
suggested_fix: Fetch the server profile (GET /api/v1/rider/profile) after sign-in or on hydrate, and seed the cache from it before any save. Until it has loaded, either block saves or send only the fields the rider changed.

title: Sign-up name fields allow 40+40 characters, but the server rejects names over 80: a maximal name makes every later profile sync fail silently
description: AuthTextField caps each name field at 40 characters, and RiderNameScreen saves '$first $last'. That can be 81 characters. The Personal info editor (showAccountTextEditor) has no length limit at all. The profile contract and the in-process mock reject `name.trim().length > 80` with 422 invalid_profile. SyncedProfileRepository._sync catches every error the same way: it sets `_syncPending = true` and logs a warning. The UI therefore never says anything. Every later save resends the same over-long name, so every PATCH is rejected, including consent and language changes, and the 'resend' can never succeed.
failure_scenario: A new rider types a 40-character first name and a 40-character last name and taps Let's ride. PATCH {name: <81 chars>} returns 422 and the app enters normally. Later the rider turns off Offers in Privacy. That PATCH also returns 422 because it carries the same name. The server never learns the name or any consent change, and the rider is shown no error.
evidence:
auth_controls.dart:377 `inputFormatters: [LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter(40)],`
rider_name.dart:68 `profile.profile.copyWith(name: last.isEmpty ? first : '$first $last')`
account_widgets.dart:339-345 the editor's TextField has no length formatter
in_process_mock_client.dart:1136-1140 `if (name is! String || name.trim().length > 80 || ...) { status = 422; ...invalid_profile }`
synced_profile_repository.dart:78-80 `} catch (error) { _syncPending = true; AppLog.warning('profile.sync_failed', ...); }`
suggested_fix: Validate the combined name against the server limit (80) in the sign-up and Personal info editors. Treat a 4xx validation answer as a user-facing error instead of as pending.

title: Privacy switches capture a stale profile and only move after the network PATCH returns, so a quick second toggle reverts the first
description: Each switch calls `_profile.update(ride.copyWith(x: on))`, where `ride` was captured in build(). ProfileController.update awaits SyncedProfileRepository.save, which awaits the local write and then the PATCH round trip, and only then calls notifyListeners. Until that answer arrives, the page does not rebuild and the controlled Switch keeps its old position. If the rider taps another switch during the round trip, its closure still holds the old `ride`, so its save carries the first switch's old value and reverts it, both locally and in the PATCH it sends. The call is also unawaited and has no try/catch. A local prefs failure (ProfileRepository.save rethrows) becomes an unhandled async error with no feedback. Personal info was fixed for this (FLOW-15), but Privacy was not.
failure_scenario: On a real backend with about 1 s latency, the rider turns Ride updates off and then turns Email off right away. The second save is built from the pre-toggle profile (rideUpdates: true), and the final cached and server state is rideUpdates: true, emailUpdates: false. When the page rebuilds, the Ride updates switch shows on again, and the rider's opt-out is lost.
evidence:
privacy.dart:41 `final ride = _profile.profile;`
privacy.dart:97-98 `onChanged: (on) => _profile.update(ride.copyWith(rideUpdates: on)),` (same pattern at 115 and 134)
profile_controller.dart:30-33 `Future<void> update(RiderProfileData next) async { await _store.save(next); notifyListeners(); }`
synced_profile_repository.dart:54-57 `final saved = await _cache.save(next); await _sync(saved); return saved;`
suggested_fix: Build each update from `_profile.profile` at tap time, notify (or update the UI optimistically) before the network sync, and wrap the call in a try/catch that shows saveFailed, as Personal info does.

title: Sign-in Continue/Verify and the Apple/Google buttons expose no tap action to screen readers
description: AuthPrimaryButton and AuthProviderButton wrap their InkWell in `Semantics(button: true, enabled: ..., label: ..., excludeSemantics: true)` and pass no `onTap`. excludeSemantics drops the InkWell's semantics node, which is where the tap action lives. The resulting node is announced as a button but has no SemanticsAction.tap. On Android, TalkBack marks it as not clickable and double-tap does not activate it. Web semantics also gives it no click handler. These buttons are the only way through sign-in (Continue, Verify, Let's ride, Apple, Google).
failure_scenario: A TalkBack user focuses 'Continue' on Sign in after entering a number and double-taps. The node has no tap action, nothing happens and no code is requested, so the rider cannot sign in with a screen reader.
evidence:
auth_controls.dart:26-30 `return Semantics( button: true, enabled: enabled, label: label, excludeSemantics: true, child: ...InkWell(onTap: enabled ? onPressed : null` (no Semantics.onTap)
auth_controls.dart:116-120 the same for AuthProviderButton
suggested_fix: Pass `onTap: enabled ? onPressed : null` to the outer Semantics, or drop excludeSemantics and use MergeSemantics.

title: 'Sign out other devices' reports failure when the sign-out succeeded but the follow-up GET failed
description: signOutOtherDevices() POSTs the sign-out and ignores its response, although the mock returns the new `security` in that response. It then does a separate GET. If the POST succeeds but the GET fails (network drop, timeout), the controller's catch sets 'Could not update active sessions.' and leaves the old state, still listing the other devices and still holding a fresh reauthenticatedAt. The server has already revoked those sessions and cleared reauthenticatedAt. A retry therefore gets 403 reauth_required and shows the same error.
failure_scenario: The rider confirms Sign out other devices. The POST returns 200 and the GET times out. The Security page shows 'Could not update active sessions.' and still lists the iPhone session, although it was revoked. Retrying fails with 403.
evidence:
account_security_repository.dart:14-17 `await _api.post('/api/v1/account/security/sessions/sign-out-others'); return load();`
account_security_controller.dart:63-67 `state = await _repository.signOutOtherDevices(); ... } catch (_) { errorMessage = 'Could not update active sessions.'; }`
in_process_mock_client.dart:572-577 the POST answer already carries 'security'
suggested_fix: Decode the `security` from the POST response. If only the refresh fails, report success and reload in the background.

title: Sign out other devices stays tappable after the 5-minute reauthentication window passes, then silently does nothing
description: hasFreshReauthentication is checked only when the page builds. Nothing rebuilds the page when the 5-minute window ends. The tile keeps its 'server revokes others' copy and its onTap, the rider confirms in the sheet, and then AccountSecurityController.signOutOtherDevices() re-checks hasFreshReauthentication and returns early, with no error, no notify and no request.
failure_scenario: The rider opens Security right after reauthenticating, leaves it open for 6 minutes, taps Sign out other devices and confirms. Nothing happens: no request is sent, no error appears and the other sessions remain.
evidence:
security.dart:214-229 `onTap: caps.signOutOtherDevices && caps.reauthentication && security.hasFreshReauthentication && !_security.loading ? () async { ... await _security.signOutOtherDevices(); } : null`
account_security_controller.dart:53-58 `... || !current.hasFreshReauthentication) { return; }`
account_security.dart:97-102 the 5-minute window against DateTime.now()
suggested_fix: Re-check freshness after the confirm and show reauthBeforeRevoke (or rebuild with a timer when the window ends) instead of returning silently.

title: Notification feed is ordered by arrival, not by send time: a tapped older tray notification is inserted above newer ones
description: ingest() always does `_items.insert(0, ...)`, even though each item carries `at` (the sentAt). Pushes received while the app is in the background are not ingested until the rider taps them from the system tray (PushCoordinator._handleOpened -> ingest(read: true)). By then newer foreground pushes may already be in the feed. The cold-start initial message is also ingested only after start() has subscribed to foreground messages. In both cases an older notification lands at the top.
failure_scenario: Push A ('Your receipt', sent 12:00) arrives while the app is backgrounded and stays in the tray. The rider opens the app from its icon, and foreground push B (12:30) is ingested. Later they tap A in the tray. The Notifications list now shows A 12:00 above B 12:30.
evidence:
notifications_repository.dart:85-99 `final at = (payload.sentAt ?? _now()).toLocal(); _items.insert(0, AppNotification(... at: at, ...));`
push_coordinator.dart:73-74 `Future<void> _handleOpened(PushPayload payload) async { _notifications.ingest(payload, read: true);`
suggested_fix: Insert at the position given by `at` (newest first), not always at index 0.

title: A push with a title but no body shows its raw wire type (e.g. 'ride.driver_assigned') as the subtitle
description: The code skips pushes that have neither a title nor a body. When there is a title but no body, the subtitle falls back to `payload.type`, an internal event code, and the feed row shows it to the rider.
failure_scenario: The server sends a notification with title 'Driver on the way' and no body, with data type 'ride.driver_assigned'. The Notifications row shows 'Driver on the way' over 'ride.driver_assigned'.
evidence: notifications_repository.dart:91 `subtitle: body?.isNotEmpty == true ? body! : payload.type,`
suggested_fix: Use an empty subtitle when there is no body (AccountTile-style rows already hide empty bodies).

title: Tapping a push while Notifications is open from the side menu stacks a second Notifications screen
description: pushPageOnce decides 'already on top' by `settings.name == AppRoutes.notifications`. The side menu pushes NotificationScreen with `RightToLeftTransition(page)` and no RouteSettings, so that route's name is null. A push tap that resolves to the Notifications destination (an info push, or a ride that has ended) then pushes a second NotificationScreen over the first.
failure_scenario: The rider opens Menu > Notifications, pulls down the shade and taps an info push. _openNotificationsFromPush -> pushPageOnce sees top name null != '/notifications' and pushes another Notifications page. Back must be pressed twice.
evidence:
notification_navigation.dart:158 `if (_topRoute(nav)?.settings.name == name) return true;`
side_menu.dart:431 `() => _pushPage(context, const NotificationScreen()),` with side_menu.dart:74 `nav.push<Object?>(RightToLeftTransition(page))` (no settings)
suggested_fix: Push NotificationScreen from the side menu with RouteSettings(name: AppRoutes.notifications), or detect the screen by type.

title: Login activity shows a dangling separator when a session has no place ('This session  ·  ', '  ·  Movera')
description: _LoginTile always interpolates session.place, which defaults to '' when the server omits it. The demo mock's only session has place ''. The current session therefore renders 'This session  ·  ', and another session renders '  ·  Movera'.
failure_scenario: In the demo build, Account > Security > Login activity shows 'This device' over 'This session  ·  ' with an empty place after the separator.
evidence:
security.dart:260-262 `body: session.current ? context.l10n.thisSession(session.place) : '${session.place}  ·  ${session.source}',`
app_en.arb:1182 `"thisSession": "This session  ·  {place}"`
in_process_mock_client.dart:158 `'place': '',`
suggested_fix: Leave out the separator and the place when the place is empty.

title: Password 'Last changed' date is formatted from a UTC DateTime, so it shows the UTC day
description: AccountSecurityState.fromJson converts every timestamp with `.toUtc()`, and _passwordLine passes it straight to DateFormat, which formats the UTC fields. A change made late in the evening (UTC) shows the previous day for Stockholm riders.
failure_scenario: passwordUpdatedAt '2026-03-10T23:30:00Z' (00:30 on 11 March in Stockholm) shows 'Last changed 3/10/2026'.
evidence:
account_security.dart:108-109 `DateTime? parseDate(Object? value) => value is String ? DateTime.tryParse(value)?.toUtc() : null;`
security.dart:46 `return context.l10n.lastChanged(L10n.formatDate(when, 'yMd'));`
suggested_fix: Format `when.toLocal()`, or the zone wall time.

title: After a sign-out wipe the profile language resets to 'en' while the device language choice is kept, so the next profile PATCH reports English
description: language_picker says 'the profile keeps the same code for the server'. UserDataWipe keeps `movera_app_language` (a device key), so AppLanguageController still speaks the rider's chosen language. It resets the profile to defaults(), whose language is 'en'. The next profile save (for example the new-rider name step) sends language 'en' although the rider explicitly chose Swedish on this device and is using the app in Swedish.
failure_scenario: The rider picked Svenska in Account and signs out. A new rider signs in on the same device, the UI is still Swedish, and they enter their name. PATCH {language: 'en'}, so the backend and driver treat the rider as English-speaking.
evidence:
app_language_controller.dart:65-73 choose() saves to the device store only; language_picker.dart:29 the profile is updated only inside the picker
user_data_wipe.dart:67-71 'movera_app_language' is kept; :127 `scope.profile.clearLocal();`
profile.dart:196 `language: defaultLanguage,` ('en')
suggested_fix: When the profile is hydrated or reset, seed profile.language from AppLanguageController.choice when there is one.

title: If the local wipe throws after the backend has accepted the deletion, the page says the request could not be sent
description: requestDeletion() awaits the POST and then signOutLocally(). signOutLocally clears the tokens and runs UserDataWipe.run() in a finally block, and RideSnapshotStore.clear() inside run() is not guarded. Any throw there propagates to DeleteAccountPage's catch, which shows deleteSendFailed although the server already scheduled the deletion and the tokens may be gone. A retry then POSTs without a session.
failure_scenario: The deletion POST returns 202 and clearing the token store or prefs throws. The rider sees 'could not send the request' and stays on a signed-out Delete page. Tapping again gets 401 and the session-expired redirect.
evidence:
account_deletion_controller.dart:19-22 `await _repository.requestDeletion(); await _auth.signOutLocally();`
delete_account.dart:64-81 `try { await _controller.requestDeletion(); ... } catch (error) { ... _error = context.l10n.deleteSendFailed; }`
ride_snapshot_store.dart:517-518 the unguarded prefs remove in clear()
suggested_fix: Treat the deletion as sent once the POST succeeds. Run the local wipe best-effort, log any failure, and show the sent view.

title: Positional legacy ids collide after a delete, so deleting one custom place removes two and editing one overwrites another
description: `_withIds` gives every custom place that has no stored id the id `place_legacy_$i`, where i is its current position in the list. Home's own add path (`HomePlacesController.applyResolved` case 'custom') appends `SavedPlaceData(title: type, type: type, address: address)` with no id, so places added from Home never have one. Once Saved Places writes the list, those positional ids are stored permanently (save and remove both persist the output of `_withIds`). After a delete shrinks the list, a place Home adds later lands at an index whose `place_legacy_<i>` id is already stored on another place. `remove` filters with `item['id'] != id`, so it drops every place with that id. `save` uses `indexWhere`, so it replaces the first place with that id instead of the one being edited.
failure_scenario: On Home, add a 'gym' place (A) and then a 'restaurant' place (B); neither gets an id. In Saved Places, delete A: B is stored as place_legacy_1. On Home, add a 'school' place (C): the list is now [B(place_legacy_1), C(no id, index 1)], so C also reads as place_legacy_1. Delete C in Saved Places and B disappears as well. Edit C instead and B's entry is overwritten with C's data while C's old entry stays.
suggested_fix: Assign a fresh unique id (`place_${newRequestId()}`) to id-less entries and persist it, rather than a position-derived id. Also give places added from Home an id.

title: Pressing Enter picks the first result of an older query still on screen and goes straight to booking
description: `_onTyped` leaves `_results` in place while a new query is in flight; it only clears them when the field is empty. `onSubmitted` then chooses `_results.first`, which can belong to an earlier, shorter query. `_choose` on the destination field calls `_finish` immediately, so the rider moves on to Select ride with a destination they did not type. `_results.first` can also be a row that `_whileTyping` hides behind a recent match, so Enter may pick a different place from the first row the rider sees.
failure_scenario: The rider types 'Kungsgatan' and suggestions arrive, then keeps typing ' 44' and presses Enter before the request for 'Kungsgatan 44' returns. `_results.first` is still the 'Kungsgatan' list's first entry (for example 'Kungsgatan 1'), and it is booked as the destination.
suggested_fix: Store the query that `_results` belongs to and only accept Enter when it equals the current text, or clear `_results` when the text changes. Pick the first row actually displayed.

title: Back during the finish step does not cancel it: a date picker or route-change price sheet appears after the picker has closed
description: While `_finishing` is true, the picker shows a full-screen overlay but has no PopScope, so system back, iOS swipe-back or browser back still pops it. `widget.onFinish` keeps running. In Home's `_confirmRouteSelection`, the `mounted` checks are Home's (Home stays mounted), so for Book for later `ScheduleDateTimeSelector.choose` opens over Home after the rider left Where to, and the chosen time is then dropped because `_finish` returns when `!mounted`. In `openRouteChange`, `RouteChangeSheet.confirm(context, ...)` uses the ride screen's context, so the price sheet still opens. If the rider confirms, `changes.apply` changes the live route and credits the wallet. But the route already completed with null, so `openRouteChange` returns null and `lastRefundDestination` is never set.
evidence:
route_picker_page.dart:390-417 (_finish awaits widget.onFinish, then `if (!mounted || draft == null) return;`)
